title: Compliance with WoAG Protective Security Directions
obligationDescription: The Accountable Authority complies with all Protective Security Directions.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority complies with all Protective Security Directions issued under the Protective Security Policy Framework.
obligationRef: PSPF - 2
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA Accountable Authority complies with all whole-of-government Protective Security Directions to maintain WoAG security standards.
threat: Non-compliance with PSPF Directions; regulatory breach; reputational and legal risk to the NDIA
applicability: All NDIA personnel; Accountable Authority (CEO)
excluded: None
guidance: Review all PSPF Directions upon publication and incorporate into the NDIA security governance framework. Report compliance status in the annual protective security report.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Monitor PSPF Directions published by Department of Home Affairs. 2. Brief Accountable Authority on new Directions. 3. Update NDIA security policies to reflect Directions. 4. Report compliance in annual report.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
consulted: General Counsel; Group Manager, Technology; NDIA Security Team
informed: All NDIA Branch Managers; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement. Refer to PSPF Req 52–53 for contingency provisions only.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority (subject to PSPF contingency provisions)
verification: Annual protective security report review; independent IRAP assessment; internal audit
evidence: Signed Accountable Authority acknowledgement of PSPF Directions; annual protective security report
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy
relatedProcedures: PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance (Dept of Home Affairs); NDIA Security Governance Framework
reviewTriggers: PSPF update or new Direction issued; machinery-of-government change; Accountable Authority change
notes: Directions are issued by the Secretary, Department of Home Affairs under the PGPA Act. All non-corporate Commonwealth entities are subject to this requirement.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Accountable Authority Ministerial Accountability for Protective Security
obligationDescription: The Accountable Authority is answerable to their minister for the entity's protective security.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority is answerable to the responsible Minister for the entity's protective security posture and performance.
obligationRef: PSPF - 6
controlObjective: Establish clear lines of ministerial accountability for the NDIA's protective security, ensuring executive responsibility is transparent and enforced.
threat: Unclear accountability for security failures; breakdown in governance and ministerial oversight
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); NDIA Executive Leadership Team
excluded: None
guidance: Establish formal reporting lines from Accountable Authority to Minister covering protective security matters. Include security performance in ministerial briefings and reporting cycles.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Document accountability arrangements in security governance framework. 2. Brief Minister on significant security events as required. 3. Include protective security in annual ministerial reporting. 4. Maintain records of ministerial briefings.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO)
consulted: General Counsel; Ministerial Liaison Office
informed: NDIA Board; NDIA Executive; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Annual protective security report; ministerial briefing records; governance framework review
evidence: Annual protective security report submitted to Minister; record of ministerial briefings on security matters
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
relatedProcedures: PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance; NDIA Ministerial Communications Protocol
reviewTriggers: Ministerial change; significant security incident; PSPF update; machinery-of-government change
notes: Ministerial accountability is a core PSPF governance obligation for all non-corporate Commonwealth entities.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Accountable Authority Responsibility for Security Risk Management
obligationDescription: The Accountable Authority is responsible for managing the security risks of their entity.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority is responsible for managing the security risks of the entity.
obligationRef: PSPF - 7
controlObjective: Ensure ultimate responsibility for NDIA security risk management rests with the Accountable Authority, creating accountability at the highest level.
threat: Unmanaged security risks; failure to identify and treat entity-level threats; inadequate risk governance
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA operations and systems
excluded: None
guidance: The Accountable Authority must formally own the NDIA's security risk register, approve the risk tolerance, and receive regular risk reporting. Risk management must be embedded in corporate governance processes.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Maintain enterprise security risk register. 2. Report risk status to Accountable Authority at least quarterly. 3. Obtain formal AA approval for risk tolerance and treatment decisions. 4. Include risk status in annual report.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Chief Risk Officer
consulted: General Counsel; Audit Committee; NDIA Board
informed: NDIA Executive Leadership Team; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Security risk register review; Audit Committee minutes; annual protective security report
evidence: Enterprise security risk register signed by AA; Audit Committee risk reporting records; annual report
auditFrequency: Annual (risk register reviewed quarterly)
relatedPolicies: NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy
relatedProcedures: NDIA Enterprise Risk Management Framework; ASD Risk Management Guidelines
reviewTriggers: Significant new threat or vulnerability; material change to NDIA operating environment; PSPF update; security incident
notes: This requirement underpins the entire NDIA security governance structure. Risk management must be integrated into the NDIA's corporate risk framework.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Appointment of Chief Security Officer
obligationDescription: A Chief Security Officer is appointed and empowered to oversee the entity's protective security arrangements.
requirement: The NDIA shall appoint and empower a Chief Security Officer to oversee the entity's protective security arrangements.
obligationRef: PSPF - 8
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2
controlObjective: Ensure a suitably qualified and empowered security executive is responsible for all protective security arrangements across the NDIA.
threat: Absence of dedicated security leadership; uncoordinated protective security arrangements; gaps in security governance
applicability: All NDIA operations; Accountable Authority
excluded: None
guidance: Formally appoint a CSO with a documented mandate, appropriate delegation, and direct access to the Accountable Authority. CSO must have authority to direct security activities across all NDIA business lines.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Establish CSO position and position description. 2. Issue formal instrument of appointment. 3. Document delegations and authorities. 4. Ensure CSO has direct reporting line to Accountable Authority.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO)
consulted: General Counsel; People and Culture; NDIA Security Team
informed: All NDIA Branch Managers; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Position description review; instrument of appointment; organisational chart verification
evidence: Signed instrument of CSO appointment; current CSO position description; security governance framework document
auditFrequency: Annual; on appointment or role change
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
relatedProcedures: PSPF Security Governance Guidance; NDIA Delegations Framework
reviewTriggers: CSO departure or appointment; restructure; PSPF update; significant change to security environment
notes: The CSO must be empowered with sufficient authority and resources to fulfil their mandate. The PSPF requires the CSO to be a separate role from the CISO.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: CSO Seniority and Minimum Security Clearance
obligationDescription: The Chief Security Officer is a Senior Executive Service officer and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Security Officer is a Senior Executive Service officer and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
obligationRef: PSPF - 9
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3, A.7.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PS-3
controlObjective: Ensure the CSO has the requisite seniority, authority and trustworthiness to perform the role and access sensitive protective security information.
threat: CSO lacking authority or clearance to access classified information; compromised security governance at executive level
applicability: Chief Security Officer (CSO)
excluded: None
guidance: Verify CSO position is classified at SES Band 1 or above. Initiate and maintain a minimum NV1 security clearance through AGSVA. Monitor clearance status and initiate renewal prior to expiry.
technicalControls: AGSVA clearance management system integration
processSteps: 1. Confirm CSO position is at SES level. 2. Submit clearance request to AGSVA if NV1 not held. 3. Monitor clearance expiry dates. 4. Record clearance status in personnel security register.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); People and Culture; NDIA Security Vetting Team
consulted: AGSVA; General Counsel
informed: NDIA Executive; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement. Temporary arrangements only permissible under PSPF Req 52–53.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Personnel security register review; AGSVA clearance verification; position description review
evidence: AGSVA clearance certificate for CSO; SES classification evidence; personnel security register entry
auditFrequency: Annual; on role appointment
relatedPolicies: NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Personnel Security Framework
relatedProcedures: PSPF Personnel Security Guidance; AGSVA Clearance Management Guidelines
reviewTriggers: CSO appointment or change; clearance approaching expiry; adverse clearance finding; PSPF update
owner: Chief Security Officer (CSO); People and Culture
notes: AGSVA manages all Australian Government security clearances. NV1 is the minimum required; some roles may require NV2. Clearance status must be monitored continuously.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: CSO Accountability to Accountable Authority
obligationDescription: The Chief Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for protective security matters.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for all protective security matters.
obligationRef: PSPF - 10
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2
controlObjective: Establish a clear and direct accountability relationship between the CSO and Accountable Authority to ensure security matters receive appropriate executive attention.
threat: Protective security outcomes not escalated appropriately; lack of executive-level accountability for security failures
applicability: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Accountable Authority (CEO)
excluded: None
guidance: Formalise the CSO's accountability through documented reporting lines and governance structures. CSO must have regular direct access to the Accountable Authority to report on security matters.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Document CSO reporting line to Accountable Authority in governance framework. 2. Schedule regular security briefings (at minimum quarterly). 3. CSO to present at Audit Committee meetings. 4. Record meetings and outcomes.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO)
consulted: General Counsel; Audit Committee Chair
informed: NDIA Board; NDIA Executive Leadership Team
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Governance framework review; Audit Committee minutes; CSO reporting schedule
evidence: Security governance framework documenting CSO accountability; Audit Committee minutes; executive briefing records
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
relatedProcedures: NDIA Security Governance Framework; NDIA Audit Committee Charter
reviewTriggers: Organisational restructure; CSO change; PSPF update; Accountable Authority change
notes: The CSO must have sufficient authority and direct access to the AA to escalate critical security matters without delay.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Appointment of Chief Information Security Officer
obligationDescription: A Chief Information Security Officer is appointed to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security for the entity's most critical technology resources.
requirement: The NDIA shall appoint a Chief Information Security Officer to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security of its most critical technology resources.
obligationRef: PSPF - 11
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2, SA-3
controlObjective: Ensure a dedicated executive is responsible for the NDIA's cyber security program, providing leadership and oversight of cyber security across all critical technology assets.
threat: Absence of cyber security leadership; unmanaged cyber risk; inadequate oversight of critical ICT systems
applicability: All NDIA technology systems and data; Accountable Authority
excluded: None
guidance: Formally appoint a CISO with a documented mandate covering the cyber security program and critical technology resources. The CISO role should be separate from the CSO. Ensure the CISO has authority to direct cyber security activities across all technology systems.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Establish CISO position and position description. 2. Issue formal instrument of appointment. 3. Define CISO mandate covering cyber security program scope. 4. Document reporting lines and delegations.
responsible: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
consulted: Chief Security Officer (CSO); General Counsel; Group Manager, Technology
informed: All NDIA Branch Managers; Australian Signals Directorate
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement (Modified effective 01/07/2025).
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Position description review; instrument of appointment; cyber security program documentation review
evidence: Signed CISO appointment instrument; CISO position description; cyber security program charter
auditFrequency: Annual; on appointment or role change
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA ICT Strategic Plan; NDIA Information Security Policy
relatedProcedures: ASD CISO Responsibilities Guide; NDIA Cyber Security Program Charter; NDIA Delegations Framework
reviewTriggers: CISO departure or appointment; significant change to cyber threat environment; PSPF update; new critical systems
notes: PSPF Req 11 was Modified effective 01/07/2025. The CISO mandate must explicitly cover the most critical technology resources as identified in the NDIA Technology Asset Register.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: CISO Capability, Experience and Minimum Security Clearance
obligationDescription: The Chief Information Security Officer has the appropriate capability and experience and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Information Security Officer has appropriate capability and experience and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
obligationRef: PSPF - 12
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3, A.7.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PS-3, AT-3
controlObjective: Ensure the CISO has the requisite technical knowledge, leadership capability and trustworthiness to manage the NDIA's cyber security program effectively.
threat: CISO lacking capability or clearance to access sensitive cyber security information; ineffective cyber security program management
applicability: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
excluded: None
guidance: Assess CISO candidate capability against established competency framework. Initiate and maintain NV1 clearance through AGSVA. Document capability evidence and clearance status in personnel security register.
technicalControls: AGSVA clearance management system integration
processSteps: 1. Define CISO capability requirements in position description. 2. Verify capability evidence (qualifications, experience) at appointment. 3. Submit clearance request to AGSVA. 4. Monitor clearance and capability currency annually.
responsible: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); People and Culture; NDIA Security Vetting Team
consulted: AGSVA; Chief Security Officer (CSO)
informed: NDIA Executive; Australian Signals Directorate
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Personnel security register review; AGSVA clearance verification; capability assessment documentation
evidence: CISO capability evidence (CV, qualifications); AGSVA clearance certificate; personnel security register entry
auditFrequency: Annual; on appointment
relatedPolicies: NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Personnel Security Framework; NDIA Cyber Security Policy
relatedProcedures: PSPF Personnel Security Guidance; AGSVA Clearance Management Guidelines; ASD CISO Responsibilities Guide
reviewTriggers: CISO appointment or change; clearance approaching expiry; significant change in required capabilities; PSPF update
owner: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); People and Culture
notes: Capability requirements should reference ASD's CISO Responsibilities guide and relevant SFIA competency frameworks. Clearance must be maintained continuously.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: CISO Accountability for Cyber Security Risks
obligationDescription: The Chief Information Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for cyber security risks and how the entity's cyber security program is managing these risks.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Information Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for cyber security risks and how the cyber security program is managing those risks.
obligationRef: PSPF - 13
controlObjective: Ensure cyber security risk accountability is maintained at the Accountable Authority level, with the CISO providing regular and transparent reporting on risk posture and program effectiveness.
threat: Cyber security risks not escalated to the Accountable Authority; inadequate executive oversight of cyber risk; governance failures
applicability: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Accountable Authority (CEO)
excluded: None
guidance: Formalise CISO accountability to the Accountable Authority through documented reporting structures. CISO must provide regular cyber security risk briefings to the AA and Audit Committee, with reporting on cyber security program performance.
technicalControls: Cyber security risk management platform; security metrics and dashboards
processSteps: 1. Document CISO reporting line to Accountable Authority. 2. Schedule regular cyber security risk briefings. 3. CISO reports on risk posture at each Audit Committee meeting. 4. Maintain records of all risk briefings and decisions.
responsible: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
consulted: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Audit Committee; Chief Risk Officer
informed: NDIA Board; NDIA Executive; Australian Signals Directorate
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement (Modified effective 01/07/2025).
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Audit Committee minutes; CISO risk reporting records; cyber security program status reports
evidence: Cyber security risk register; CISO briefing records to AA; Audit Committee minutes; cyber security program status reports
auditFrequency: Annual; cyber risk reporting reviewed at each Audit Committee meeting
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy
relatedProcedures: ASD CISO Responsibilities Guide; NDIA Audit Committee Charter; NDIA Cyber Security Program Charter
reviewTriggers: Significant cyber incident; material change to NDIA's risk profile; CISO change; PSPF update; new critical systems
notes: PSPF Req 13 was Modified effective 01/07/2025. PSPF now requires CISO to report to the Audit Committee at each meeting (see GOV requirement for Req 213 in scope). Linked to cyber security strategy reporting obligations.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Security Practitioner Capability, Empowerment and Resourcing
obligationDescription: Where appointed, security practitioners are appropriately skilled, empowered and resourced to perform their designated functions.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that, where appointed, security practitioners are appropriately skilled, empowered and resourced to perform their designated security functions.
obligationRef: PSPF - 14
controlObjective: Ensure security practitioners across the NDIA have the skills, authority and resources necessary to perform their security functions effectively.
threat: Security practitioners unable to perform duties effectively; skill gaps leading to inadequate security controls; under-resourced security functions
applicability: All designated security practitioners across the NDIA
excluded: Personnel not in designated security practitioner roles
guidance: Establish competency frameworks for all security practitioner roles. Assess capability on appointment and annually. Provide adequate budget, staffing and tooling. Document delegations and authorities for each practitioner role.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control); security tooling and platforms as required by role
processSteps: 1. Define security practitioner roles and competency requirements. 2. Conduct capability assessments at appointment and annually. 3. Identify resourcing needs and include in budget cycle. 4. Review empowerment through delegation framework.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); People and Culture
consulted: Group Manager, Technology; Business Area Managers
informed: All NDIA staff; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Competency assessment records; resourcing review documentation; delegation framework review
evidence: Security practitioner competency assessments; resourcing plans; delegation instruments; training records
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Workforce Plan; NDIA Cyber Security Policy
relatedProcedures: PSPF Workforce Management Guidance; NDIA Capability Development Framework
reviewTriggers: New security practitioner appointment; significant change to threat environment; budget cycle; PSPF update
notes: Applies to all designated security practitioners including the AGSVA vetting unit, security advisors, system administrators with security functions and cyber security team members.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Security Practitioner Access to Government Training
obligationDescription: Where appointed, security practitioners have access to training across government to maintain and upskill on new and emerging security issues.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that, where appointed, security practitioners have access to government security training to maintain and upskill on new and emerging security issues.
obligationRef: PSPF - 15
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 7.2, A.6.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AT-3
controlObjective: Ensure NDIA security practitioners maintain current knowledge of evolving security threats, technologies and practices through access to government training programs.
threat: Outdated security knowledge; inability to respond effectively to new and emerging threats; skill degradation
applicability: All designated security practitioners across the NDIA
excluded: Personnel not in designated security practitioner roles
guidance: Identify relevant government-provided training for each security practitioner role (including ASD, AGSVA, and AGD training programs). Include training completion in performance planning. Maintain training records.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control); learning management system for training records
processSteps: 1. Map available government training programs to security practitioner roles. 2. Enrol practitioners in relevant programs. 3. Track completion via learning management system. 4. Review training currency annually.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); People and Culture
consulted: ASD; AGSVA; Department of Home Affairs
informed: All NDIA security practitioners; NDIA HR team
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Security Officer (CSO)
verification: Training completion records in learning management system; annual capability review
evidence: Training completion records; training plan by practitioner role; learning management system reports
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Learning and Development Policy; NDIA Cyber Security Policy
relatedProcedures: ASD Cyber Security Training Catalogue; AGSVA Training Programs; PSPF Workforce Management Guidance
reviewTriggers: New government training programs available; new or emerging security threats; PSPF update; practitioner role changes
notes: Government training includes ASD's Cyber Security Partnership Program, AGSVA training, and cross-agency security forums. CISO and CSO should attend PSPF and ISM update briefings.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Accountable Authority Approval of Security Governance Arrangements
obligationDescription: The Accountable Authority approves security governance arrangements that are tailored to the entity's size, complexity and risk environment.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority approves security governance arrangements tailored to the entity's size, complexity and risk environment.
obligationRef: PSPF - 16
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA's security governance arrangements are formally approved by the Accountable Authority and are proportionate to the NDIA's size, risk profile and operational complexity.
threat: Security governance not fit-for-purpose; inadequate or disproportionate controls for NDIA's risk environment
applicability: All NDIA security governance structures and committees; Accountable Authority
excluded: None
guidance: Document security governance arrangements (committees, reporting lines, roles, responsibilities) in the NDIA Security Governance Framework. Submit for formal Accountable Authority approval. Review and reapprove when the NDIA's risk environment changes significantly.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Document current security governance arrangements. 2. Review appropriateness against NDIA size and risk profile. 3. Submit governance framework for AA approval. 4. Record approval and re-submit at review cycle.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
consulted: Audit Committee; General Counsel; Group Manager, Technology
informed: NDIA Executive Leadership Team; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Security governance framework review; AA sign-off records; Audit Committee review
evidence: Signed NDIA Security Governance Framework (AA-approved); governance committee charters; approval records
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework; NDIA Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: PSPF Security Governance Guidance; NDIA Security Governance Framework
reviewTriggers: Significant organisational change; material change to NDIA risk environment; PSPF update; Accountable Authority change
notes: Governance arrangements must be reviewed whenever the NDIA undergoes significant organisational change or when its risk environment changes materially.

section: Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
title: Dedicated Security Communication Channel (Security Email Address)
obligationDescription: A dedicated security email address is established and monitored as the central conduit for distribution of protective security-related information across the entity.
requirement: The NDIA shall establish and maintain a dedicated security email address as the central conduit for distributing protective security-related information across the entity.
obligationRef: PSPF - 17
controlObjective: Ensure a monitored, centralised communication channel exists for distributing protective security information to all relevant NDIA personnel promptly and reliably.
threat: Delayed or missed distribution of security information; communication gaps during security incidents; personnel unaware of security advisories
applicability: All NDIA personnel; NDIA Security Team
excluded: None
guidance: Create and maintain a dedicated security email address (e.g., security@ndia.gov.au). Ensure the mailbox is monitored during business hours and that a process exists for urgent after-hours matters. Distribute all PSPF-related communications, security advisories and incident notifications through this channel.
technicalControls: Email system configuration; access controls and monitoring for security mailbox; distribution list management
processSteps: 1. Provision dedicated security mailbox in NDIA email system. 2. Assign monitoring responsibilities to security team. 3. Establish distribution lists for different security communication types. 4. Test mailbox operability regularly.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); NDIA IT Operations; NDIA Security Team
consulted: Group Manager, Technology; Communications Team
informed: All NDIA staff; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Security Officer (CSO)
verification: Mailbox operability testing; monitoring records; communications log review
evidence: Security mailbox configuration evidence; monitoring roster; sample communications distributed through the channel
auditFrequency: Annual; test quarterly
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy; NDIA ICT Acceptable Use Policy
relatedProcedures: NDIA Security Communications Procedure; PSPF Security Governance Guidance
reviewTriggers: Significant security incident; PSPF update; IT system migration; personnel change in monitoring responsibility
notes: The security email address is the primary channel for receiving PSPF security alerts from the Department of Home Affairs. It must be operational at all times and monitored by a designated security team member.

title: Annual Protective Security Report — Minister
obligationDescription: The annual protective security report is provided to the entity's Minister.
requirement: The NDIA shall provide the annual protective security report to the entity's responsible Minister.
obligationRef: PSPF - 31
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-11
controlObjective: Ensure the Minister receives the NDIA's annual protective security report to fulfil accountability obligations and enable ministerial oversight of NDIA's security posture.
threat: Minister uninformed of NDIA's security performance; ministerial accountability gaps; non-compliance with PSPF reporting obligations
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); Ministerial Liaison
excluded: None
guidance: Prepare and submit the annual protective security report to the responsible Minister within the timeframes prescribed by the Department of Home Affairs. The report must address all required PSPF performance domains.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Compile annual protective security report per PSPF guidance. 2. Obtain AA approval (see GOV-016). 3. Submit report to Minister through Ministerial Liaison. 4. Retain submission records.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Ministerial Liaison Office
consulted: General Counsel; Audit Committee
informed: NDIA Board; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Submission records to Minister; annual protective security report; Ministerial Liaison records
evidence: Annual protective security report; evidence of submission to Minister; Ministerial Liaison transmission records
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
relatedProcedures: PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance (Dept of Home Affairs); NDIA Ministerial Communications Protocol
reviewTriggers: Ministerial change; machinery-of-government change; PSPF reporting guidance update
notes: Must be submitted annually. Refer to Department of Home Affairs PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance for required content and submission timeframes. Linked to GOV-015 (Home Affairs) and GOV-016 (AA approval).

title: Annual Protective Security Report — Department of Home Affairs
obligationDescription: The annual protective security report is submitted to the Department of Home Affairs.
requirement: The NDIA shall submit the annual protective security report to the Department of Home Affairs.
obligationRef: PSPF - 32
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-11
controlObjective: Ensure the Department of Home Affairs receives the NDIA's annual protective security report to enable whole-of-government assurance and reporting.
threat: Non-compliance with whole-of-government reporting obligations; incomplete WoAG security reporting data
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); NDIA Security Team
excluded: None
guidance: Submit the annual protective security report to the Department of Home Affairs via the prescribed channel and within the required timeframe. Retain evidence of submission.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Prepare annual protective security report per PSPF guidance. 2. Obtain AA approval (see GOV-016). 3. Submit to Department of Home Affairs via prescribed channel. 4. Retain submission confirmation and records.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); NDIA Security Team
consulted: General Counsel; Audit Committee
informed: Accountable Authority; NDIA Board; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Submission confirmation from Department of Home Affairs; annual protective security report; submission records
evidence: Annual protective security report; Department of Home Affairs submission confirmation; submission records
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
relatedProcedures: PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance (Dept of Home Affairs); Department of Home Affairs reporting portal guidance
reviewTriggers: PSPF reporting guidance update; change to submission portal; Department of Home Affairs request
notes: Submission is made via the Department of Home Affairs' online reporting portal. Retain confirmation of submission. Linked to GOV-014 (Minister) and GOV-016 (AA approval). Ensure report content aligns with all PSPF performance requirements.

title: Accountable Authority Approval and Verification of Annual Security Report
obligationDescription: The Accountable Authority approves the entity's annual protective security report and confirms that they have verified the report's content.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority approves the entity's annual protective security report and confirms that they have verified the report's content.
obligationRef: PSPF - 33
controlObjective: Ensure the Accountable Authority has personally reviewed and approved the annual protective security report, confirming the accuracy and completeness of its content.
threat: Inaccurate or unverified annual security reporting; accountability gaps; misinformation to Minister and Department of Home Affairs
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO)
excluded: None
guidance: The Accountable Authority must personally review the annual protective security report before submission, confirming accuracy of content. Approval must be formally documented (signed). Provide pre-briefing to AA covering report content and any significant security issues.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Prepare draft annual protective security report. 2. Brief Accountable Authority on report content. 3. AA reviews and signs approval. 4. Submit report with AA approval documentation. 5. Retain approval records.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
consulted: General Counsel; Audit Committee
informed: NDIA Board; Department of Home Affairs; Minister
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: AA-signed approval document; briefing records; annual protective security report
evidence: AA-signed annual protective security report approval; pre-submission briefing records to AA; evidence of AA review
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework; NDIA Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance; NDIA Ministerial Communications Protocol; NDIA Delegations Framework
reviewTriggers: Accountable Authority change; significant security event affecting report content; PSPF reporting guidance update
notes: The AA confirmation must be formal and documented — verbal confirmation is insufficient. Linked to GOV-014 and GOV-015. The AA's sign-off must be obtained prior to submission to the Minister and Home Affairs.

title: Cooperation with Home Affairs Assurance Activities
obligationDescription: Entities cooperate with the Department of Home Affairs' assurance activities to review annual protective security reports.
requirement: The NDIA shall cooperate with the Department of Home Affairs' assurance activities to review annual protective security reports.
obligationRef: PSPF - 34
controlObjective: Enable the Department of Home Affairs to conduct whole-of-government assurance activities, supporting the accuracy and consistency of annual protective security reporting across entities.
threat: Obstruction of WoAG assurance activities; inaccurate or inconsistent protective security reporting at whole-of-government level
applicability: Chief Security Officer (CSO); Accountable Authority (CEO); all relevant NDIA personnel
excluded: None
guidance: Designate a primary point of contact for Department of Home Affairs assurance activities. Respond promptly to assurance requests. Provide requested documentation and access within stipulated timeframes. Escalate to Accountable Authority where required.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance control)
processSteps: 1. Designate contact point for Home Affairs assurance activities. 2. Respond to assurance requests within required timeframes. 3. Provide documentation as requested. 4. Escalate issues to AA as required. 5. Record all assurance interactions.
responsible: Chief Security Officer (CSO); NDIA Security Team
consulted: General Counsel; Group Manager, Technology; Accountable Authority
informed: NDIA Executive; Department of Home Affairs
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority
verification: Records of Home Affairs assurance engagements; response records; documentation provided to Home Affairs
evidence: Correspondence with Department of Home Affairs; documentation provided during assurance activities; response records
auditFrequency: As required by Department of Home Affairs
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
relatedProcedures: PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance; Department of Home Affairs Assurance Framework
reviewTriggers: Home Affairs assurance request; significant security incident; PSPF reporting guidance update
notes: Question type for Req 34 is Yes/No/NA — applicable where Home Affairs conducts assurance reviews. NDIA must cooperate fully and not obstruct or delay assurance activities.

title: Annual Cyber Security Survey Submission to ASD
obligationDescription: The annual Cyber Security Survey is submitted to the Australian Signals Directorate.
requirement: The NDIA shall complete and submit the annual Cyber Security Survey to the Australian Signals Directorate in accordance with PSPF Requirement 35, ensuring the survey accurately reflects the NDIA's cyber security maturity and posture, supported by documented evidence.
obligationRef: PSPF - 35
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.1, 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-7, PM-6; ASD Essential Eight Maturity Model
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA participates in whole-of-government cyber security performance reporting by submitting an accurate and timely annual Cyber Security Survey to ASD, demonstrating the Agency's cyber security maturity and commitment to continuous improvement.
threat: Failure to submit the annual Cyber Security Survey; inaccurate or unsubstantiated survey responses; non-compliance with PSPF Req 35; inability to demonstrate cyber security maturity to ASD; gaps in whole-of-government cyber security visibility.
applicability: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); NDIA Cyber Security team; all NDIA ICT systems and technology assets assessed against the Essential Eight and other ASD survey metrics.
excluded: Systems operating under approved security exceptions, provided those exceptions are documented within the survey response.
guidance: Establish an annual Cyber Security Survey completion process led by the CISO. Evidence must be collected from ICT operations, security monitoring tools and IRAP assessment findings. Survey responses must be accurate, evidence-based and consistent with the NDIA's self-assessed Essential Eight maturity levels. Submit via ASD's prescribed channel within the required timeframe. Retain submission confirmation and all supporting evidence.
technicalControls: Essential Eight maturity assessment tools; cyber security metrics dashboards; ICT asset register; security monitoring and logging platforms.
processSteps: 1. CISO to initiate survey completion in accordance with ASD's published survey schedule. 2. Gather and validate evidence from ICT teams on Essential Eight and other cyber security metrics. 3. CISO reviews and validates all survey responses against supporting evidence. 4. Obtain CSO endorsement of final survey content. 5. Submit survey to ASD via prescribed channel within the required timeframe. 6. Retain ASD submission confirmation and all supporting evidence.
responsible: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); NDIA Cyber Security team; Chief Security Officer (CSO)
consulted: Chief Information Officer (CIO); Group Manager, Technology; NDIA ICT Operations
informed: Accountable Authority (CEO); Audit Committee; Australian Signals Directorate; NDIA Executive Leadership Team
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: ASD submission confirmation; CISO endorsement records; internal review of survey responses against supporting evidence.
evidence: ASD submission confirmation; completed survey responses; CISO and CSO endorsement records; supporting evidence for each survey response (e.g. Essential Eight assessment results, IRAP findings, security monitoring data).
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: ASD Cyber Security Survey guidance; PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance (Dept of Home Affairs); NDIA Essential Eight Assessment Procedure; ASD Essential Eight Maturity Model
reviewTriggers: PSPF update; change to ASD survey format, scope or submission requirements; significant change to NDIA cyber security posture; Essential Eight Maturity Model update; CISO change; material security incident.
notes: The ASD Cyber Security Survey is distinct from the PSPF Annual Protective Security Report (Reqs 31–34) — it is submitted directly to ASD and specifically measures cyber security maturity. Survey responses must be accurate and supported by verifiable evidence; misrepresentation constitutes a compliance and reputational risk. PSPF question type for Req 35 is Yes/No. Note: this row carries Policy Number NDIA-POL-ICT-GOV-002, which differs from NDIA-POL-ICT-GOV-001 used across other ICT Governance Policy rows — this should be reviewed for consistency.

section: Duty to Govern the Commonwealth Entity
title: Duty to Govern the Commonwealth Entity
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must govern the entity in a way that: (a) promotes the proper use and management of public resources; (b) promotes achievement of the entity's purposes; and (c) promotes financial sustainability.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure the Accountable Authority governs the entity in a manner that promotes the proper use and management of public resources, achievement of the entity's purposes, and financial sustainability.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 15(1)
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-1; Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA is governed in compliance with PGPA Act obligations, promoting proper use of public resources, achievement of purposes, and financial sustainability including for ICT governance.
threat: Misuse or mismanagement of public resources; failure to achieve entity purposes; financial unsustainability; governance failure; legal and reputational risk
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); NDIA Executive Leadership Team; all NDIA operations
excluded: None
guidance: Embed PGPA governance obligations in the NDIA corporate governance framework, policies and procedures. Brief incoming Accountable Authority on PGPA obligations. Conduct annual compliance self-assessment and report to Audit Committee.
technicalControls: None (legislative/governance obligation)
processSteps: 1. Maintain NDIA governance framework aligned to PGPA Act. 2. Brief Accountable Authority on obligations at appointment. 3. Embed PGPA governance in relevant policies. 4. Conduct annual PGPA compliance self-assessment. 5. Report findings to Audit Committee.
responsible: Chief Financial Officer (CFO); General Counsel; Chief Security Officer (CSO)
consulted: NDIA Audit Committee; NDIA Board; Department of Finance
informed: NDIA Executive Leadership Team; Responsible Minister; ANAO
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Internal audit; Audit Committee review; ANAO performance audit; annual governance self-assessment
evidence: NDIA Corporate Governance Framework (current, AA-approved); Audit Committee minutes; annual PGPA compliance self-assessment report
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Financial Management Policy; NDIA ICT Governance Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013; PGPA Rule 2014; Department of Finance Governance Guidance; NDIA Governance Framework
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act amendment; machinery-of-government change; Accountable Authority change; significant governance failure; ANAO finding; Department of Finance guidance update
notes: PGPA s 15(1) is the foundational governance obligation for all Commonwealth entities. It underpins all downstream security and governance requirements including the PSPF. ICT governance must be managed as part of the broader entity governance obligation.

section: Duty to Keep Responsible Minister and Finance Minister Informed
title: Duty to Keep Responsible Minister and Finance Minister Informed
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must: keep the responsible Minister informed of entity activities; provide reports, documents and information as required; notify the Minister of significant decisions; give reasonable notice of significant issues; and notify as soon as practicable after becoming aware of significant issues affecting the entity.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure the Accountable Authority keeps the responsible Minister and Finance Minister informed of entity activities, provides required reports and documents, notifies them of significant decisions, and gives reasonable notice of significant issues.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 19(1)
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-11; Commonwealth Accountability and Transparency Framework
controlObjective: Ensure ministers receive timely and accurate information on NDIA activities, significant decisions and issues to enable effective ministerial oversight and accountability.
threat: Ministerial accountability gaps; significant issues not reported in time; governance breach; parliamentary scrutiny due to uninformed minister
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); Ministerial Liaison; NDIA Executive Leadership Team
excluded: Routine operational matters below significance threshold
guidance: Establish and maintain a formal ministerial liaison process with defined significance thresholds for reporting. Brief Accountable Authority on ministerial reporting obligations at appointment. Maintain auditable records of all ministerial communications and notifications.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance obligation)
processSteps: 1. Define significance thresholds for ministerial notification. 2. Establish ministerial liaison process and contacts. 3. Notify Minister of significant decisions and issues as they arise. 4. Provide required reports and documents on schedule. 5. Maintain records of all ministerial communications.
responsible: Chief of Staff; Ministerial Liaison Officer; General Counsel
consulted: CFO; Group Managers; Legal
informed: NDIA Board; Department of Finance; Minister's Office; ANAO
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Ministerial liaison records review; audit of significant event notifications; annual governance review
evidence: Records of ministerial briefings and notifications; significant event notification records; ministerial correspondence
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Ministerial Communications Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 19; NDIA Ministerial Liaison Protocol; NDIA Significant Events Reporting Procedure
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act amendment; ministerial change; significant organisational event; machinery-of-government change; ANAO finding
notes: Significant issues include matters that could affect public confidence in the NDIA, result in material financial impact, or have parliamentary implications. This obligation is separate from but related to the PSPF annual protective security reporting obligations (Reqs 31–34).

section: Application of Government Policy Orders – Corporate CCEs
title: Compliance with Government Policy Orders
obligationDescription: If a Government Policy Order applies to the NDIA, the accountable authority must ensure the order is complied with in relation to the entity and, so far as practicable, any subsidiary.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure that any Government Policy Order applicable to the entity is complied with, including in relation to any subsidiaries, so far as practicable.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 22(3)
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.1, 5.2; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-1; Commonwealth Regulatory Framework
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA identifies, monitors and complies with all Government Policy Orders issued under the PGPA Act that apply to the entity.
threat: Non-compliance with GPOs; inconsistent application of government policy; regulatory breach; reputational and legal risk to the entity
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA operations and any subsidiaries
excluded: None
guidance: Maintain a register of all applicable Government Policy Orders. Assign responsibility for monitoring and compliance to relevant business owners. Review GPO register at least annually and upon issuance of new GPOs. Report compliance status to Audit Committee.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance obligation); compliance management registers
processSteps: 1. Establish and maintain a register of applicable Government Policy Orders. 2. Assign compliance ownership for each GPO. 3. Monitor for new or amended GPOs. 4. Assess compliance status annually. 5. Report to Audit Committee and AA.
responsible: General Counsel; CFO; Group Managers
consulted: Department of Finance; relevant policy departments; Audit Committee
informed: NDIA Executive Leadership Team; Responsible Minister; ANAO
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: GPO compliance register review; internal audit; Audit Committee review; ANAO assessment
evidence: GPO compliance register; compliance assessments per applicable GPO; Audit Committee reporting
auditFrequency: Annual; on issuance of new or amended GPO
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA ICT Governance Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 22; PGPA Rule 2014; Department of Finance Policy Register; NDIA Compliance Framework
reviewTriggers: New Government Policy Order issued; existing GPO amended or revoked; PGPA Act amendment; ANAO finding
notes: Government Policy Orders are legislative instruments made under PGPA Act s 22 and are binding on applicable Commonwealth entities. The ICT Governance Policy must reference current applicable GPOs. Monitor the Federal Register of Legislation for updates.

title: Preparation and Publication of Annual Corporate Plan
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must prepare a corporate plan at least once each reporting period covering the entity's purposes, operating environment, performance measures and activities, including for any subsidiaries. The plan must be given to the responsible Minister and Finance Minister.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure the Accountable Authority prepares a corporate plan each reporting period, covering purposes, operating environment, performance measures and activities, and provides the plan to the responsible Minister and Finance Minister.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 35
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 6.1, 9.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PL-1; Commonwealth Performance Framework
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA has a current, AA-approved corporate plan that sets out its purposes, priorities, performance measures and activities — including ICT governance and cyber security strategic objectives.
threat: Absence of strategic direction; failure to achieve entity purposes; non-compliance with PGPA performance reporting requirements; inadequate ICT planning
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); NDIA Executive Leadership Team; all NDIA business areas
excluded: None
guidance: Prepare the corporate plan annually in accordance with the Commonwealth Performance Framework. Incorporate ICT strategic goals, cyber security uplift plans, and technology governance objectives. Submit to the responsible Minister and Finance Minister. Publish in accordance with PGPA Rule requirements.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance obligation)
processSteps: 1. Commence corporate plan development process no later than six months before reporting period end. 2. Incorporate ICT and security objectives from relevant strategies. 3. Obtain AA approval. 4. Provide to responsible Minister and Finance Minister. 5. Publish as required by PGPA Rule.
responsible: CFO; Corporate Planning team; NDIA Executive Leadership Team
consulted: Responsible Minister; Finance Minister; NDIA Board; CISO (for ICT/security content)
informed: All NDIA staff; ANAO; Department of Finance
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Corporate plan existence and currency review; submission records to Ministers; ANAO assessment; Department of Finance review
evidence: Published corporate plan (AA-approved); ministerial submission records; Department of Finance acknowledgement
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA ICT Strategic Plan; NDIA Cyber Security Strategy; NDIA Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 35; PGPA Rule 2014 Part 2-1; Resource Management Guide No. 132; Commonwealth Performance Framework
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act or Rule amendment; significant change to NDIA purposes or operating environment; new government priorities; ministerial direction
notes: ICT governance and cyber security uplift objectives should be reflected in the corporate plan to ensure alignment between legislative planning obligations and the NDIA cyber security strategy. The corporate plan must be published on the NDIA website.

title: Maintenance of Records About Entity Performance
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must cause records to be kept that properly record and explain the entity's performance in achieving its purposes. Records must enable preparation of annual performance statements.
requirement: The NDIA shall cause records to be kept that properly record and explain the entity's performance in achieving its purposes, including records sufficient to enable preparation of annual performance statements.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 37
ismControls: ISM-0040; ISM controls for records management (records security)
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.33, A.5.34; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-3, AU-12; Archives Act 1983; Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard
controlObjective: Ensure accurate and auditable records exist to demonstrate the NDIA's performance against corporate plan purposes, enabling transparent and verifiable performance reporting.
threat: Inability to demonstrate performance; inaccurate or unverifiable annual performance statements; PGPA non-compliance; ANAO qualification; loss of performance evidence
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA business areas; Corporate Planning
excluded: Preliminary or working papers not forming part of the official record
guidance: Establish and maintain a records management framework that captures performance data and supporting evidence. Integrate recordkeeping obligations into corporate planning and performance measurement processes. Ensure records are compliant with Archives Act 1983 requirements.
technicalControls: Records management system; document management platform; performance data repositories
processSteps: 1. Define records to be kept for each corporate plan performance measure. 2. Assign responsibility for performance record maintenance. 3. Conduct periodic records audits. 4. Ensure records are accessible and auditable. 5. Comply with Archives Act disposal authorities.
responsible: CFO; Corporate Planning; Chief Information Officer (CIO); Records Manager
consulted: NDIA Audit Committee; ANAO; National Archives of Australia
informed: All NDIA business areas; NDIA Executive; Minister
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Records audit; ANAO assessment; internal audit; National Archives compliance assessment
evidence: Performance records in records management system; records disposal authorities; records audit reports
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Records Management Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 37; Archives Act 1983; Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard; National Archives Normal Administrative Practice
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act or Rule amendment; significant change to performance measures; Archives Act update; ANAO finding; records system migration
notes: Records must be sufficient to support independent verification by the ANAO. ICT performance metrics (system availability, security posture, project delivery) should be captured as performance records where included in the corporate plan.

title: Measuring and Assessing Entity Performance
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must measure and assess the performance of the entity in achieving its purposes, in compliance with requirements prescribed by the PGPA Rule.
requirement: The NDIA shall measure and assess its performance in achieving its purposes in compliance with PGPA Rule requirements, including ICT governance and security performance.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 38
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.1, 10.2; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-7, PM-6; Commonwealth Performance Framework
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA systematically measures and assesses its performance against corporate plan targets, including ICT governance effectiveness and cyber security program performance.
threat: Failure to detect underperformance; inaccurate performance reporting; non-compliance with PGPA Rule; inability to demonstrate achievement of purposes; ICT and security performance not measured
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA business areas; Corporate Planning
excluded: None
guidance: Establish performance measurement and assessment processes aligned to corporate plan measures. Include ICT governance and cyber security metrics as key performance indicators. Report assessment results to Audit Committee and AA. Integrate security performance measurement into broader entity performance monitoring.
technicalControls: Performance management systems; ICT performance dashboards; security metrics platforms
processSteps: 1. Define performance measures and data collection methods for each corporate plan purpose. 2. Collect and analyse performance data at regular intervals. 3. Include ICT and security KPIs in performance assessment. 4. Report performance to Audit Committee quarterly. 5. Document assessments for annual performance statements.
responsible: CFO; Corporate Planning; CISO (for security metrics); Group Managers
consulted: NDIA Audit Committee; NDIA Board; ANAO
informed: All NDIA business areas; Responsible Minister; Department of Finance
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Performance reporting review; Audit Committee review of performance results; ANAO assessment; internal audit
evidence: Performance assessment reports; ICT and security KPI results; Audit Committee performance reporting; corporate plan measurement data
auditFrequency: Annual; KPI reporting reviewed quarterly
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA ICT Strategic Plan; NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 38; PGPA Rule 2014 Part 2-2; Commonwealth Performance Framework; Resource Management Guide No. 131
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act or Rule amendment; significant change to corporate plan purposes or measures; ANAO finding; new government performance reporting requirements
notes: ICT governance performance measures (e.g., Essential Eight maturity, system availability, project delivery against plan) should be incorporated into the NDIA performance framework to satisfy both this PGPA obligation and PSPF cyber security strategy requirements.

title: Preparation of Annual Performance Statements
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must prepare annual performance statements for inclusion in the entity's annual report, reporting on the entity's performance against its purposes as set out in the Corporate Plan.
requirement: The NDIA shall prepare annual performance statements for inclusion in the entity's annual report, reporting on performance against the purposes set out in the Corporate Plan.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 39
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-11; Commonwealth Performance Framework
controlObjective: Ensure transparent public reporting of NDIA performance through annual performance statements, covering achievement of corporate plan purposes including ICT governance objectives.
threat: Non-compliance with PGPA performance reporting obligations; inaccurate public reporting; ANAO qualification; parliamentary scrutiny; inability to demonstrate achievement of purposes
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); Corporate Planning; CFO
excluded: None
guidance: Prepare annual performance statements based on performance records and assessments (see GOV-022, GOV-023). Include ICT governance and security outcomes where they form part of corporate plan purposes. Obtain AA approval before inclusion in the annual report. Statements must be prepared in accordance with PGPA Rule Part 2-2.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance obligation); performance reporting platforms
processSteps: 1. Compile performance evidence against each corporate plan purpose. 2. Draft annual performance statements. 3. Obtain ANAO review as required. 4. Obtain AA approval. 5. Include in annual report and table in Parliament.
responsible: CFO; Corporate Planning; General Counsel
consulted: NDIA Audit Committee; ANAO; NDIA Board
informed: All NDIA staff; Responsible Minister; Parliament; Department of Finance
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Annual report review; ANAO performance statements assessment; Audit Committee review; internal quality assurance
evidence: Approved annual performance statements; performance evidence supporting each statement; ANAO review correspondence; AA approval records
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Records Management Policy; NDIA ICT Strategic Plan
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 39; PGPA Rule 2014 Part 2-2; Resource Management Guide No. 134; Commonwealth Performance Framework
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act or Rule amendment; ANAO audit finding; significant change to corporate plan purposes; new performance reporting guidance from Department of Finance
notes: Annual performance statements are subject to ANAO review. Where ICT governance or cyber security outcomes form part of the corporate plan purposes, they must be addressed in the performance statements. Statements must be honest and verifiable.

title: Establishment and Maintenance of Audit Committee
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must ensure the entity has an audit committee with functions including reviewing the appropriateness of the entity's financial reporting, performance reporting, systems of risk oversight and management, and systems of internal control.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure it has an audit committee with functions including reviewing the appropriateness of financial reporting, performance reporting, systems of risk oversight and management, and systems of internal control.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 45
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.2, 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-2, PM-1; PGPA Rule Part 2-3; ANAO Better Practice Guide — Audit Committees
controlObjective: Ensure an effective, independent audit committee exists to provide oversight of NDIA governance, risk management, compliance, and performance reporting including ICT and cyber security matters.
threat: Inadequate oversight of financial, performance and risk management; governance failures undetected; ICT and security risks not reviewed at committee level; non-compliance with PGPA
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); Audit Committee members; all NDIA governance structures
excluded: None
guidance: Establish and maintain an Audit Committee in accordance with PGPA Rule Part 2-3 requirements. Ensure ICT governance and cyber security are standing agenda items. The CISO must report to the Audit Committee at each meeting per PSPF 2025 Req 213. Maintain the Audit Committee Charter, reviewed at least annually.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance obligation); audit management and reporting tools
processSteps: 1. Establish Audit Committee with appropriate membership per PGPA Rule. 2. Develop and maintain Audit Committee Charter. 3. Schedule regular committee meetings (minimum quarterly). 4. Ensure CISO provides cyber security risk briefing at each meeting. 5. Review committee effectiveness annually.
responsible: Audit Committee Chair; CFO; General Counsel; Chief Internal Auditor
consulted: CISO (for cyber security reporting); ANAO; External Auditors
informed: NDIA Board; Responsible Minister; NDIA Executive; ANAO
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Audit Committee Charter review; Audit Committee meeting minutes; ANAO assessment; annual effectiveness review
evidence: Audit Committee Charter (AA-approved); Audit Committee meeting minutes; CISO briefing records; annual effectiveness review report
auditFrequency: Annual; CISO cyber security reporting at each Audit Committee meeting
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA ICT Governance Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 45; PGPA Rule 2014 Part 2-3; ANAO Better Practice Guide — Audit Committees; NDIA Audit Committee Charter
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act or Rule amendment; Audit Committee membership change; significant governance failure; ANAO finding; PSPF update affecting CISO reporting obligations
owner: Chief Financial Officer (CFO); Audit Committee Chair
notes: PSPF 2025 Req 213 (new, effective 01/07/2025) requires the CISO to report on cyber security risk at each Audit Committee meeting and biannually on the cyber security strategy and uplift plan. This must be reflected in the Audit Committee Charter and agenda. ICT and cyber security must be standing agenda items.

title: Preparation and Tabling of Annual Report
obligationDescription: The accountable authority must prepare an annual report for the entity in accordance with the PGPA Rule. The report is presented to the responsible Minister for tabling in Parliament.
requirement: The NDIA shall prepare an annual report in accordance with the PGPA Rule for presentation to the responsible Minister for tabling in Parliament.
obligationRef: PGPA Act 2013 s 46
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-11; Parliamentary Reporting Requirements; PGPA Rule Part 2-3
controlObjective: Ensure transparent public accountability through an annual report to Parliament covering NDIA performance, governance, financial management and ICT outcomes.
threat: Non-compliance with PGPA annual reporting obligations; reputational damage; parliamentary scrutiny; ANAO qualification; public accountability failure
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA operations
excluded: None
guidance: Prepare the annual report in accordance with PGPA Rule Part 2-3 and Department of Finance annual report guidance. Include all mandatory content including financial statements, performance statements, governance and ICT disclosures. Obtain AA approval and submit to the responsible Minister for tabling in Parliament.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance obligation)
processSteps: 1. Establish annual report preparation project plan and timeline. 2. Coordinate inputs from all business areas (finance, performance, ICT, governance). 3. Include protective security report content per PSPF Reqs 31–34. 4. Obtain AA approval. 5. Submit to Minister for tabling in Parliament by deadline.
responsible: CFO; Corporate Planning; General Counsel; Communications
consulted: Responsible Minister; ANAO; Audit Committee; NDIA Board; CISO
informed: All NDIA staff; Parliament; Department of Finance; ANAO; public
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under PGPA Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Annual report existence and tabling confirmation; ANAO financial statement audit; compliance with PGPA Rule requirements; timeliness review
evidence: Published annual report; Ministerial submission records; tabling records in Parliament; ANAO audit opinion
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Financial Management Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA ICT Governance Policy
relatedProcedures: PGPA Act 2013 s 46; PGPA Rule 2014 Part 2-3; Department of Finance Annual Report Guidance; NDIA Annual Report Style Guide
reviewTriggers: PGPA Act or Rule amendment; change to annual report guidance from Department of Finance; significant organisational change; parliamentary committee request
notes: The annual report must include annual performance statements (s 39) and financial statements audited by the ANAO. ICT governance and cyber security disclosures should be included where material. The PSPF annual protective security report obligations (Reqs 31–34) are related but separate submissions.

title: NDIA Statutory Functions — ICT Governance Alignment
obligationDescription: The Agency's functions include: delivering the NDIS; collecting, analysing and using data and information relating to the NDIS; developing and enhancing the disability sector; facilitating innovation; building community awareness.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure its ICT governance framework and technology capabilities are aligned to and support the performance of all Agency statutory functions defined in NDIS Act 2013 s.118, including NDIS delivery, data collection and analysis, disability sector development, innovation facilitation and community awareness.
obligationRef: NDIS Act 2013 Ch.6 / Pt.1 s.118
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 4.1, 4.2, 6.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-1, SA-3; Disability (Access to Premises) Standards; Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1
controlObjective: Ensure ICT governance and systems are aligned to and enable performance of all NDIA statutory functions under s.118, with particular focus on NDIS data management and service delivery capabilities.
threat: ICT systems not fit for purpose to support statutory functions; data management failures impairing NDIS delivery; technology constraints limiting innovation or community awareness; non-delivery of NDIS obligations.
applicability: All NDIA ICT systems and data assets; all NDIA business areas; NDIA participants and their representatives.
excluded: Functions performed by other Commonwealth entities not delegated to the NDIA.
guidance: Map NDIA ICT capabilities to each statutory function. Identify capability gaps and address through ICT strategic planning. Ensure ICT governance decisions consider impact on delivery of all statutory functions. Review alignment annually.
technicalControls: NDIS IT systems (participant management, plan management, payment systems); data analytics platforms; digital communication and community awareness channels.
processSteps: 1. Map ICT systems to NDIA statutory functions. 2. Identify capability gaps. 3. Incorporate gap remediation in ICT strategic plan. 4. Review alignment at each major ICT governance decision point. 5. Report alignment status to Board and AA annually.
responsible: Chief Information Officer (CIO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Group Managers (service delivery, data, innovation)
consulted: DSS; participants and disability community representatives; ANAO
informed: Ministerial Council; Minister; all NDIA staff; public
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — foundational legislative obligation under NDIS Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: ICT-to-function alignment review; annual ICT strategic plan assessment; Board review of capability gaps.
evidence: ICT capability mapping to statutory functions; ICT strategic plan; Board review records; gap analysis reports.
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA ICT Strategic Plan; NDIA Data Management Policy; NDIA Innovation Policy
relatedProcedures: NDIS Act 2013 s.118; NDIA ICT Strategy; NDIA Service Delivery Framework; WCAG 2.1 Guidelines
reviewTriggers: NDIS Act amendment; new or changed NDIS program requirements; significant ICT strategic change; Government policy change; accessibility standards update.
notes: s.118 defines the NDIA's core statutory mandate. All ICT governance decisions should be assessed against their impact on the Agency's ability to perform these functions. ICT systems for data collection and analysis are especially critical given their role in NDIS sustainability monitoring.

title: Compliance with Ministerial Directions and Annual Report Publication
