obligationDescription: The Minister may give written directions to the Agency about the performance of its functions. The Agency must comply. Directions must be published in the Annual Report.
requirement: The NDIA shall comply with all written Ministerial directions about the performance of its functions in accordance with NDIS Act 2013 s.121, ensuring ICT implications are assessed and implemented, and that all directions are published in the Annual Report.
obligationRef: NDIS Act 2013 Ch.6 / Pt.1 s.121
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.1, 5.2; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-1; Commonwealth Regulatory Framework
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA promptly and effectively implements Ministerial directions — including any ICT-related obligations — and meets the obligation to publish all directions in the Annual Report.
threat: Non-compliance with Ministerial directions; delayed or inadequate ICT impact assessment of directions; failure to publish directions in Annual Report; reputational and legal risk.
applicability: Board; Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA operations and ICT systems affected by directions.
excluded: Informal ministerial requests not constituting written directions under s.121.
guidance: Establish a process for receiving, assessing, implementing and publishing Ministerial directions. Designate a coordination point (General Counsel / Ministerial Liaison). Assess ICT impact of each direction. Include directions in Annual Report preparation process.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance); document management systems for directions register.
processSteps: 1. Receive and register Ministerial direction. 2. Assess compliance requirements including ICT impacts. 3. Develop implementation plan. 4. Implement direction within required timeframe. 5. Include direction in Annual Report. 6. Report compliance to Board and AA.
responsible: General Counsel; Ministerial Liaison; Chief Information Officer (CIO) (for ICT-related directions); Group Managers
consulted: Responsible Minister; Legal Counsel; DSS; ANAO
informed: All NDIA staff; Parliament; public (via Annual Report)
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — mandatory legislative obligation. Compliance is required. Seek legal advice if a direction is ambiguous or conflicts with other legislative obligations.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Directions register review; Annual Report content review; compliance implementation evidence.
evidence: Ministerial directions register; compliance implementation records; Annual Report pages referencing directions; legal advice records where applicable.
auditFrequency: Annual; on receipt of each Ministerial direction.
relatedPolicies: NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA Legal and Compliance Policy
relatedProcedures: NDIS Act 2013 s.121; NDIA Ministerial Communications Protocol; NDIA Directions Compliance Procedure; NDIA Annual Report Preparation Procedure
reviewTriggers: New Ministerial direction received; NDIS Act amendment; Annual Report preparation cycle; change of Minister; legal advice update.
notes: Ministerial directions under s.121 are binding on the NDIA. Directions may impose ICT-related requirements including system changes, data sharing arrangements or new reporting capabilities. All directions must be published in the Annual Report. General Counsel must assess each direction for ICT governance implications.

title: Board Responsibilities for Strategic Governance, Risk Management and Internal Control
obligationDescription: The Board is responsible for: determining strategic objectives; ensuring the Agency performs its functions effectively; ensuring appropriate risk management; overseeing financial management; ensuring proper internal governance.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure the Board fulfils its statutory governance responsibilities under NDIS Act 2013 s.124, including determining strategic ICT objectives, ensuring effective performance of Agency functions, overseeing ICT risk management and financial management of technology assets, and ensuring proper internal ICT governance.
obligationRef: NDIS Act 2013 Ch.6 / Pt.2 / Div.1 s.124
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.1, 5.2, 6.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-1, PM-9; PGPA Act 2013 s.45 (Audit Committee); Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA Board exercises effective, informed oversight of ICT strategy, risk and internal governance, fulfilling its statutory responsibilities under s.124.
threat: Board failing to exercise adequate oversight of ICT risks; strategic ICT decisions made without Board engagement; inadequate ICT risk management leading to critical system failures or security breaches.
applicability: Board; Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA strategic ICT decisions and risk management frameworks.
excluded: Day-to-day operational ICT matters delegated to the CEO under s.159.
guidance: Ensure ICT strategy and cyber security risk are standing Board agenda items. Provide regular Board briefings on ICT risk posture and strategic ICT initiatives. The CISO must report to the Audit Committee per PSPF 2025 Req 213. Maintain Board-level ICT risk dashboard.
technicalControls: Board reporting and governance platforms; ICT risk dashboards; audit and risk management systems.
processSteps: 1. Include ICT strategy and cyber security risk as standing Board agenda items. 2. Provide quarterly ICT risk briefings to Board. 3. Ensure CISO presents to Audit Committee per PSPF Req 213. 4. Obtain Board approval for major ICT strategic decisions. 5. Report ICT risk status in Annual Report.
responsible: Board; Accountable Authority (CEO); Chief Information Officer (CIO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
consulted: Audit Committee; ANAO; external ICT advisors; General Counsel
informed: All NDIA staff; Minister; Ministerial Council; ANAO
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under NDIS Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Board minutes; Audit Committee minutes; ICT risk reporting records; Board ICT strategy review records.
evidence: Board meeting minutes covering ICT strategy and risk; Audit Committee minutes (CISO reporting); Board-approved ICT strategic plans; ICT risk briefing records.
auditFrequency: Annual; ICT risk reporting reviewed quarterly by the Board.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Cyber Security Policy
relatedProcedures: NDIS Act 2013 s.124; NDIA Board Charter; NDIA Audit Committee Charter; NDIA ICT Governance Framework
reviewTriggers: NDIS Act amendment; Board composition change; significant ICT strategic change; major ICT incident; PSPF update; ANAO finding.
notes: Board oversight must be meaningful and informed — not merely ratifying management recommendations. ICT risk is a material enterprise risk for the NDIA and must receive appropriate Board attention. PSPF 2025 Req 213 requires CISO to report at each Audit Committee meeting and biannually on the cyber security strategy.

title: Board Consideration of NDIS Financial Sustainability, Objects and Participant Interests
obligationDescription: In performing its functions, the Board must have regard to the financial sustainability of the NDIS, the objects and principles of the Act, and the interests of participants.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure the Board, in performing its functions, has regard to the financial sustainability of the NDIS, the objects and principles of the NDIS Act 2013, and the interests of participants, including in all ICT governance and technology investment decisions.
obligationRef: NDIS Act 2013 Ch.6 / Pt.2 / Div.1 s.125A
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 4.2, 6.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-1; Commonwealth Risk Management Policy; Disability (Access to Premises) Standards; WCAG 2.1
controlObjective: Ensure ICT governance and technology investment decisions explicitly consider NDIS financial sustainability, the objects and principles of the NDIS Act, and the interests and rights of participants.
threat: ICT decisions that undermine NDIS financial sustainability; technology systems that fail to uphold the rights and interests of participants; ICT governance that does not reflect the principles of the NDIS Act.
applicability: Board; Accountable Authority (CEO); all ICT strategy and investment decisions; all participant-facing systems.
excluded: Technical operational decisions that do not materially affect NDIS sustainability or participant interests.
guidance: Embed consideration of NDIS sustainability, Act objects and participant interests into ICT governance decision-making frameworks (e.g. business cases, architectural decisions, procurement). Conduct participant impact assessments for significant ICT changes. Report to Board on ICT contribution to NDIS sustainability.
technicalControls: Business case assessment frameworks; participant impact assessment tools; accessibility compliance testing tools for participant-facing systems.
processSteps: 1. Include sustainability and participant interest criteria in ICT business case templates. 2. Conduct participant impact assessments for significant ICT changes. 3. Report to Board on ICT contribution to NDIS sustainability. 4. Ensure accessibility compliance of participant-facing systems. 5. Review alignment with NDIS objects and principles annually.
responsible: Board; Accountable Authority (CEO); Chief Information Officer (CIO); Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
consulted: Participant Advisory Group; DSS; disability representative organisations; ANAO
informed: All participants and their representatives; Minister; Ministerial Council; NDIA staff
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under NDIS Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: ICT business case reviews; participant impact assessment records; Board deliberation records; accessibility compliance reports.
evidence: ICT business cases incorporating sustainability and participant impact criteria; accessibility compliance test reports; Board deliberation records; participant feedback mechanism evidence.
auditFrequency: Annual; on major ICT investment decisions.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Participant Engagement Policy; NDIA ICT Strategic Plan
relatedProcedures: NDIS Act 2013 s.125A; NDIA ICT Investment Assessment Framework; NDIA Participant Impact Assessment Procedure; Disability (Access to Premises) Standards
reviewTriggers: NDIS Act amendment; significant change to NDIS sustainability position; new participant engagement requirements; accessibility standards update; ANAO finding.
notes: ICT investments must demonstrate value for money and contribution to scheme sustainability. Participant-facing ICT systems must comply with WCAG 2.1 AA (minimum) and reflect NDIS Act principles of independence, inclusion and reasonable and necessary support. Participant interests must be a primary consideration in major ICT decisions.

title: CEO Day-to-Day Management Responsibility — ICT Governance Alignment
obligationDescription: The CEO is responsible for managing the day-to-day affairs of the Agency and must act in accordance with the strategies, policies and directions of the Board.
requirement: The NDIA shall ensure the CEO manages the day-to-day affairs of the Agency, including ICT operations and governance, in accordance with the Board's strategies, policies and directions as required by NDIS Act 2013 s.159.
obligationRef: NDIS Act 2013 Ch.6 / Pt.4 / Div.1 s.159
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.1, 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2; PGPA Act 2013 s.15
controlObjective: Ensure the CEO exercises effective day-to-day oversight of ICT operations and governance, aligned with Board direction and consistent with all applicable legislative and policy frameworks.
threat: CEO disengaged from ICT management decisions; ICT operations not aligned with Board strategy; gaps between Board-approved ICT policy and day-to-day implementation; accountability failures for ICT incidents.
applicability: Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA ICT operations, systems and day-to-day management decisions.
excluded: Strategic ICT decisions reserved for the Board under s.124.
guidance: Establish a clear delegation framework for ICT management from CEO to CIO and CISO. CEO to receive regular ICT operational and security briefings. Ensure ICT operations are consistent with Board-approved strategies and policies. Brief incoming CEO on PSPF Accountable Authority obligations.
technicalControls: None (administrative/governance); ICT executive reporting and briefing systems.
processSteps: 1. Establish ICT delegation framework from CEO to CIO and CISO. 2. Schedule regular ICT operational and security briefings for CEO. 3. CEO to ensure ICT operations comply with Board policies. 4. CEO to escalate material ICT issues to Board. 5. CEO to report on ICT performance in Annual Report.
responsible: CEO; Chief Information Officer (CIO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Chief Security Officer (CSO)
consulted: Board; General Counsel; Chief Financial Officer (CFO); Group Managers
informed: All NDIA staff; Minister; Board
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation under NDIS Act 2013.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: CEO ICT briefing records; ICT delegation framework review; Board-CEO alignment on ICT decisions; PSPF compliance assessment.
evidence: CEO ICT briefing records; ICT delegation instrument; Board-approved ICT strategies and policies; PSPF Accountable Authority compliance evidence.
auditFrequency: Annual; on significant ICT incidents or governance events.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Policy; NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Delegations Framework
relatedProcedures: NDIS Act 2013 s.159; NDIA Delegations Framework; NDIA ICT Governance Framework; PSPF Entity Governance Guidance
reviewTriggers: CEO change; NDIS Act amendment; significant ICT incident; Board strategy change; PSPF governance requirement change; ANAO finding.
notes: The CEO's day-to-day management responsibilities (s.159) are the operational counterpart to the Board's strategic responsibilities (s.124). The CEO is also the Accountable Authority under the PGPA Act, vesting all PSPF security governance obligations in the role. ICT governance must be clearly positioned within the CEO's management responsibilities.

title: Compliance with NDIS Rules and Regulations — ICT Obligations
obligationDescription: NDIS Rules (legislative instruments) and Regulations may be made or amended at any time. They may impose new obligations on the Agency, including information-handling, record-keeping and system requirements.
requirement: The NDIA shall monitor, assess and comply with NDIS Rules and Regulations made or amended under NDIS Act 2013 ss.209–210, including any obligations imposed on information-handling, record-keeping and ICT systems, ensuring ICT governance frameworks are updated to reflect new requirements.
obligationRef: NDIS Act 2013 Ch.7 / Pt.5 s.209 / s.210
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.1, 6.1, A.5.33; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-1, AU-3; Archives Act 1983; Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA identifies, assesses and implements ICT-related obligations arising from NDIS Rules and Regulations in a timely and controlled manner.
threat: Failure to identify new ICT obligations in NDIS Rules; delayed or inadequate ICT implementation of regulatory changes; non-compliance with record-keeping or information-handling rules; regulatory breach; risk of participant harm.
applicability: All NDIA ICT systems, data management and record-keeping capabilities; all business areas affected by NDIS Rules.
excluded: NDIS Rules with no ICT, information-handling or record-keeping implications.
guidance: Establish a regulatory change monitoring process covering NDIS Rules and Regulations. Conduct ICT impact assessments for all new or amended Rules. Integrate regulatory change requirements into ICT change management processes. Maintain a regulatory obligations register with ICT implications noted.
technicalControls: Regulatory change management tools; ICT project management and change control systems; records management platforms.
processSteps: 1. Monitor Federal Register of Legislation for new or amended NDIS Rules and Regulations. 2. Assess ICT implications of each change. 3. Update ICT systems and processes to comply. 4. Update regulatory obligations register. 5. Report material ICT regulatory changes to Board and AA.
responsible: General Counsel; Chief Information Officer (CIO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Records Manager; Chief Data Officer
consulted: DSS; Department of Finance; Privacy Officer; Legal Counsel
informed: All NDIA staff; ANAO; participants and representatives
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Not applicable — legislative obligation. Seek legal advice where compliance timeline is not achievable; document any interim risk acceptance.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Regulatory obligations register review; ICT impact assessment records; compliance implementation evidence; internal audit.
evidence: Regulatory obligations register (ICT obligations noted); ICT impact assessments; change implementation records; legal advice records.
auditFrequency: Annual; on issuance of new or amended NDIS Rules or Regulations.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA Legal and Compliance Policy; NDIA Records Management Policy; NDIA Privacy Policy
relatedProcedures: NDIS Act 2013 ss.209–210; NDIA Regulatory Obligations Register; NDIA ICT Change Management Procedure; Federal Register of Legislation monitoring process
reviewTriggers: New or amended NDIS Rules or Regulations; Privacy Act amendment; Archives Act amendment; other relevant legislative change; ANAO finding.
notes: NDIS Rules are legislative instruments that can be amended by the Minister at any time. ICT governance must be agile to accommodate rule changes. Key areas where NDIS Rules may impose ICT obligations include information and data management, plan management system requirements, and participant portal accessibility.

title: NDIA Obligation to Provide Information to Commonwealth, State and Territory Ministers
obligationDescription: The Agency must give information requested by Commonwealth, State or Territory Ministers relating to the NDIS or the Agency's operations.
requirement: The NDIA shall provide, upon request, information to Commonwealth, State or Territory Ministers relating to the NDIS or Agency operations in accordance with NDIS Act 2013 s.175, supported by ICT systems capable of accurate and timely data extraction with appropriate security and access controls.
obligationRef: NDIS Act 2013 Ch.6 / Pt.5 / Div.1 s.175
ismControls: ISM-0040, ISM-0047; ISM controls for information sharing and access management.
otherStandards: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.15, A.5.17, Cl. 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-3, PM-11; Privacy Act 1988 (Cth); Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Cth)
controlObjective: Ensure the NDIA can provide accurate, timely and appropriately protected information to Commonwealth, State and Territory Ministers upon request, with maintained audit records of all information provided.
threat: Failure to provide requested ministerial information; provision of inaccurate or incomplete data; security breach through unauthorised disclosure; non-compliance with NDIS Act; damage to inter-jurisdictional relationships.
applicability: All NDIA data and ICT systems; Accountable Authority (CEO); Ministerial Liaison; all business areas holding relevant information.
excluded: Information that is legally privileged, Cabinet-in-Confidence or subject to other lawful restrictions on disclosure.
guidance: Establish a process for receiving, assessing and responding to ministerial information requests. Ensure ICT systems support rapid and accurate data extraction. Apply appropriate security and access controls to ministerial information handling. Maintain an audit trail of all information provided. Conduct privacy review where participant data is involved.
technicalControls: Data access and extraction tools; secure transmission mechanisms (e.g. GovDex, encrypted transfer); audit logging; document management system.
processSteps: 1. Receive and register ministerial information request. 2. Assess scope and identify relevant data sources. 3. Extract requested information from ICT systems. 4. Conduct privacy and security review. 5. Provide information through secure channel. 6. Record provision in information request register.
responsible: CEO; Chief Information Officer (CIO); Chief Data Officer; Ministerial Liaison; General Counsel; Privacy Officer
consulted: Relevant State/Territory government counterparts; DSS; Privacy Office; Legal Counsel
informed: Board; Responsible Minister; NDIA Executive; ANAO
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Requests may be declined or modified where disclosure is prohibited by law (e.g. legally privileged, participant privacy protections under Privacy Act). Seek legal advice. Document and communicate reasons for any limitation on information provided.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable Authority (CEO); General Counsel
verification: Ministerial information request register review; security review records; privacy assessment records; audit log review.
evidence: Ministerial information request register; responses provided; privacy assessments; audit logs of data extraction and transmission; legal advice records where applicable.
auditFrequency: Annual governance review; on each ministerial information request.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Governance Policy; NDIA Privacy Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy; NDIA Records Management Policy
relatedProcedures: NDIS Act 2013 s.175; NDIA Ministerial Information Request Procedure; NDIA Privacy Guidelines; Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)
reviewTriggers: NDIS Act amendment; significant ministerial information request; privacy law change; inter-jurisdictional agreement change; ANAO finding.
notes: Information must be provided in a form that is accurate, accessible and appropriately de-identified where participant data is included. Requests from State/Territory Ministers typically relate to jurisdictional NDIS implementation. The NDIA must balance transparency obligations under s.175 with participant privacy protections under the Privacy Act 1988.

section: Authorised, lawful and proper use of NDIA ICT
title: Authorised use of NDIA ICT
obligationDescription: Use NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks, applications and information resources only for authorised NDIA purposes and in accordance with legal, policy and APS obligations.
requirement: Users must use NDIA ICT for authorised NDIA work. Limited personal use is permitted only when it is lawful, reasonable, low risk, does not interfere with work, and complies with NDIA policies, lawful directions and applicable laws.
obligationRef:
APS-VCE-01: Public Service Act 1999 s 13 and APSC Code of Conduct guidance.
APS-VCE-02: Public Service Act 1999 s 13(4)-(5); APSC Code of Conduct elements.
APS-EPC-01: Public Service Act 1999 ss 10, 10A and 13; APSC APS Values guidance.
NDIS-04: NDIS Act ss 118 and 124 - Agency and Board functions; s 169 - staff engaged under Public Service Act.
PGPA-01: PGPA Act governance and use of public resources obligations, including duties of accountable authorities and officials.
PSA-01: Public Service Act 1999 s 13.
PSA-02: Public Service Act 1999 s 13(8).
ismControls: Nil — APS conduct and PGPA framework drives this requirement.
otherStandards: Nil
controlObjective: Ensure NDIA ICT is used only for authorised NDIA work, supporting proper use of public resources under APS and PGPA obligations.
threat: Misuse of public resources; unauthorised personal use; reputational damage; breach of APS Code or PGPA duties.
applicability: All NDIA workers — APS employees, executives, contractors, consultants, secondees, labour-hire and authorised third parties — when using NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks, applications, data and information.
excluded: External participants, providers and members of the public using NDIA public-facing services in their own capacity; personal devices or accounts outside NDIA work (except under approved BYOD/remote-work arrangements where this requirement still applies to NDIA data accessed).
guidance: Communicate the authorised-use rule at onboarding, annual training and via log-on banner. Permit limited personal use only where lawful, reasonable, low risk and consistent with NDIA directions.
technicalControls: Log-on banner; identity and access management; web/content filtering of high-risk categories; activity logging.
processSteps: Issue accounts after AUP acknowledgement; reinforce via log-on banner; investigate suspected misuse via APS Code process; apply consequences per AUP-025.
responsible: ICT Service Owners; People Branch (onboarding & training)
consulted: CISO; Privacy Officer; Legal; Integrity
informed: All NDIA workers; line managers
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Submit a written exception via the NDIA ICT exception register stating business need, duration, residual risk and compensating controls; obtain risk assessment and approval before deviating; review at least annually.
exceptionAuthority: CIO or delegate
verification: AUP acknowledgement at onboarding and annual refresh; sample review of activity logs; investigation outcomes.
evidence: Signed acknowledgements; training records; log-on banner screenshots; misuse investigation reports.
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: ICT-POL-001; ICT-POL-006; ICT-POL-015.
relatedProcedures: AUP acknowledgement procedure; onboarding/offboarding procedure.
reviewTriggers: New or amended legislation; PSPF or ISM update; significant cyber, privacy or conduct incident; ANAO or internal audit finding; machinery-of-government change; material change to NDIA business or technology.
notes: Foundational clause underpinning all other AUP requirements (7 source obligations).

section: Respectful, lawful and inclusive digital conduct
title: Respectful, lawful and inclusive digital conduct
obligationDescription: Prevent discrimination, bullying, harassment, abuse, hate speech, victimisation, adverse action and offensive conduct through NDIA digital channels.
requirement: Users must not use NDIA ICT, email, messaging, meetings, collaboration tools or social media to discriminate, bully, harass, threaten, intimidate, humiliate, abuse, victimise, sexually harass, coerce, or publish hateful, hostile or offensive material.
obligationRef:
ADA-01: Objects and unlawful discrimination provisions, including ss 3, 14-18.
APS-VCE-03: APS Values and Code of Conduct guidance; Public Service Act ss 10 and 13.
APS-VCE-05: Public Service Act 1999 s 13(3); APS Employment Principles and Code guidance.
AHRC-01: AHRC Act functions relating to human rights, equal opportunity in employment and unlawful discrimination.
CCA-02: Criminal Code, Part 10.6 telecommunications offences, including carriage service offences.
DDA-01: Disability Discrimination Act 1992, ss 5-6, 15, 24 and 29.
DDA-03: DDA harassment and discrimination provisions.
FWA-01: Fair Work Act workplace protections, anti-bullying and sexual harassment provisions.
FWA-02: Fair Work Act general protections and workplace rights provisions.
OSA-01: Online Safety Act schemes for cyber-bullying, cyber-abuse and intimate image material.
PSA-03: Public Service Act 1999 s 13(3).
RDA-01: Racial Discrimination Act 1975, including s 9 and related unlawful discrimination provisions.
RDA-02: Racial Discrimination Act 1975, racial hatred provisions including Part IIA and s 18C.
SDA-01: Sex Discrimination Act 1984 discrimination provisions, including ss 5-7 and related provisions.
SDA-02: Sex Discrimination Act 1984 sexual harassment, harassment and hostile workplace provisions, including ss 28A and 28AA.
SDA-03: Sex Discrimination Act 1984 victimisation provisions.
ismControls: Nil — anti-discrimination, work health and APS conduct law.
otherStandards: Nil
controlObjective: Prevent discrimination, bullying, harassment, abuse, hate speech, victimisation and other unlawful conduct through NDIA digital channels.
threat: Unlawful discrimination, sexual harassment, cyber-abuse, hostile workplace; civil penalties; AHRC/Fair Work complaints; reputational harm.
applicability: All NDIA workers — APS employees, executives, contractors, consultants, secondees, labour-hire and authorised third parties — when using NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks, applications, data and information.
excluded: External participants, providers and members of the public using NDIA public-facing services in their own capacity; personal devices or accounts outside NDIA work (except under approved BYOD/remote-work arrangements where this requirement still applies to NDIA data accessed).
guidance: Apply respectful-behaviour expectations across email, IM, meetings, collaboration tools, intranet and social media. Embed examples in training. Integrate with the SDA positive duty.
technicalControls: Content filtering on email and collaboration platforms; reporting tools for harmful content; eDiscovery and preservation.
processSteps: Train annually; provide clear reporting channels (manager, People, integrity hotline); investigate under APS Code and WHS; apply sanctions and report unlawful content to authorities where required.
responsible: People Branch; Integrity & Conduct; managers
consulted: Legal; Privacy Officer; CISO; CIO; WHS
informed: All NDIA workers
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: No exceptions — obligation is set by statute or mandatory framework.
exceptionAuthority: Not applicable
verification: Investigation outcomes; training completion; complaint register and trends; AHRC/Fair Work matter outcomes.
evidence: Training records; complaint register; investigation files; remedial-action records; positive duty assessments.
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: Workplace Behaviour Policy; APS Code of Conduct Policy; WHS Policy; Social Media Policy; ICT-POL-015.
relatedProcedures: Misconduct investigation procedure; harassment & bullying complaint procedure; positive duty procedure.
reviewTriggers: New or amended legislation; PSPF or ISM update; significant cyber, privacy or conduct incident; ANAO or internal audit finding; machinery-of-government change; material change to NDIA business or technology.
notes: Highest source count (16) — aggregates ADA/AHRC/CCA/DDA/FWA/OSA/PSA/RDA/SDA.

section: Accessible and inclusive digital content and communications
title: Accessible and inclusive digital content
obligationDescription: Ensure NDIA digital services, content and communications are accessible, understandable and inclusive for participants, workers and the public.
requirement: Users must create, publish and send NDIA digital information in accessible, inclusive and respectful formats. Where a person needs a different communication mode, users must provide an approved accessible alternative or reasonable adjustment.
obligationRef:

obligationDescription: Prevent unapproved tools, applications, scripts, cloud services, prohibited applications and technology supplier or asset risks.
requirement: Users must use only approved NDIA technology, applications, scripts, suppliers and cloud services, cooperate with asset stocktakes and vulnerability management, and must not install or use prohibited or unapproved applications, including TikTok on government devices, unless an approved exception exists.
obligationRef:
E8-01: Essential Eight Maturity Model - application control.
DIR-001: PSPF Direction 001-2024 - Managing FOCI Risks in Technology Assets.
DIR-002: PSPF Direction 002-2024 - Technology Asset Stocktake.
PSPF - 91: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 92: 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
ismControls: ISM software and supply-chain guidelines.
otherStandards: Nil
controlObjective: Prevent unapproved tools, applications, scripts, cloud services, prohibited applications and technology supplier or asset risks.
threat: Shadow IT and unmanaged cloud; supply-chain compromise; foreign ownership/control/influence (FOCI) exposure; prohibited applications on government devices.
applicability: All NDIA workers — APS employees, executives, contractors, consultants, secondees, labour-hire and authorised third parties — when using NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks, applications, data and information.
excluded: External participants, providers and members of the public using NDIA public-facing services in their own capacity; personal devices or accounts outside NDIA work (except under approved BYOD/remote-work arrangements where this requirement still applies to NDIA data accessed).
guidance: Maintain approved-application list; enforce application control; block TikTok on government devices (CSO/CISO exception); manage FOCI in procurement; conduct technology asset stocktakes.
technicalControls: Application control (allow-listing); SaaS discovery/CASB; technology asset inventory; software request workflow.
processSteps: Submit software/SaaS requests for approval; cooperate with asset stocktakes; remove unauthorised apps; apply CSO/CISO exception process for TikTok where business need exists.
responsible: ICT Operations; CISO team; Procurement
consulted: Legal; Privacy Officer; system owners
informed: All NDIA workers
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Submit a written exception via the NDIA ICT exception register stating business need, duration, residual risk and compensating controls; obtain risk assessment and approval before deviating; review at least annually.
exceptionAuthority: CSO or CISO (for prohibited-application exceptions)
verification: Application-control coverage; stocktake completeness; FOCI risk reviews; exception register reviews.
evidence: Approved-app list; allow-list logs; technology asset stocktake; FOCI assessments; exception register.
auditFrequency: Quarterly
relatedPolicies: To be populated once all policies in NDIA ICT Policy Framework have been drafted.
relatedProcedures: Software request procedure; asset stocktake procedure; FOCI assessment procedure.
reviewTriggers: New or amended legislation; PSPF or ISM update; significant cyber, privacy or conduct incident; ANAO or internal audit finding; machinery-of-government change; material change to NDIA business or technology.
notes: 5 source obligations. TikTok prohibition is explicit per PSPF Direction.

section: Devices, media, remote work and approved communication channels
title: Devices, removable media, remote work and approved channels

requirement: Users must protect NDIA devices, removable media, equipment and remote access sessions, use approved channels for meetings, messaging and collaboration, and must not discuss, display or transmit security classified information through unauthorised locations, tools or devices.
obligationRef:
ISM-04: ISM guidelines for enterprise mobility, IT equipment and media.
PSPF - 70: 09. Classifications and Caveats
ismControls: ISM enterprise mobility, IT equipment and media guidelines.
otherStandards: Nil
controlObjective: Protect NDIA mobile devices, removable media, ICT equipment and remote sessions, and use approved channels for sensitive or classified discussions.
threat: Loss or theft of devices/media; eavesdropping; classified discussion via unauthorised channels; remote-session compromise.
applicability: All NDIA workers — APS employees, executives, contractors, consultants, secondees, labour-hire and authorised third parties — when using NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks, applications, data and information.
excluded: External participants, providers and members of the public using NDIA public-facing services in their own capacity; personal devices or accounts outside NDIA work (except under approved BYOD/remote-work arrangements where this requirement still applies to NDIA data accessed).

consulted: Privacy Officer; Property/Facilities; HR

verification: Device encryption coverage; MDM compliance; lost-device reports; remote-access monitoring.
evidence: MDM reports; device register; media disposal records; remote-access logs; loss/theft incident reports.

relatedProcedures: Mobile device procedure; removable media procedure; remote work procedure.

title: Email, internet, web, macros and data transfer

requirement: Users must use NDIA email, internet, web, collaboration, document and data transfer services safely and only through approved channels. Users must not bypass email/web filtering, macro controls, document hardening or data transfer restrictions, and NDIA may block or quarantine unsafe or non-work-related content.

otherStandards: Nil

threat: Phishing, malware, data exfiltration; macro-based attacks; bypass of filtering/blocking controls; uncontrolled data transfer.

verification: Filtering effectiveness; macro-policy compliance; phishing simulation results; data-transfer exception reviews.

section: Security controls, hardening, patching, backups and directions
title: Security controls, hardening, patching, backups and directions
obligationDescription: Protect system hardening, patching, monitoring, logging, backups, approved repositories and compliance with protective security directions.
requirement: Users must not disable, weaken, avoid or interfere with NDIA security controls, system hardening, monitoring, logging, patching, backups or recovery processes. Users must store official information in approved repositories and comply with protective security directions.

E8-02: Essential Eight Maturity Model - patch applications and patch operating systems.
E8-05: Essential Eight Maturity Model - regular backups.
ISM-05: ISM guidelines for system hardening, system monitoring and system management.
DIR-004: Protective Security Directions under the PSPF.
PGPA-03: PGPA Act duties of accountable authorities, including ss 15-16.
ismControls: ISM system hardening, monitoring and management guidelines.
otherStandards: Nil
controlObjective: Protect system hardening, patching, monitoring, logging, backups, approved repositories and compliance with protective security directions.
threat: Disabled or weakened controls; unpatched vulnerabilities; failed backups; loss of monitoring/logging; non-compliance with PSPF Directions.
applicability: All NDIA workers — APS employees, executives, contractors, consultants, secondees, labour-hire and authorised third parties — when using NDIA ICT, devices, accounts, networks, applications, data and information.
excluded: External participants, providers and members of the public using NDIA public-facing services in their own capacity; personal devices or accounts outside NDIA work (except under approved BYOD/remote-work arrangements where this requirement still applies to NDIA data accessed).
guidance: Prohibit disabling/weakening of security controls; maintain hardening baselines; patch within ISM timeframes; verify backups; store official information only in approved repositories.
technicalControls: Endpoint protection; vulnerability/patch management; SIEM; backup/recovery; configuration management.
processSteps: Monitor configuration drift; remediate non-compliance; test backups; report PSPF Direction compliance; investigate attempts to bypass controls.
responsible: SOC; ICT Operations; backup team; system owners
consulted: CIO; Internal Audit; Privacy Officer
informed: All NDIA workers
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Submit a written exception via the NDIA ICT exception register stating business need, duration, residual risk and compensating controls; obtain risk assessment and approval before deviating; review at least annually.
exceptionAuthority: CISO
verification: Hardening compliance scans; patching SLAs; backup restore tests; PSPF Direction self-assessment.
evidence: Vulnerability scan reports; patch reports; backup test results; PSPF self-assessment.
auditFrequency: Continuous
relatedPolicies: To be populated once all policies in NDIA ICT Policy Framework have been drafted.
relatedProcedures: Hardening procedure; patching procedure; backup procedure; configuration management procedure.

title: Unauthorised access, system impairment and illegal content
obligationDescription: Prohibit unauthorised access, modification, system impairment, malware and illegal or harmful online content using NDIA ICT.
requirement: Users must not attempt unauthorised access, alter or impair systems, data or communications, introduce malicious code, or access, create, store or share unlawful, child abuse, violent, intimate images or other harmful material using NDIA ICT.
obligationRef:
CCA-01: Criminal Code, Part 10.7 computer offences, including Divisions 477 and 478.
CCA-03: Criminal Code offences relating to child abuse material, abhorrent violent material, intimate images and other unlawful content.
OSA-02: Online Safety Act online content scheme and related harmful content provisions.
ismControls: Aligns with ISM cyber security event and incident response guidelines.
otherStandards: Nil
controlObjective: Prohibit unauthorised access, modification, system impairment, malware and illegal or harmful online content using NDIA ICT.
threat: Criminal offences; reputational and legal exposure; harm to victims of illegal content; system compromise.

excluded: External participants, providers and members of the public using NDIA public-facing services in their own capacity; personal devices or accounts outside NDIA work (except under approved BYOD/remote-work arrangements where this requirement still applies to NDIA data accessed).

section: Monitoring, logging, surveillance and communications privacy
title: Monitoring, logging, surveillance and communications privacy
obligationDescription: Define lawful monitoring, logging, filtering, computer surveillance, communications privacy and privileged access controls.

WPA-ACT-02: Workplace Privacy Act 2011 (ACT) data surveillance and workplace surveillance requirements.
WPA-ACT-03: Workplace Privacy Act 2011 (ACT) covert surveillance restrictions.
WSA-NSW-01: Workplace Surveillance Act 2005 (NSW) Part 2, including ss 10 and 12.
WSA-NSW-02: Workplace Surveillance Act 2005 (NSW) computer surveillance provisions.
WSA-NSW-03: Workplace Surveillance Act 2005 (NSW) covert surveillance provisions.

otherStandards: Nil

otherStandards: Nil

title: Regulatory, complaint and investigation cooperation
obligationDescription: Preserve evidence and route regulator contact, complaints, takedown matters and external requests through authorised NDIA channels.

title: Consequences of breach and enforcement
obligationDescription: Identify potential consequences for breaches of acceptable use, privacy, security and conduct obligations.

excluded: External participants, providers and members of the public using NDIA public-facing services in their own capacity; personal devices or accounts outside NDIA work (except under approved BYOD/remote-work arrangements where this requirement still applies to NDIA data accessed).
guidance: Set out that breaches may result in access restriction, investigation, APS Code action, sanctions, civil penalties, regulatory reporting or referral to law enforcement; apply procedural fairness.

exceptionsPermitted: No

relatedProcedures: APS Code investigation procedure; breach response procedure; civil-penalty referral procedure.

notes: 2 source obligations. Closes the policy with enforcement clarity.

title: Governance, roles and accountability
obligationDescription: NDIA must operate ICT A&A under approved governance that supports NDIA's statutory functions, assigns accountable roles and delegations to the Accountable Authority, CISO, Authorising Officers and system owners, and escalates material ICT security risks through approved audit, risk, Board and ministerial reporting channels where required.
requirement: NDIA must have clear governance for ICT authorisation and accreditation. Each system must have named accountable roles, and serious ICT security risks must be escalated through approved governance channels.

PSPF - 11 (PSPF 2025): 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities

threat: Unclear accountability, poor security decisions, unmanaged residual risk and weak executive oversight.

excluded: None for NDIA ICT systems within the A&A process.
guidance: Maintain an A&A governance model that defines delegations, decision rights, escalation paths and reporting obligations.
technicalControls: A&A register, approval workflow, document repository, audit logging for approvals and access controls for A&A artefacts.
processSteps: Assign accountable roles; confirm delegations; record decisions; escalate material risks; report through approved governance forums.

responsible: Authorising Officers; System Owners; Cyber Security Governance team.
consulted: Enterprise Risk; Legal; Privacy; Internal Audit; Business Owners.
informed: Executive governance committees; Audit and Risk Committee; affected business areas.
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional

title: ISM-aligned A&A lifecycle and authorisation decision
obligationDescription: No NDIA ICT system may process, store or communicate government information in production until the Authorising Officer has used an ISM-aligned A&A lifecycle, considered residual security risk and granted an Authority to Operate; all authorisation decisions must be recorded in the authorised systems register.
requirement: An NDIA ICT system must not go live or handle government information until an Authorising Officer has reviewed the security risk and granted an Authority to Operate. The decision must be recorded.

otherStandards: PSPF Technology Lifecycle Management; IRAP Consumer Guide.
controlObjective: Prevent systems from operating without a risk-based authorisation decision.
threat: Unauthorised operation, unmanaged control gaps, regulatory non-compliance and exposure of government information.
applicability: All new systems, major releases, cloud services, gateways, shared services and production environments.
excluded: None for systems processing, storing or communicating NDIA or government information.
guidance: Use the ISM-aligned A&A lifecycle from system definition through control selection, implementation, assessment, authorisation and monitoring.
technicalControls: Release gates, environment access controls, deployment approvals, ATO register controls and production change controls.
processSteps: Complete A&A artefacts; assess controls; document residual risk; obtain AO decision; record ATO conditions before go-live.

consulted: CISO; IRAP Assessor where applicable; Privacy; Legal; Enterprise Architecture.

relatedProcedures: ICT A&A Procedure; ATO decision template; release gate checklist; authorised systems register procedure.

section: 3. Risk management and residual risk acceptance
title: Risk appetite, ownership and internal control
obligationDescription: Each system must have an SRMP and named risk owner or steward that assesses residual, shared and legacy-technology risks against NDIA's risk appetite, tolerance and internal control requirements, with approved treatments or compensating controls for risks outside tolerance.
requirement: Each system must have a security risk management plan and a named risk owner. Risks must be assessed against NDIA's risk appetite and treated, controlled or formally accepted before operation.
obligationRef:

otherStandards: PSPF Security Risk Management; PGPA Act; Commonwealth Risk Management Policy.
controlObjective: Ensure residual, shared and legacy-technology risks are understood, owned and kept within NDIA tolerance.
threat: Risk ownership gaps, legacy risk accumulation, inappropriate risk acceptance and weak internal controls.
applicability: All systems and services subject to A&A, including inherited services and legacy technologies.
excluded: None for in-scope systems; out-of-scope services must be documented in the SRMP.
guidance: Prepare and maintain an SRMP that records risks, ratings, controls, treatments, risk owner decisions and acceptance conditions.
technicalControls: Risk register tooling, POA&M tracking, control monitoring dashboards and evidence repositories.
processSteps: Identify risks; rate against risk appetite; assign owner; document treatment; approve residual risk; track actions to closure.
responsible: System Owner; Security Risk Adviser; Project Manager; Technology Owner.
consulted: Enterprise Risk; CISO; Privacy; Legal; Supplier Manager where applicable.
informed: Authorising Officer; governance forums; operational support teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Document the risk acceptance decision, compensating controls, expiry date and monitoring requirements in the SRMP.
exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer within delegation; Accountable Authority for risks outside tolerance or material enterprise risk.
verification: SRMP quality review and sample testing of risk acceptance records and treatment actions.
evidence: SRMP; risk register entries; control treatment plans; risk acceptance approvals; POA&M updates.
auditFrequency: Quarterly
relatedPolicies: NDIA Enterprise Risk Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Internal Control Framework.
relatedProcedures: Security risk assessment procedure; SRMP template; POA&M procedure; risk acceptance guide.
reviewTriggers: Risk rating change, new threat intelligence, major incident, supplier change, control failure or audit finding.
notes: Supports risk-informed ATO decisions.

title: System definition, boundary, classification and criticality
obligationDescription: Before assessment, the system owner must define the system boundary, architecture, data flows, hosting, integrations, inherited services, records and datasets, information classification, sensitivity, business criticality, aggregation risk and applicable legal, regulatory and privacy obligations in the SSP and SRMP.
requirement: Before assessment starts, the system owner must describe what the system is, where its boundary sits, what information it handles, how it connects to other services and which legal, privacy and classification requirements apply.

title: Baseline security controls and access safeguards
obligationDescription: Systems must implement the approved control baseline before authorisation, including ISM controls, Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, protective DNS or equivalent controls, approved cryptography, access control, unique identity, MFA, restricted administration and tested backups; any gap requires approved compensating controls, remediation and residual risk acceptance.
requirement: Systems must meet the approved security control baseline before they are authorised. Any control gaps must have approved compensating controls, a remediation plan and explicit acceptance of residual risk.

applicability: All production systems and supporting environments, including cloud, SaaS, infrastructure, applications and gateways.

informed: Business Owner; service desk; operational support teams.

exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer with CISO endorsement; Accountable Authority for critical untreated risk.
verification: Control assessment, configuration review, vulnerability scan, backup test and evidence sampling.

section: 6. Information handling, privacy and lawful disclosure
title: Privacy, protected information and lawful use or disclosure
obligationDescription: Systems handling personal information or protected Agency information must apply privacy by design, reasonable security safeguards, role-based access, logging, monitoring and data-loss controls, and allow collection, use, disclosure, sharing, outsourcing, retention and destruction only for authorised purposes.
requirement: Systems that handle personal or protected Agency information must protect that information from the start. Collection, access, use, sharing, retention and disposal must be lawful, authorised and limited to approved purposes.

title: Security testing, vulnerability management and remediation
obligationDescription: Systems must complete risk-based security testing before production and after significant change, operate vulnerability disclosure and triage processes, and track findings, deficiencies and IRAP recommendations in a POA&M until closed, treated or explicitly risk accepted.
requirement: Systems must be security tested before production and after major changes. Vulnerabilities and assessment findings must be tracked until fixed, treated or formally accepted.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 110 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
PSPF - 115 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs

IRAP-08 (IRAP): PSPF Req 0110 - Use of IRAP findings
ismControls: ISM Control 1163 - continuous monitoring plan and penetration testing; ISM Control 1564 - plan of action and milestones.
otherStandards: PSPF Cyber Security Programs; IRAP finding treatment requirements.
controlObjective: Find, prioritise and remediate weaknesses before they become operational security incidents.
threat: Exploitable vulnerabilities, unremediated IRAP findings, insecure changes and unmanaged technical debt.
applicability: All production systems, externally exposed services, major releases, infrastructure changes and high-risk integrations.
excluded: Low-risk changes may use proportionate testing when approved and documented.
guidance: Use risk-based test planning and track all findings in a POA&M until closure, treatment or formal acceptance.
technicalControls: Vulnerability scanning, penetration testing where appropriate, secure code review, dependency scanning, ticketing and POA&M tracking.
processSteps: Plan testing; complete scans or tests; triage findings; assign owners; remediate or accept risk; retest and close findings.
responsible: Security Testing Lead; Vulnerability Management team; Development team; Operations team.
consulted: CISO; Authorising Officer; Supplier; Change Manager; IRAP Assessor where applicable.
informed: SOC; Business Owner; service support teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Testing deferral or unresolved findings must be documented in the POA&M with risk rating, compensating controls and expiry date.
exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer with CISO endorsement for high or critical findings.
verification: Review test reports, vulnerability scan results, POA&M status and retest evidence.
evidence: Penetration test report; scan results; vulnerability triage records; POA&M; remediation tickets; risk acceptance approvals.
auditFrequency: Monthly
relatedPolicies: Vulnerability Management Policy; Change Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy.
relatedProcedures: Security testing procedure; vulnerability triage process; POA&M procedure; change security checklist.
reviewTriggers: Major release, internet exposure, high-severity vulnerability, incident, IRAP finding or significant architecture change.
notes: Testing effort should be proportionate to system risk and exposure.

title: Continuous monitoring, review and reauthorisation
obligationDescription: System owners must continuously monitor authorised systems, review A&A artefacts at least annually, maintain provider assurance, use threat intelligence, and trigger reassessment when architecture, functionality, suppliers, threats, controls or the operating environment materially change.
requirement: Authorised systems must keep being monitored after go-live. A&A artefacts must be reviewed at least each year and reassessed when significant changes or new risks arise.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 90 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 215 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
ISM RMF-08 (ISM RMF): ISM RMF Step 6 - Monitor the system
ISM RMF-12 (ISM RMF): ISM Control 0888 - Annual documentation review
ASD Cloud-08 (ASD Cloud SRM): ASD Cloud SRM - Continuous assurance of provider responsibilities
ismControls: ISM RMF Step 6 - monitor the system; ISM Control 0888 - annual cyber security documentation review.
otherStandards: PSPF Technology Lifecycle Management; PSPF Cyber Security Programs; ASD Cloud Shared Responsibility Model.
controlObjective: Maintain assurance that authorised systems remain secure and fit for operation.
threat: Control drift, stale ATOs, unmanaged supplier changes, emerging threats and expired assurance evidence.
applicability: All authorised systems, inherited services, cloud services and supporting control environments.
excluded: None for authorised production systems.
guidance: Create a continuous monitoring plan with control owners, monitoring metrics, review schedule and reassessment triggers.
technicalControls: SIEM alerts, vulnerability monitoring, control health dashboards, configuration monitoring, supplier assurance feeds and audit logs.
processSteps: Monitor controls; review artefacts annually; assess changes; update SRMP and POA&M; reauthorise where triggers are met.
responsible: Operations team; SOC; Security Assurance; Supplier Manager; Control Owners.
consulted: CISO; Authorising Officer; Enterprise Architecture; Privacy where relevant.
informed: Business Owner; governance forums; service management.
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Any missed monitoring or review must be recorded with reason, risk, compensating controls and catch-up date.
exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer with CISO endorsement for material monitoring gaps.
verification: Review continuous monitoring records, annual review evidence, change records and ATO condition status.
evidence: Continuous monitoring plan; annual review record; updated SSP/SRMP; POA&M; control dashboards; change assessments.
auditFrequency: Continuous
relatedPolicies: Cyber Security Monitoring Policy; Change Management Policy; Supplier Risk Policy.
relatedProcedures: Continuous monitoring procedure; ATO renewal guide; security artefact review checklist.
reviewTriggers: Major change, new threat, supplier change, control failure, critical vulnerability, incident or ATO expiry.
notes: A&A is a lifecycle activity, not a one-off approval.

title: Supplier, procurement and contract security
obligationDescription: ICT procurements, contracts and supplier arrangements must include proportionate security, privacy, incident, compliance, assurance, subcontractor, foreign ownership/control/influence, transition and termination obligations, and supplier risks must be monitored and reassessed throughout the contract lifecycle.
requirement: Security, privacy and assurance requirements must be built into ICT procurement, contracts and supplier management. Supplier risks must be monitored for the life of the arrangement.

PSPF - 39 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
PSPF - 40 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management

PSPF - 46 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
PSPF - 47 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
PSPF - 48 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
PGPA-22 (PGPA): PGPA Act s 18 - Requirements imposed on others

otherStandards: PSPF Third Party Risk Management; PGPA requirements imposed on others.
controlObjective: Ensure suppliers protect NDIA information and services to the level required by the A&A decision.
threat: Supplier control gaps, weak contract obligations, unmanaged subcontractors, foreign ownership or control risk and poor exit arrangements.
applicability: All ICT procurements, contracts, supplier-managed services, outsourced operations, subcontractors and material supplier changes.
excluded: Low-risk purchases may use proportionate controls, but minimum security and privacy obligations still apply.
guidance: Include security, privacy, incident, audit, assurance, subcontracting, transition and termination obligations in procurement and contracts.
technicalControls: Supplier access controls, logging, integration controls, secure data transfer, incident notification channels and contract compliance reporting.
processSteps: Assess supplier risk; include security requirements in procurement; evaluate responses; contract obligations; monitor performance; review exit risks.
responsible: Supplier Manager; System Owner; Procurement team; Contract Manager.
consulted: CISO; Legal; Privacy; Enterprise Risk; Finance; Business Owner.
informed: Authorising Officer; operations teams; governance forums.
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Document supplier security deviation, risk, compensating controls, contract treatment and review date in the SRMP or supplier risk register.
exceptionAuthority: Procurement Delegate with CISO and Legal endorsement; Authorising Officer for ATO impact.
verification: Procurement and contract review, supplier assurance review and sample testing of contract security obligations.
evidence: Supplier risk assessment; security schedule; contract clauses; assurance reports; subcontractor approvals; transition and exit plan.
auditFrequency: Quarterly
relatedPolicies: Procurement Policy; Supplier Risk Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Privacy Policy.
relatedProcedures: ICT procurement security checklist; supplier risk assessment procedure; contract security schedule template.
reviewTriggers: New supplier, contract variation, subcontractor change, incident, ownership change, service transition or exit.
notes: A&A evidence should include supplier obligations that NDIA relies on.

requirement: Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and shared services must only be authorised when NDIA understands the shared responsibilities, provider assurance, data location, residual risks and required mitigations.

otherStandards: PSPF Cyber Security Programs; PSPF Third Party Risk Management; IRAP; Hosting Certification Framework; ASD Cloud Shared Responsibility Model.
controlObjective: Ensure cloud and shared services are authorised with clear responsibilities and acceptable provider risk.

applicability: Cloud, SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, data centres, gateways, Secure Service Edge services, shared platforms and provider-managed environments.

technicalControls: Shared responsibility control mapping, encryption, identity federation, logging, network security, gateway controls, backup and provider assurance monitoring.

responsible: Cloud Platform Owner; Security Architect; Supplier Manager; Operations team.
consulted: CISO; Legal; Privacy; Procurement; Enterprise Architecture; IRAP Assessor where applicable.
informed: Authorising Officer; Business Owner; SOC; service management.
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Provider assurance gaps must be documented with compensating controls, business justification, risk acceptance and expiry date.
exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer with CISO and Procurement/Legal endorsement; Accountable Authority for material provider risk.
verification: Review cloud assurance pack, shared responsibility matrix, IRAP/HCF evidence, gateway controls and residual provider risk.
evidence: Shared responsibility matrix; IRAP report; HCF certification or procurement evidence; cloud security architecture; data residency assessment; SRMP.
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: Cloud Security Policy; Supplier Risk Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Data Governance Policy.
relatedProcedures: Cloud A&A checklist; shared responsibility mapping guide; IRAP evidence review procedure; hosting procurement guide.
reviewTriggers: Provider change, IRAP expiry, service region change, shared responsibility change, new gateway or material incident.
notes: NDIA remains responsible for risk acceptance even when services are outsourced.

title: Incident response, breach notification and operational readiness
obligationDescription: ATO packages must include incident response and operational readiness arrangements that support timely detection, escalation, investigation, containment, remediation, supplier incident directions, eligible data breach notification and escalation of suspicious or unauthorised disclosure requests.
requirement: ATO packages must show that incident response and operational readiness are in place. Incidents, data breaches and unauthorised disclosure risks must be detected, escalated, contained and reported through approved channels.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 42 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
ISM RMF-07 (ISM RMF): ISM RMF Step 5 - Authorise the system
NDB-01: Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme - Eligible data breach notification
NDIS-17 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act s 63 - Offence: soliciting disclosure
ismControls: ISM RMF Step 5 - authorise the system; relevant ISM incident response, logging, monitoring and operational readiness controls.
otherStandards: PSPF Third Party Risk Management; Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme; NDIS Act protected information provisions.
controlObjective: Ensure systems can operate safely and respond effectively to security, privacy and disclosure incidents.
threat: Delayed incident response, missed breach notification, supplier response gaps and uncontrolled protected information disclosure.
applicability: All systems seeking ATO, including supplier-operated services and systems handling personal or protected Agency information.
excluded: None for production ATO packages.
guidance: Confirm incident roles, escalation paths, logging, supplier notification obligations and breach assessment processes before ATO.
technicalControls: Security monitoring, alerting, logging, incident ticketing, evidence preservation, breach workflow and supplier notification channels.
processSteps: Confirm readiness; test escalation; document incident playbooks; include supplier obligations; verify breach assessment and notification paths.
responsible: SOC; System Owner; Operations team; Supplier Manager; Privacy team.
consulted: Legal; Communications; Business Owner; Authorising Officer; Records Manager.
informed: Executive crisis management; affected business areas; governance forums.
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: ATO cannot be granted until minimum incident response and operational readiness arrangements are in place.
exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer may withhold ATO; CISO owns cyber incident readiness requirements.
verification: Operational readiness review, incident response evidence review and tabletop or walkthrough where warranted.
evidence: Incident response plan; logging design; escalation matrix; supplier incident clauses; breach assessment procedure; exercise record.
auditFrequency: Quarterly
relatedPolicies: Cyber Security Incident Response Policy; Privacy Policy; Supplier Risk Policy.
relatedProcedures: Incident response playbook; eligible data breach procedure; operational readiness checklist; supplier incident procedure.
reviewTriggers: Incident, data breach, supplier incident, new monitoring source, system go-live or major operational change.
notes: Operational readiness should be proven before production use.

title: Physical security and facility accreditation dependencies
obligationDescription: A&A must verify that physical facilities, security zones, racks, SCIFs and outsourced hosting locations relied on by a system are certified, accredited and protected commensurate with classification, aggregation, business impact and TOP SECRET or remote-access requirements before operational use.
requirement: A&A must confirm that facilities and physical locations used by a system provide protection that matches the information classification, aggregation risk and business impact of the system.
obligationRef:

PSPF - 95 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 96 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 137 (PSPF 2025): 17. Access to Resources

PSPF - 198 (PSPF 2025): 24. Security Zones
PSPF - 199 (PSPF 2025): 24. Security Zones

PSPF - 201 (PSPF 2025): 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
ismControls: Relevant ISM physical, media, environmental and facility dependency controls selected in the SSP and SRMP.
otherStandards: PSPF Technology Lifecycle Management; PSPF Access to Resources; PSPF Security Zones; PSPF Physical Security Measures and Controls.
controlObjective: Ensure physical facilities and hosting locations do not undermine system security.
threat: Unauthorised physical access, insecure hosting, unsuitable zones, equipment compromise and classification mismatch.
applicability: Facilities, security zones, data centres, racks, communications rooms, secure rooms and outsourced hosting locations used by in-scope systems.
excluded: Purely logical services with no NDIA-managed or supplier-specific physical dependency still require provider assurance evidence.
guidance: Confirm the physical protection level, certification or accreditation status of all facilities relied on by the system.
technicalControls: Physical access controls, visitor controls, CCTV or monitoring where required, rack security, environmental controls and secure remote access controls.
processSteps: Identify physical dependencies; confirm zone or facility status; check access controls; document gaps; include dependencies in ATO decision.
responsible: Facilities Security; Data Centre Owner; System Owner; Supplier Manager.
consulted: CISO; Protective Security; Enterprise Architecture; Authorising Officer; Supplier.
informed: Operations team; Business Owner; service management.
exceptionsPermitted: Conditional
exceptionProcess: Physical dependency gaps must be recorded with risk, interim safeguards, remediation plan and expiry date.
exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer with Protective Security and CISO endorsement.
verification: Review facility certification, zone approval, access records and provider physical security evidence.
evidence: Facility accreditation or certification; security zone records; access control evidence; provider assurance; physical security risk assessment.
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: Protective Security Policy; Physical Security Policy; Cyber Security Policy.
relatedProcedures: Physical security dependency checklist; facility accreditation procedure; data centre assurance guide.
reviewTriggers: Facility change, hosting move, classification change, physical security incident or provider assurance change.
notes: Physical assurance is a dependency of ICT authorisation.

title: Records, metadata, retention and secure disposal
obligationDescription: Systems must identify and preserve required records, datasets, logs, metadata, security labels and access-rights information, and must retain, transfer, alter, de-identify, sanitise or dispose of information and assets only through authorised records, privacy, Archives Act and ISM processes.
requirement: Systems must keep required records, logs, metadata, labels and access-rights information. Information and assets must only be changed, retained, transferred, de-identified, sanitised or disposed of through approved processes.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 68 (PSPF 2025): 09. Classifications and Caveats
PSPF - 69 (PSPF 2025): 09. Classifications and Caveats

ARC-09 (Archives Act): NAA guidance - Metadata and supporting documentation
ARC-10 (Archives Act): Archives Act s 24 / NAA guidance - Disposal only under approved authority

otherStandards: PSPF Classifications and Caveats; PSPF Technology Lifecycle Management; Archives Act and National Archives guidance.
controlObjective: Ensure official information remains reliable, findable, protected and lawfully retained or disposed of.
threat: Loss of records, unlawful disposal, missing metadata, poor auditability, excessive retention and insecure sanitisation.
applicability: Systems that create, receive, store, alter, transmit, archive, de-identify, sanitise or dispose of NDIA business information.
excluded: None for systems that hold official information; temporary technical logs must still be assessed for retention and security needs.
guidance: Map records, metadata, logs and disposal events to records authorities, privacy requirements and secure disposal controls.
technicalControls: Records capture, metadata, retention rules, audit logging, access control, legal hold, secure deletion or sanitisation and disposal evidence.
processSteps: Identify records; apply metadata and labels; set retention; protect logs; approve disposal; preserve evidence of records events.
responsible: System Owner; Data Owner; Application Owner; Operations team.
consulted: Privacy; Legal; CISO; Business Owner; National Archives liaison where relevant.
informed: Authorising Officer; business users; service management.
exceptionsPermitted: No
exceptionProcess: Records and disposal obligations cannot be waived. Any uncertainty must be escalated to Records, Legal and Privacy before action.
exceptionAuthority: Records Manager and Legal; Authorising Officer may withhold or condition ATO.
verification: Records and disposal design review, retention configuration review and sample testing of metadata and disposal records.
evidence: Records assessment; metadata schema; retention schedule; disposal authority; legal hold process; sanitisation or disposal certificates.
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: Records Management Policy; Information Management Policy; Privacy Policy; Cyber Security Policy.
relatedProcedures: Records-in-systems checklist; metadata standard; retention and disposal procedure; secure sanitisation procedure.
reviewTriggers: New dataset, retention change, system decommissioning, legal hold, audit finding or disposal event.
notes: Supports accountability, FOI, audit and lawful information disposal.

obligationDescription: If CDR obligations apply, the system must define the CDR data environment, implement mandatory CDR security controls, assess NDIA and outsourced controls, retain required logs, complete internal and conformance testing before activation, report deficiencies and incidents, and maintain ongoing CDR conformance.
requirement: Where Consumer Data Right obligations apply, the system must meet the CDR security, testing, logging, incident and conformance requirements before activation and throughout operation.

excluded: Systems confirmed as outside CDR scope, with rationale documented in the SSP or obligation assessment.

processSteps: Assess CDR applicability; define environment; implement mandatory controls; test internally; complete conformance steps; monitor ongoing compliance.

informed: Authorising Officer; Business Owner; operations and incident response teams.

evidence: CDR applicability assessment; CDR data environment definition; control matrix; logs retention evidence; test results; conformance evidence; incident process.

relatedProcedures: CDR applicability checklist; CDR conformance procedure; API security testing procedure; outsourced control assessment guide.
reviewTriggers: CDR scope change, API change, outsourced control change, conformance failure, CDR incident or regulatory update.
notes: Conditional requirement: mandatory only where the CDR regime applies.

section: 16. Conditional SOCI, SOGS and critical infrastructure obligations
title: Conditional SOCI, SOGS and critical infrastructure obligations
obligationDescription: If SOCI, SOGS or critical infrastructure obligations apply, the ATO package and SRMP must confirm applicability, critical asset status, data service provider notifications, protected-information handling, risk management program alignment, register or ownership reporting, enhanced cyber obligations, mandatory cyber reporting and government assistance escalation.
requirement: Where SOCI, SOGS or other critical infrastructure obligations apply, the ATO package must show that those obligations are understood, assigned, implemented, reported and escalated as required.

applicability: Only systems, data services, assets and suppliers that meet SOCI, SOGS or other critical infrastructure applicability criteria.

responsible: System Owner; CISO; Legal; Enterprise Risk; Supplier Manager.

title: Governance, accountability, risk and investment oversight
obligationDescription: NDIA must govern Agency and Scheme Applications through accountable owners, CISO oversight, documented risk appetite, approved lifecycle and investment decisions, and retained evidence that risks, exceptions, control reviews and approval gates are escalated and accepted by authorised roles.
requirement: NDIA must assign clear business and ICT owners for every Agency and Scheme Application. Owners must make sure risks, funding, approvals, exceptions and control reviews are documented, escalated when needed, and accepted by the right delegated role before the application is used or changed.

excluded: None. Applicability may be tailored only where an application is formally out of scope and the exclusion is recorded.
guidance: Maintain an application owner, ICT owner, risk profile, control baseline, investment approvals and decision records in the application register. Use governance forums for material risks and exceptions.
technicalControls: Application inventory; risk register; workflow approvals; evidence repository; access to governance records; audit logging of approval changes.

responsible: Business Application Owner; ICT Application Owner; Portfolio/Investment Manager; Security Risk Manager.
consulted: CISO; CFO/Finance; Enterprise Architecture; Legal; Procurement; Privacy Officer.
informed: Executive governance forums; affected business areas; Internal Audit as required.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - limited
exceptionProcess: Record the reason, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and owner in the risk/exception register before relying on the exception.
exceptionAuthority: CIO or delegate, with CISO approval for security risk and business owner acceptance for residual risk.
verification: Register review; governance minutes review; sample approval and exception records.
evidence: Application register; risk assessments; investment approvals; control review reports; exception records; governance decisions.
auditFrequency: Quarterly
relatedPolicies: Enterprise Risk Management Policy; ICT Governance Policy; Investment Governance Policy; Cyber Security Policy.
relatedProcedures: Application onboarding; risk assessment; ICT investment approval; exception management procedure.

section: 2. Lawful Scheme operation and decision integrity

requirement: Agency and Scheme Applications must only support NDIS processes, business rules and decisions that have been approved and are lawful. When an application supports a participant decision, it must show the delegation used, record the evidence and reasons, provide required notices and review information, and keep a human accountable for the decision.

evidence: Approved business rules; requirements traceability; delegation register; test results; decision logs; notice templates; review pathway evidence.

reviewTriggers: Legislative or NDIS Rules change; delegation change; ART or court decision; participant harm issue; audit finding; material release.
notes: Plain English policy statement is intended to support lawful and reviewable Scheme decisions.

Legacy applications must have an agreed uplift, replacement or retirement plan.
