title: Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
obligationDescription: Access to applications and information must be approved, unique, least-privilege, MFA-protected, monitored, reviewed and removed when no longer needed; classified or caveated information must require need-to-know, clearance and approved sharing arrangements; Digital ID use must meet assurance, privacy, accreditation and accessible fallback requirements.
requirement: Only people and systems with an approved need may access Agency and Scheme Applications. Access must use unique accounts, least privilege and multi-factor authentication where required; privileged access must be tightly controlled, monitored and reviewed; access must be removed promptly when roles change or people leave. Classified sharing and Digital ID must meet required assurance, privacy, consent and accessibility controls.

obligationDescription: Applications must implement ISM and Essential Eight aligned controls, secure architecture, patching, application control, hardening, protected logging, tested backups, required cryptography, vulnerability disclosure, and incident and continuity procedures that are tested, monitored and reportable within required timeframes.
requirement: Agency and Scheme Applications must be built and operated with security controls that match their risk. This includes secure design, Essential Eight and ISM-aligned controls, timely patching, hardening, logging, monitoring, backups, encryption, vulnerability management, incident response and business continuity testing.

Contracts must require the controls, evidence, incident notification, NDIA data ownership, access rules, subcontractor obligations, monitoring, transition and exit support needed to protect NDIA and participants.

requirement: Agency and Scheme Applications must protect personal information, NDIS protected information, TFNs and shared data from the start. They must collect only what is needed, explain how information is used, restrict access, keep information accurate, dispose of it safely, complete privacy impact assessments where required, report eligible breaches, and only share or disclose data under an approved authority or agreement.

TFN-03 (TFN Rule): TFN Rule - security safeguards
TFN-04 (TFN Rule): TFN Rule - destruction or de-identification
DAT-01 (DATA Scheme): Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022
DAT-02 (DATA Scheme): DATA Scheme - data sharing principles
DAT-03 (DATA Scheme): DATA Scheme Code
DAT-04 (DATA Scheme): DATA Act - privacy, secrecy and integrity safeguards
DAT-05 (DATA Scheme): DATA Scheme - output controls
ismControls: ISM privacy-supporting security controls: access control, encryption, logging, masking, secure disposal, data loss prevention and monitoring.
otherStandards: Privacy Act and APPs; Notifiable Data Breaches Scheme; Australian Government Privacy Code; TFN Rule; DATA Scheme; NDIS Protection and Disclosure Rules; PGPA cooperation obligation.
controlObjective: Protect personal, participant, protected, TFN and shared data and ensure use and disclosure are lawful, minimal and transparent.
threat: Privacy breach, unauthorised disclosure, over-collection, misuse of protected or TFN data, unsafe data sharing and re-identification.
applicability: All applications that collect, store, process, share, disclose, analyse, mask, de-identify or dispose of personal, protected, TFN or data scheme information.
excluded: Applications with no personal, protected or shared data, confirmed by privacy screening.
guidance: Screen every application for privacy impact. Apply privacy-by-design controls, data minimisation, notices, PIA/threshold assessments, approved sharing agreements and breach response.
technicalControls: Data classification; access controls; masking; encryption; audit logging; data quality controls; secure transfer; disposal; breach detection; DLP; de-identification controls.
processSteps: Complete privacy screen or PIA; approve data flows; configure access and masking; validate notices; monitor data quality; report breaches; review sharing agreements.
responsible: Business Owner; ICT Application Owner; Data Steward; Privacy Team; Cyber Security.
consulted: Legal; Records; CISO; Data Sharing Authority; Scheme Policy.
informed: Affected business teams; data users; governance forums; OAIC/participants where required by breach process.
exceptionsPermitted: No - for legal/privacy obligations; Yes - only for technical implementation with approved risk controls
exceptionProcess: Privacy obligations cannot be waived. Any temporary control gap must be recorded with risk, compensating controls, expiry and privacy endorsement.
exceptionAuthority: Senior Privacy Official, with CISO and Business Owner acceptance where security or operational risk is involved.
verification: Privacy assessment or PIA review; data flow review; access/log sample; breach readiness test; data sharing agreement review.
evidence: Privacy threshold or PIA; collection notices; data inventory; data sharing agreements; access records; masking/DLP evidence; breach registers; training records.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for high-risk applications; annual for others
relatedPolicies: Privacy Policy; Data Governance Policy; Information Sharing Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Records Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: Privacy impact assessment; data sharing assessment; breach response; data minimisation; secure disposal; TFN handling procedure.
reviewTriggers: Privacy Act, APP, TFN, DATA Scheme or NDIS disclosure rule change; new data sharing; breach; high-risk release; audit finding.
notes: Requirement is framed for privacy by design and safe sharing of protected participant information.

title: Fraud prevention, detection, investigation and reporting
obligationDescription: Applications must have proportionate controls to prevent, detect, investigate and report suspected fraud or corruption, including approved fraud risk assessment for high-risk changes, identity, entitlement, validation, segregation of duties and approval controls, monitoring analytics, protected audit evidence and alignment with NDIA's fraud and corruption control plan.
requirement: Agency and Scheme Applications must include controls that help prevent, find, investigate and report suspected fraud and corruption. For high-risk changes, NDIA must complete a fraud risk assessment and use identity, entitlement, validation, segregation of duties, approval, monitoring and protected audit evidence controls that match the risk.
obligationRef:
FRAUD-01 (Fraud and Corruption): Fraud and Corruption Rule 2024
FRAUD-02 (Fraud and Corruption): Fraud and Corruption Policy 2024 - fraud risk assessments
FRAUD-03 (Fraud and Corruption): Fraud and Corruption Policy 2024 - prevention controls
FRAUD-04 (Fraud and Corruption): Fraud and Corruption Policy 2024 - detection, data analytics and monitoring
FRAUD-05 (Fraud and Corruption): Fraud and Corruption Policy 2024 - response and investigation
FRAUD-06 (Fraud and Corruption): NDIA Fraud and Corruption Control Plan
ismControls: Access control, segregation of duties, logging, monitoring, data analytics and evidence protection controls supporting fraud detection and investigation.
otherStandards: Fraud and Corruption Rule 2024; Fraud and Corruption Policy 2024; NDIA Fraud and Corruption Control Plan.
controlObjective: Reduce fraud and corruption opportunities and preserve evidence for investigation and reporting.
threat: Fraudulent claims or payments, insider misuse, false identities or entitlements, collusion, manipulation of records and loss of evidence.
applicability: Applications that support payments, claims, provider or participant records, identity, eligibility, entitlement, case management, compliance or investigations.
excluded: Low-risk applications with no financial, entitlement, identity or compliance impact, if fraud screening confirms.
guidance: Assess fraud risk at design and major change; build preventative and detective controls; protect logs and evidence; align with the fraud control plan and investigation needs.
technicalControls: Segregation of duties; workflow approvals; identity verification; rule validations; anomaly detection; immutable audit logs; case flags; monitoring dashboards; secure evidence storage.
processSteps: Complete fraud risk assessment; design controls; test scenarios; monitor analytics; escalate suspicious events; preserve evidence; support investigation and reporting.
accountable: Chief Risk Officer or Fraud Control Executive
responsible: Fraud Control Team; Business Owner; ICT Application Owner; Data Analytics; Cyber Security Operations.
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Internal Audit; Scheme Integrity; Finance; Security.
informed: CIO; business executives; relevant operational teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - strictly limited
exceptionProcess: Document residual fraud risk, compensating controls and monitoring. High residual risk must be accepted before release.
exceptionAuthority: Fraud Control Executive or Chief Risk Officer, with Business Owner and CISO endorsement where system controls are affected.
verification: Fraud control design review; test case review; analytics/alert review; audit log sampling; investigation evidence review.
evidence: Fraud risk assessment; control matrix; test results; monitoring reports; alert triage records; audit logs; investigation handover records.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for high-risk functions; annual control review
relatedPolicies: Fraud and Corruption Control Plan; Risk Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Data Governance Policy.
relatedProcedures: Fraud risk assessment; control testing; monitoring/analytics; incident escalation; evidence preservation procedure.
reviewTriggers: New fraud typology; payment or entitlement change; investigation finding; high-risk release; fraud control plan update; audit finding.
notes: Requirement should be applied early in design for any payment, entitlement or identity-related feature.

section: 11. Accessibility, digital experience and service quality
title: Inclusive design, accessible content, user research, performance and alternatives
obligationDescription: Applications must be designed, tested and operated so people with disability and other users can complete required tasks through accessible, inclusive, plain-language, reliable and measurable services, with user research, release-level accessibility evidence, current content, performance monitoring, reasonable adjustments and assisted or non-digital alternatives where required.
requirement: Agency and Scheme Applications must be designed and run so people with disability and other users can complete required tasks. Services must use plain language, accessible content and inclusive design, be tested with users, meet agreed performance and reliability levels, and provide reasonable adjustments or assisted/non-digital alternatives where needed.
obligationRef:
DDA-05 (DDA / Accessibility): Disability Discrimination Act 1992
DDA-06 (DDA / Accessibility): Digital Experience Policy - accessibility criterion
DDA-07 (DDA / Accessibility): Style Manual - accessible and inclusive content
DDA-08 (DDA / Accessibility): Human Rights Commission web access advisory notes
DDA-09 (DDA / Accessibility): DDA - reasonable adjustments and alternatives
DIG-01 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Policy
DIG-02 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Standard - user needs and journeys
DIG-03 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Standard - accessibility and inclusion
DIG-04 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Standard - performance and reliability
DIG-05 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Standard - content and transparency
ismControls: Availability, change management, logging and incident management controls that support reliable digital services; not primarily an ISM control requirement.
otherStandards: Disability Discrimination Act; Digital Experience Policy and Standard; Australian Government Style Manual; Human Rights Commission guidance.
controlObjective: Provide inclusive, reliable and accessible services that do not disadvantage users.
threat: Exclusion of people with disability, poor usability, failure to complete tasks, complaints, legal breach and service unreliability.
applicability: Public-facing, participant, provider, staff and partner applications, including digital forms, content, notifications and assisted channels.
excluded: Internal technical tools may tailor user research and accessibility evidence, but must still meet workplace accessibility obligations.
guidance: Design for accessibility from discovery through release. Use plain English, WCAG-aligned testing, user research, performance monitoring and alternative service paths.
technicalControls: Accessible UI components; semantic content; keyboard and screen reader support; captions and transcripts; performance monitoring; uptime alerts; analytics; content version control.
processSteps: Identify user needs; design and test accessible journeys; remediate defects before release; publish plain language content; monitor performance; maintain assisted alternatives.
accountable: Chief Digital Officer or Service Design Executive
responsible: Product Owner; UX/Service Design; Content Design; ICT Application Owner; Quality Assurance; Release Manager.
consulted: Accessibility SME; Disability Community/User Research; Legal; Privacy; Communications; Service Delivery.
informed: Service channels; contact centre; operational teams; users where appropriate.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only temporary
exceptionProcess: Accessibility defects must be risk assessed, prioritised, documented with an accessible workaround and remediated by an approved date.
exceptionAuthority: Service Design Executive/Product Executive with Accessibility SME endorsement; Legal consulted for high-risk accessibility exceptions.
verification: Accessibility test; user research evidence; content review; performance/reliability reporting; complaints and reasonable adjustment review.
evidence: Accessibility conformance report; test results; user research findings; content approvals; performance dashboards; release accessibility sign-offs; workaround instructions.
auditFrequency: Per release; annual service review
relatedPolicies: Digital Service Standard Policy; Accessibility Policy; Content Governance Policy; Service Delivery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Inclusive design; accessibility testing; content review; user research; reasonable adjustment; release acceptance procedure.
reviewTriggers: Digital Experience Standard change; accessibility defect; user complaint; new channel; major release; service performance issue.
notes: Plain English and inclusive design are core policy expectations for Agency and Scheme Applications.

title: AI governance, impact assessment, transparency, monitoring and safe use
obligationDescription: AI-enabled or automated functionality must be approved, risk and impact assessed, documented, transparent and accountable to named owners, must record logic, inputs and human oversight where decisions are supported, must be monitored for accuracy, bias, security, privacy, drift and harmful outputs, and must use official information only with approved AI tools.
requirement: Any AI or automated function in an Agency or Scheme Application must be approved before use and must have a named owner. NDIA must assess its risks and impacts, explain when AI is used, record the logic, inputs and human oversight for decision support, monitor accuracy, bias, privacy, security, drift and harmful outputs, and only use official information with approved AI tools.
obligationRef:
RAI-01 (Responsible AI): Policy for responsible use of AI in government
RAI-02 (Responsible AI): AI accountability requirements
RAI-03 (Responsible AI): AI use case impact assessment
RAI-04 (Responsible AI): AI transparency statements
RAI-05 (Responsible AI): AI preparedness and operations
RAI-06 (Responsible AI): Generative AI and official information
FOI-09 (FOI Act): OAIC guidance on automated decision-making and FOI reporting
ismControls: ISM controls for secure development, access control, logging, data protection, monitoring and supply-chain risk as applied to AI systems.
otherStandards: Policy for responsible use of AI in government; AI accountability requirements; AI impact assessment; AI transparency statements; AI preparedness and operations; OAIC FOI guidance on automated decision-making.
controlObjective: Ensure AI is accountable, transparent, safe, secure, fair and monitored throughout its lifecycle.
threat: Unapproved AI use, biased or inaccurate outputs, opaque automated decisions, privacy or security breach, harmful content and loss of human accountability.
applicability: All AI, machine learning, generative AI, automated decision support, rules-driven automation with material impacts and third-party AI features.
excluded: Low-risk automation with no personal or protected data, no decision impact and no AI model, if recorded as not in scope.
guidance: Maintain an AI use case register; complete impact assessment; assign an owner; approve data and tool use; implement human oversight, transparency, monitoring and retirement controls.
technicalControls: AI use case inventory; access controls; prompt and data controls; model and version logs; output monitoring; bias and accuracy testing; audit trails; content filters; secure approved AI platforms.
processSteps: Submit use case; assess impact; approve owner, tool and data; document model and logic; test risks; publish transparency information; monitor; review incidents; retire unsafe use.
accountable: AI Accountable Official / Chief Digital Officer
responsible: AI Product Owner; Business Owner; ICT Application Owner; Data Science/Analytics; Cyber Security; Privacy Team.
consulted: Legal; Privacy; CISO; Data Governance; Scheme Policy; Accessibility; Records.
informed: Users; affected business areas; governance forums; participants/public where transparency statements require.
exceptionsPermitted: No - for unapproved AI use; Yes - only for controlled pilot
exceptionProcess: Unapproved AI use is not permitted. Pilots must be registered, time-bound, use approved tools and data, and have human review and monitoring.
exceptionAuthority: AI Accountable Official or delegated AI governance body, with Privacy and CISO endorsement for relevant risks.
verification: AI register review; impact assessment review; transparency statement check; monitoring reports; sample decision/output audit.
evidence: AI use case record; impact assessment; approval decision; model/logic documentation; test results; transparency statement; monitoring logs; incident records.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for high-risk AI; before release and after material model or data change
relatedPolicies: Responsible AI Policy; Data Governance Policy; Privacy Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Scheme Decision Making Policy.
relatedProcedures: AI impact assessment; AI use case approval; model monitoring; generative AI use; automated decision recordkeeping.
reviewTriggers: AI policy change; model or data change; new use case; harmful output; bias/accuracy issue; privacy or security incident; audit finding.
notes: Requirement is designed to cover both AI-enabled functions and automation that materially supports decisions.

title: Policy governance, accountability, risk tolerance and acceptable use
obligationDescription: NDIA must govern all ICT digital experience capabilities through approved investment, assurance and risk arrangements. Accountable owners must document risk tolerance, compliance obligations, exceptions and escalations, and all staff and contractors must use ICT resources properly, ethically and in support of NDIA functions.
requirement: The NDIA must clearly own and govern every digital experience capability. ICT must be used lawfully, ethically and for NDIA business, with risks, exceptions and decisions recorded.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 36 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 37 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 38 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
IOF-06 (IOF): IOF lifecycle states
IOF-07 (IOF): Assurance Framework for Digital and ICT Investments
IOF-08 (IOF): Digital Investment Plan Policy
DIG-06 (DX Policy): Digital Experience Policy - applicability to IOF investments

DIG-08 (DX Policy): DX Policy effective dates

NDIS-32 (NDIS Act): NDIA functions under the NDIS Act

PGPA-24 (PGPA): PGPA Act s16 - risk oversight, internal controls and risk management
PGPA-26 (PGPA): Government policy orders and ministerial directions

APS-EPC-06 (APS Code): APS Code - proper use of Commonwealth resources
APS-EPC-07 (APS Code): APS Code and managing information
APS-EPC-08 (APS Code): APS reputation and public communications
ismControls: ISM governance, risk management, security documentation, acceptable use and exception management controls.
otherStandards: PSPF security risk management; Investment Oversight Framework; Digital Experience Policy; NDIS Act; PGPA Act; APS Code of Conduct.
controlObjective: Ensure digital services have accountable owners, approved risk settings and clear rules for appropriate ICT use.
threat: Unowned services, unmanaged risk, misuse of Commonwealth resources, non-compliance and loss of public trust.
applicability: All NDIA digital experience capabilities, ICT resources, investments, staff, contractors and suppliers.
excluded: No blanket exclusions. Any exclusion must be approved as an exception and have compensating controls.
guidance: Assign a business owner, record risks and obligations, define acceptable use, and include governance checkpoints in investment and delivery gates.
technicalControls: Risk register, control register, approved access model, audit logging, exception register and monitoring of acceptable use.
processSteps: Assess risk; approve ownership; record obligations; communicate acceptable use; monitor compliance; review exceptions and escalations.
responsible: Digital service owners; ICT governance; risk and assurance teams; project sponsors
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Cyber Security; Procurement; Enterprise Architecture; business owners
informed: All NDIA staff, contractors, suppliers and delivery partners
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only with documented risk acceptance.
exceptionProcess: Submit an exception request with reason, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and review date.
exceptionAuthority: CIO or approved delegate, with risk owner endorsement.
verification: Governance review, risk register sampling, control assurance and internal audit.
evidence: Approved business cases, risk assessments, governance minutes, exception records, acceptable use communications and assurance reports.
auditFrequency: Annual, and at major investment, service launch or material change.
relatedPolicies: ICT Digital Experience Policy; ICT Governance Policy; Risk Management Policy; Acceptable Use Policy
relatedProcedures: Investment assurance guide; risk assessment procedure; acceptable use guidance; exception management process
reviewTriggers: Changes to PSPF, PGPA, APS Code, Digital Experience Policy, investment framework, risk appetite or audit findings.
notes: Plain-English requirement drafted from governance, risk, investment and acceptable use obligations.

title: User-centred service design, access model, connected journeys and digital transactions
obligationDescription: Digital services must have a clear purpose, defined user groups, evidence-based user needs, a documented service offering and a channel/access model. Service teams must connect related channels and partners, record access decisions, and support legally effective electronic transactions, communications, signatures and approvals with retained evidence.
requirement: The NDIA must design digital services around real user needs, make access choices clear, connect related channels, and keep evidence for valid electronic transactions.
obligationRef:
DSS-01 (Digital Service Std): Criterion 1 - Have a clear intent
DSS-02 (Digital Service Std): Criterion 2 - Know your user
DSS-04 (Digital Service Std): Criterion 4 - Connect services
DAS-01 (Digital Access): Criterion 1 - Understand how users access services
DAS-02 (Digital Access): Criterion 2 - Define your service offering
DAS-04 (Digital Access): Criterion 4 - Follow the decision-making framework
DAS-05 (Digital Access): Criterion 5 - Engage with delivery partners
AGADPS-01 (Digital Portal Std): Digital Portal Standard - align to DX Policy and Digital Access Standard

ET-07 (Electronic Transactions): Electronic writing requirements
ET-08 (Electronic Transactions): Electronic signatures, records and retention
ET-09 (Electronic Transactions): Time and place of dispatch and receipt
ismControls: ISM controls for secure design, authentication, audit logging, transaction integrity and records protection.
otherStandards: Digital Service Standard; Digital Access Standard; Digital Portal Standard; Electronic Transactions Act.
controlObjective: Make digital services purposeful, connected and legally effective.
threat: Poor take-up, inaccessible services, invalid transactions, missing evidence and fragmented user journeys.
applicability: All public, participant, provider, partner and internal digital services and transactions.
excluded: No blanket exclusions. Non-digital channels remain in scope when they support the same service journey.
guidance: Define user groups, service purpose, access model, channel choices, delivery partners and evidence needs before build and at major change.
technicalControls: User research repository, service catalogue, identity and transaction records, audit trails, electronic signature and retention controls.
processSteps: Confirm service intent; research users; map channels; choose access model; test journeys; record transaction and approval evidence.
responsible: Product owners; UX researchers; service designers; ICT delivery teams; records officers
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Cyber Security; Accessibility; delivery partners; business owners
informed: Participants, providers, staff and delivery partners affected by the service
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - where access model decisions are documented and approved.
exceptionProcess: Record the decision, reason, user impact, alternate channel, risk, expiry date and review owner.
exceptionAuthority: Digital Service Owner or approved delegate.
verification: Service standard assessment, user research review, journey testing and transaction evidence sampling.
evidence: Service blueprint, user research findings, access model, journey maps, delivery partner records and transaction evidence.
auditFrequency: At service design gates, at launch and annually.
relatedPolicies: ICT Digital Experience Policy; Service Design Policy; Records Management Policy; Privacy Policy
relatedProcedures: Digital service design playbook; user research guide; electronic transactions procedure; access model decision guide
reviewTriggers: Changes to Digital Service Standard, Digital Access Standard, transaction law, user needs, channels or service performance.
notes: Plain-English requirement drafted from service design, digital access and electronic transaction obligations.

title: Inclusion, accessibility, multilingual access and channel choice
obligationDescription: NDIA digital services, content, identity proofing and workplace technologies must be inclusive and accessible. They must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA where applicable, use plain and culturally appropriate communication, support language services and reasonable adjustments, and provide assisted or non-digital options where users need them.
requirement: The NDIA must make digital services, content and workplace technology accessible and inclusive. People must have language support, reasonable adjustments and assisted or non-digital options when needed.
obligationRef:
DSS-03 (Digital Service Std): Criterion 3 - Leave no one behind

DIS-02 (Digital Inclusion): Criterion 2 - Motivate digital use
DIS-04 (Digital Inclusion): Criterion 4 - Make it accessible
DIS-05 (Digital Inclusion): Criterion 5 - Provide flexibility and choice

DDA-12 (DDA Accessibility): AHRC guidelines on equal access to digital goods and services
DDA-13 (DDA Accessibility): DDA - employment-related access and adjustments
WCAG-01 (WCAG 2.2): WCAG 2.2 Level AA
WCAG-02 (WCAG 2.2): WCAG principles - perceivable, operable, understandable and robust

MAE-04 (MAE Language Access): Contractors and service providers

otherStandards: Digital Service Standard; Digital Inclusion Standard; WCAG 2.2 AA; Disability Discrimination Act; MAE Policy; Digital ID Act.
controlObjective: Make sure people can use NDIA digital services regardless of disability, language, culture, digital skills or access needs.
threat: Exclusion, discrimination, poor service outcomes, legal breach and loss of trust.
applicability: All public and internal websites, portals, forms, apps, documents, identity processes, content and workplace technologies.
excluded: No exclusion for disability, language or low digital access. Temporary issues must provide an equivalent path.
guidance: Apply WCAG 2.2 AA, inclusive research, plain language, language services, accessibility testing and reasonable adjustment planning.
technicalControls: Accessible patterns, assistive technology support, captions, transcripts, keyboard navigation, accessible identity proofing and defect tracking.
processSteps: Identify access needs; test with diverse users; fix defects; publish accessibility information; provide assisted or alternative channels.
responsible: Service designers; content designers; accessibility specialists; ICT delivery; assisted-channel teams
consulted: People with disability or user representatives; Legal; Privacy; Multicultural and accessibility teams; Cyber Security
informed: Participants, nominees, providers, staff, contractors and support channels
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only as a time-bound accessibility exception with equivalent access.
exceptionProcess: Record barrier, impact, alternative access, remediation plan, owner, due date and review date.
exceptionAuthority: Digital Service Owner with accessibility and legal or risk endorsement.
verification: Accessibility assessment, WCAG testing, user testing and remediation tracking.
evidence: WCAG reports, accessibility statements, usability test results, adjustment plans, defect logs and alternative-channel procedures.
auditFrequency: At each release and at least annually.
relatedPolicies: ICT Digital Experience Policy; Accessibility Policy; Diversity and Inclusion Policy; Reasonable Adjustment Policy
relatedProcedures: WCAG testing procedure; content style guide; language services guide; assisted digital procedure
reviewTriggers: Changes to WCAG, DDA guidance, Digital Inclusion Standard, MAE policy, user feedback, complaints or service design.
notes: Plain-English requirement drafted from accessibility, digital inclusion, language access and reasonable adjustment obligations.

title: Content quality, official identity, proactive publication and rights management
obligationDescription: NDIA public and internal digital content must be clear, consistent, trustworthy, discoverable and correctly branded. Publishing teams must meet web content, publication, FOI/IPS, annual reporting, copyright, licensing and third-party content obligations before release or reuse.
requirement: The NDIA must publish digital content that is clear, accurate, current and officially branded. Content must be approved before release and reused only when rights are clear.
obligationRef:
DSS-05 (Digital Service Std): Criterion 5 - Build trust in design
AGASM-01 (AGA Style): Style Manual - clear, useful and consistent content
AGASM-02 (AGA Style): Plain English and user-centred writing
AGASM-03 (AGA Style): Consistent official content in collaboration tools

AGBG-03 (Branding Guidelines): Official document and publication branding

COPY-05 (Copyright): Government copyright and public sector information licensing
COPY-06 (Copyright): Third-party and supplier content
ismControls: ISM controls for web content security, publishing approvals, change control, access control and protection of official information.

technicalControls: Content management permissions, version control, approval workflow, metadata, link checking and secure publishing controls.

informed: Participants, providers, staff and external users

evidence: Approval records, content inventories, review dates, style and brand checks, rights clearance and FOI/IPS publication records.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for high-use public content; annually for other content.
relatedPolicies: ICT Digital Experience Policy; Communications Policy; FOI and Information Publication Policy; Copyright Policy
relatedProcedures: Content design guide; publishing workflow; brand guide; copyright clearance procedure
reviewTriggers: Changes to content standards, branding rules, FOI/IPS, copyright rules, service changes, complaints or analytics.
notes: Plain-English requirement drafted from content quality, official identity, proactive publication and rights obligations.

title: Privacy, personal information, protected Agency information and identity privacy
obligationDescription: NDIA must manage personal information, protected Agency information and identity data using privacy-by-design. Digital services must minimise collection, give clear notices, use or disclose information only as authorised, secure information, support access and correction, manage overseas processing, complete PIAs where required and maintain privacy governance, training and registers.
requirement: The NDIA must protect personal, identity and protected Agency information by design. Collect only what is needed, explain why, use or share it lawfully, secure it, and support access and correction.

PA-20 (Privacy APPs): APP 3 and APP 5 - collection and notification
PA-21 (Privacy APPs): APP 6 - use or disclosure
PA-22 (Privacy APPs): APP 11 - security of personal information
PA-23 (Privacy APPs): APP 12 and APP 13 - access and correction
PA-24 (Privacy APPs): APP 8 - cross-border disclosure

PC-08 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - published PIA register
PC-09 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - privacy capability and training
DID-08 (Digital ID): Digital ID Act - privacy safeguards
ismControls: ISM controls for information security, access control, encryption, logging, data loss prevention, secure disposal and privacy-impact mitigation.
otherStandards: NDIS Act protected Agency information; Privacy Act APPs; Privacy Code; Digital ID privacy safeguards.
controlObjective: Protect personal information and keep NDIA use of data lawful, fair and transparent.
threat: Privacy breach, unauthorised disclosure, identity harm, regulatory action and loss of participant trust.
applicability: All digital services, data stores, integrations, identity services, collaboration tools and suppliers handling personal or protected information.
excluded: No exclusion where personal, identity or protected Agency information is handled.
guidance: Apply privacy-by-design, data minimisation, privacy notices, PIAs for high-risk projects, cross-border checks and privacy training.
technicalControls: Role-based access, MFA, encryption, logging, DLP, secure APIs, consent or notice controls, retention and disposal controls.
