DPS-05 (Digital Performance): Criterion 5 - Analyse and report performance
ismControls: ISM controls for monitoring, logging, service continuity, incident detection, availability management and performance reporting.
otherStandards: Digital Service Standard; Digital Performance Standard.
controlObjective: Keep digital services reliable, relevant and improving over time.
threat: Poor availability, slow performance, unmet user needs, service failure, low adoption and missed improvement opportunities.
applicability: All live public, participant, provider, partner and internal digital services and channels.
excluded: Small internal tools may use proportionate measures, but still need ownership and issue tracking.
guidance: Define service measures, baselines, availability targets, dashboards, feedback loops and an improvement backlog before go-live.
technicalControls: Service monitoring, analytics, uptime checks, logs, dashboards, alerting, feedback tools and performance test results.
processSteps: Set measures; monitor service; analyse results; report; prioritise improvements; update roadmap and user support information.
responsible: Service management; product owners; ICT operations; data and analytics; user support teams
consulted: Users or representatives; Accessibility; Cyber Security; Privacy; Communications; business owner
informed: Users, support teams, executives and delivery partners
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only where proportionality is justified and approved.
exceptionProcess: Record measure not used, reason, risk, alternate evidence, approval, review date and improvement plan.
exceptionAuthority: Digital Service Owner or service management delegate.
verification: Performance dashboard review, SLA review, user feedback analysis, service review and audit sampling.
evidence: Monitoring dashboards, analytics reports, availability records, user feedback, improvement backlog, service review minutes and release notes.
auditFrequency: Quarterly service review and annual assurance.
relatedPolicies: ICT Digital Experience Policy; Service Management Policy; Business Continuity Policy
relatedProcedures: Service monitoring framework; digital performance measurement guide; feedback management procedure; continuous improvement process
reviewTriggers: Changes to Digital Performance Standard, service measures, user needs, service incidents, complaints or continuous improvement findings.
notes: Plain-English requirement drafted from performance, availability, monitoring and continuous improvement obligations.

title: Harm prevention, vulnerability disclosure, incidents and breach response
obligationDescription: Digital services must be designed and operated to avoid harm and protect users. NDIA must maintain vulnerability disclosure, incident and breach response processes, require supplier incident reporting, assess suspected eligible data breaches, contain and remediate harm, and notify affected people or regulators where required.
requirement: The NDIA must design and run digital services so they do not harm users. Security incidents, vulnerabilities and suspected data breaches must be reported, assessed and fixed quickly.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 42 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
DSS-07 (Digital Service Std): Criterion 7 - Do no harm
DIS-03 (Digital Inclusion): Criterion 3 - Protect users
PSPF - 115 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
NDB-03 (NDB Scheme): Privacy Act Part IIIC - eligible data breaches
NDB-04 (NDB Scheme): Assessment of suspected eligible data breaches
NDB-05 (NDB Scheme): Remediation and harm reduction
ismControls: ISM controls for vulnerability management, incident detection and response, logging, supplier incident reporting, containment, backup and recovery.
otherStandards: PSPF third party risk and cyber security programs; Digital Service Standard; Digital Inclusion Standard; Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
controlObjective: Prevent harm, respond quickly to incidents and protect affected people.
threat: User harm, exploitation of vulnerabilities, delayed breach response, regulatory breach, data loss and service disruption.
applicability: All digital services, suppliers, collaboration tools, data stores, security vulnerabilities, incidents and suspected eligible data breaches.
excluded: No exclusion for incidents or suspected breaches. All must be reported through approved channels.
guidance: Use threat modelling, safe design checks, vulnerability disclosure, incident playbooks, breach assessment and supplier reporting obligations.
technicalControls: Security monitoring, vulnerability intake, incident ticketing, SIEM/EDR, alerting, containment tooling, forensic logging and breach workflow.
processSteps: Identify risk; report issue; triage; contain; assess harm and breach status; remediate; notify if required; learn from incident.
accountable: Chief Information Security Officer / Chief Privacy Officer
responsible: Cyber Security; Privacy; service owners; ICT operations; suppliers; incident management team
consulted: Legal; Communications; Records; Procurement; business owners; Agency Security Adviser
informed: Affected users, executives, regulators and support teams as required
exceptionsPermitted: No for reporting obligations. Any treatment delay requires formal risk acceptance.
exceptionProcess: Urgently escalate proposed delay or deviation with impact, legal and privacy advice, compensating controls and expiry.
exceptionAuthority: CISO for cyber incidents; Chief Privacy Officer for privacy breaches; incident executive as required.
verification: Incident exercise, breach register review, vulnerability management review, supplier incident review and audit.
evidence: Incident records, vulnerability reports, breach assessments, notifications, remediation evidence, post-incident reviews and exercise reports.
auditFrequency: After each incident, quarterly trend review and annual exercise.
relatedPolicies: ICT Digital Experience Policy; Information Security Policy; Privacy Policy; Incident Management Policy; Supplier Risk Policy
relatedProcedures: Cyber incident response plan; vulnerability disclosure procedure; data breach response plan; supplier incident reporting procedure
reviewTriggers: Changes to NDB scheme, PSPF cyber programs, threat environment, supplier risks, vulnerability trends or incident lessons learned.
owner: Incident Response and Privacy Breach SME
notes: Plain-English requirement drafted from harm prevention, vulnerability disclosure, incident and breach response obligations.

title: AI and emerging technology governance
obligationDescription: AI and emerging technologies used in NDIA digital services, collaboration tools or EUC environments must have an approved purpose, accountable owner, human oversight and documented risk assessment. Uses must be transparent where required and must meet privacy, security, accessibility, procurement and public-trust obligations before and during use.
requirement: The NDIA must use AI and emerging technology only for approved purposes with clear accountability, human oversight and documented risk controls. People must be told when transparency is required.
obligationRef:
DSS-08 (Digital Service Std): Criterion 8 - Innovate with purpose
RAI-07 (AI in Government): AI in Government Policy v2.0
RAI-08 (AI in Government): AI transparency and public trust
RAI-09 (AI in Government): AI use-case accountability
RAI-10 (AI in Government): AI-enabled applications and web services
ismControls: ISM controls for secure development, data protection, access, logging, monitoring, supplier risk, change management and security assessment of AI-enabled services.
otherStandards: Digital Service Standard; AI in Government Policy; AI transparency, accountability and public trust requirements.
controlObjective: Use AI and new technology safely, transparently and in line with public trust obligations.
threat: Unfair or unsafe decisions, privacy breach, security weakness, opaque automation, bias, procurement risk and loss of trust.
applicability: All AI-enabled applications, automated decision support, chatbots, analytics, generative AI, emerging technology pilots and supplier AI features used by NDIA.
excluded: Personal experimentation with unapproved tools is excluded from official use and must not handle NDIA information.
guidance: Define purpose, owner, human oversight, data use, transparency needs, risk controls, approvals and ongoing monitoring before use.
technicalControls: Approved AI platform, access controls, data controls, logging, prompt/output management, model monitoring, supplier controls and secure integration.
processSteps: Register use case; assess risk; approve design; test for privacy, security, accessibility and bias; publish transparency where needed; monitor outcomes.
accountable: AI Use Case Owner / Chief Information Officer
responsible: Service owners; data scientists; ICT delivery; cyber security; procurement; suppliers
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Ethics and risk; Accessibility; Communications; Records; affected business owners
informed: Users, staff, participants, providers and oversight bodies where relevant
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only through AI governance risk acceptance before use.
exceptionProcess: Submit AI exception with use case, risk assessment, transparency impact, mitigations, human oversight, expiry and monitoring plan.
exceptionAuthority: AI Governance Committee or CIO/delegate, with Privacy and Cyber endorsement for relevant risks.
verification: AI use-case register review, risk assessment review, control testing, model or service monitoring and user impact review.
evidence: Use-case approval, risk assessment, transparency notice, PIA or security assessment, test results, monitoring logs and human oversight records.
auditFrequency: At approval, every six months for high-risk AI, and after material model, data or use change.
relatedPolicies: ICT Digital Experience Policy; AI Use Policy; Data Governance Policy; Privacy Policy; Information Security Policy; Procurement Policy
relatedProcedures: AI risk assessment procedure; AI use-case register; transparency statement template; secure AI integration guide; human oversight guide
reviewTriggers: Changes to AI in Government Policy, AI technology, use case risk, model data, transparency expectations, incidents or public trust concerns.
notes: Plain-English requirement drafted from AI and emerging technology governance obligations.

title: Governance, risk appetite, ownership and oversight
obligationDescription: NDIA must manage ICT disaster recovery as an enterprise governance, risk and internal-control capability with approved authority, defined risk appetite and tolerances, named business and ICT owners, measurable risk reporting, and architecture, change and investment gates that prevent systems entering operation without appropriate recoverability.
requirement: The NDIA must govern ICT disaster recovery as an enterprise risk control. Business and ICT owners must be named, recovery risk appetite and tolerances must be approved, recovery risks must be reported, and new or changed systems must not go live unless they can be recovered to agreed targets.
obligationRef:
PGPA-33 (PGPA): PGPA Act s15 - duty to govern the Commonwealth entity
PGPA-34 (PGPA): PGPA Act s16 - duty to establish and maintain systems relating to risk and control
CRMP-01 (CRMP): CRMP - accountable authority responsibility for risk management
CRMP-02 (CRMP): CRMP - risk management capability and culture
CRMP-03 (CRMP): CRMP - risk information and reporting
PSPF - 36 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 37 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 38 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 98 (PSPF 2025): 14. Cyber Security Strategies
PSPF-STD-01 (PSPF Standards): Direction 004-2025 - Commonwealth Technology Management
PSPF-STD-02 (PSPF Standards): Commonwealth Technology Standard
AGAIOF-02 (AGA IOF): Investment Oversight Framework - digital investment assurance
ismControls: Relevant ISM governance, risk management, system security planning and recovery readiness controls as applicable.
otherStandards: PGPA Act duties; Commonwealth Risk Management Policy; PSPF Security Risk Management and Cyber Security Strategies; Commonwealth Technology Management; Commonwealth Technology Standard; Australian Government Architecture Investment Oversight Framework.
controlObjective: Make disaster recovery a governed, funded and reported enterprise risk control with clear ownership and risk tolerance.
threat: Unclear ownership, under-funded recovery capability, unapproved risk acceptance, poor reporting and systems entering production without recoverability.
applicability: All NDIA ICT services, platforms, data stores, recovery environments, projects, changes and ICT investments that support NDIA business outcomes.
excluded: None. Any limit to scope must be documented as an approved risk exception.
guidance: Assign accountable business and ICT owners, define risk appetite and tolerances, include recovery in architecture and change gates, and report recovery risk to governance forums.
technicalControls: Service ownership register; DR risk register; architecture and change gating; dependency records; recovery capability reporting dashboards.
processSteps: 1. Confirm owners and risk appetite. 2. Record DR risks and controls. 3. Include DR checks in design, change and release approvals. 4. Report status and exceptions to governance forums.
accountable: NDIA Accountable Authority delegate / Chief Information Officer
responsible: ICT DR Manager; Business Service Owners; System Owners; Enterprise Architecture; Cyber Security; Risk Management; Portfolio and Change Management.
consulted: Business Continuity; Internal Audit; Finance; Legal; Procurement; Privacy; Security Governance.
informed: Executive governance forums; Audit and Risk Committee; impacted business areas; service delivery leaders.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only through a documented and time-bound risk exception.
exceptionProcess: Submit an exception with business reason, risk assessment, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan; record it in the risk register and review it regularly.
exceptionAuthority: CIO and relevant business risk owner; Accountable Authority delegate or risk committee for high residual risk.
verification: Governance review, risk register review, architecture and change gate sampling, and internal audit.
evidence: Approved risk appetite statement, DR ownership matrix, risk register entries, governance minutes, architecture approvals, change records and exception approvals.
auditFrequency: At least annually and after major organisational, service or technology change.
relatedPolicies: Enterprise Risk Management Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Business Continuity Policy; ICT Change Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy.
relatedProcedures: DR governance procedure; risk assessment procedure; architecture review checklist; change and release gate checklist.
reviewTriggers: Major incident, audit finding, material system or service change, new or changed regulatory requirement, change in risk appetite or ownership.
owner: ICT DR Policy Owner / ICT Risk SME
notes: Defines the governance foundation for all other DRP requirements.

section: 2. Scope, critical services and recovery objectives
title: Critical services, BIA, RTO/RPO and service continuity scope
obligationDescription: NDIA must identify the services, systems, data, legacy platforms, suppliers and interdependencies that support NDIS outcomes, assess business and user impact, and set approved recovery priorities, maximum tolerable outages, recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives that align with business continuity and participant service needs.
requirement: The NDIA must identify which services, systems, data, suppliers and dependencies are critical to NDIS outcomes. Each critical service must have an approved business impact assessment, recovery priority, maximum tolerable outage, recovery time objective and recovery point objective aligned with business continuity and participant service needs.
obligationRef:
NDIS-33 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act - establishment, functions and service delivery responsibilities
PSPF - 55 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning
PSPF - 56 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning
PSPF-STD-03 (PSPF Standards): Systems of Government Significance Standard
ISM-11 (ISM): ISM Cyber Security Principles - RES-01
ISM-13 (ISM): ISM - service continuity for online services
ACSS - 01 (Cyber Strategy): Strategy - national cyber resilience and six cyber shields
DIG-09 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Policy - whole-of-government digital experience requirements
DIG-10 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Policy - mandatory standards framework
DSS-11 (Digital Service Std): Digital Service Standard - service design and delivery criteria
DIS-07 (Digital Inclusion): Digital Inclusion Standard - existing and new services
ismControls: ISM RES-01; ISM service continuity for online services; relevant backup, availability and recovery controls.
otherStandards: NDIS Act service delivery responsibilities; PSPF Contingency Planning; Systems of Government Significance Standard; Australian Cyber Security Strategy; Digital Experience Policy; Digital Service Standard; Digital Inclusion Standard.
controlObjective: Identify critical services and set clear, approved recovery targets that reflect business and participant impact.
threat: Failure to prioritise the right services, excessive outage duration, unacceptable data loss, poor participant outcomes and inconsistent recovery decisions.
applicability: All NDIA business services, ICT systems, data sets, suppliers, integrations and manual workarounds that support NDIS participant, provider or staff outcomes.
excluded: Services assessed as non-critical may have lower recovery targets, but they still require documented ownership and an approved recovery position.
guidance: Maintain a service catalogue and BIA, map dependencies, approve RTO and RPO for each critical service, and align ICT DR plans with business continuity priorities.
technicalControls: Service catalogue/CMDB; dependency mapping; BIA repository; RTO/RPO register; recovery prioritisation tooling; monitoring of service availability.
processSteps: 1. Identify services and dependencies. 2. Complete or refresh the BIA. 3. Agree MTO, RTO and RPO. 4. Approve recovery priorities. 5. Update DR plans and workarounds.
accountable: Chief Information Officer and relevant Business Service Owner
responsible: Business Continuity Manager; ICT DR Manager; Service Owners; System Owners; Data Owners; Supplier Managers.
consulted: Participant service areas; Cyber Security; Privacy; Enterprise Architecture; Risk; Accessibility; Communications.
informed: Executive governance forums; impacted business areas; support teams; key suppliers.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only through an approved risk exception where business impact is understood.
exceptionProcess: Document the proposed deviation from approved recovery targets, business impact, participant impact, compensating controls and remediation date.
exceptionAuthority: Business Service Owner and CIO; Accountable Authority delegate for critical services or high residual risk.
verification: BIA review, service catalogue review, DR plan review and recovery target testing.
evidence: Approved BIA, service criticality ratings, dependency maps, RTO/RPO register, DR plans, business continuity plans and approval records.
auditFrequency: At least annually and after material service, process, supplier or technology change.
relatedPolicies: Business Continuity Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Service Management Policy; Digital Service Standard alignment guidance.
relatedProcedures: BIA procedure; service criticality assessment; dependency mapping procedure; RTO/RPO approval process; continuity workaround procedure.
reviewTriggers: New or changed critical service, major incident, supplier change, system replacement, BIA refresh, audit finding or changed participant service requirement.
owner: Business Continuity Manager / ICT DR Manager
notes: Recovery targets should be approved by the business, not set by ICT alone.

section: 3. Resilient architecture, cloud, hosting and dependencies
title: Architecture resilience, cloud/hosting assurance and physical dependencies
obligationDescription: NDIA must design and operate production, backup, replication and recovery environments using resilient architecture, approved network and access controls, current asset and dependency records, certified or otherwise approved cloud, hosting and data-centre services, documented data locations, and physical protections proportionate to business impact and information sensitivity.
requirement: The NDIA must design and operate production and recovery environments so critical services can continue or be restored. Recovery architecture must use approved cloud, hosting, network and access controls, current asset and dependency records, known data locations and appropriate physical protection.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 211 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 96 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 109 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
PSPF - 111 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
PSPF - 112 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
PSPF - 217 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
PSPF - 200 (PSPF 2025): 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
PSPF - 201 (PSPF 2025): 25. Physical Security Measures and Controls
PSPF-STD-04 (PSPF Standards): Gateway Security Standard
SOCI-10 (SOCI): SOCI Act - critical infrastructure risk management and incident notification
SOCI-11 (SOCI): SOCI - data storage and processing sector
HCF-19 (HCF): HCF - certified hosting for high-value and protected government data
HCF-20 (HCF): HCF - Australian data storage expectations
WGCP-05 (Cloud Policy): Cloud Policy - uniform framework for cloud adoption
WGCP-06 (Cloud Policy): Cloud Policy Requirement 1 - prioritise cloud when modernising IT infrastructure
WGCP-07 (Cloud Policy): Cloud Policy - security, compliance and capability uplift
AGAIOF-01 (AGA IOF): Australian Government Architecture - architecture guardrails
ismControls: Relevant ISM architecture, cloud, gateway, network security, access control, logging, backup and recovery controls as applicable.
otherStandards: PSPF Technology Lifecycle Management, Cyber Security Programs and Physical Security Measures; Gateway Security Standard; SOCI obligations; Hosting Certification Framework; Whole-of-Government Cloud Policy; Australian Government Architecture guardrails.
controlObjective: Ensure the technology design, hosting model and physical dependencies can support agreed recovery targets and data protection needs.
threat: Single points of failure, insecure or uncertified hosting, unavailable recovery environments, dependency failures, unmanaged data locations and physical disruption.
applicability: Production, backup, replication, test and recovery environments; cloud and hosting services; data centres; networks; gateways; integrations; privileged access paths; physical dependencies.
excluded: Non-production environments are excluded only where they do not process production data or support recovery activities; exclusions must be documented.
guidance: Design for resilience, separate recovery from production where needed, use approved hosting and cloud services, record data locations, and keep architecture and dependency records current.
technicalControls: Resilient network and hosting design; backup and replication platforms; privileged access controls; monitoring; logging; CMDB; data location register; physical security controls.
processSteps: 1. Define resilience patterns. 2. Validate hosting and cloud approvals. 3. Map dependencies and data locations. 4. Review physical and network dependencies. 5. Test failover and recovery paths.
responsible: Enterprise Architect; Infrastructure and Cloud Services; Network Services; System Owners; ICT DR Manager; Cyber Security; Facilities or physical security teams.
consulted: Business Service Owners; Procurement; Supplier Managers; Risk; Privacy; Data Owners.
informed: Executive governance forums; operational support teams; impacted suppliers; business service owners.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only where compensating controls maintain approved recovery and security outcomes.
exceptionProcess: Raise an architecture or hosting exception with documented business need, residual risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan.
exceptionAuthority: CIO, Chief Architect or delegated architecture governance body; risk owner for high residual risk.
verification: Architecture review, hosting assurance review, dependency validation, failover testing and supplier evidence review.
evidence: Approved architecture diagrams, data location records, hosting approvals, dependency maps, CMDB records, failover test results, supplier assurance reports and risk acceptances.
auditFrequency: At least annually and before major architecture, hosting, cloud, network or supplier change.
relatedPolicies: ICT Architecture Policy; Cloud Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Physical Security Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Architecture review procedure; cloud/hosting assurance checklist; dependency mapping procedure; failover runbooks; physical dependency checklist.
reviewTriggers: Cloud or hosting change, new critical service, major infrastructure change, SOCI relevance change, security incident, failed test or audit finding.
owner: Enterprise Architecture SME / Infrastructure and Cloud Services Lead
notes: Architecture decisions should show how agreed RTO and RPO can be met.

title: Backups, restoration, immutable recovery and transaction integrity
obligationDescription: NDIA must maintain protected and tested backups of important data, software, configurations and records, with retention aligned to approved RPO/RTO, recovery procedures that verify integrity and completeness, and additional reconciliation controls before restoring financial, claims, payment or other high-impact services.
requirement: The NDIA must keep recoverable backups of important data, software, configurations and records. Backups must be protected from unauthorised change or deletion, tested regularly, retained to meet approved recovery targets, and restored only after integrity and transaction checks are complete.
obligationRef:
PGPA-36 (PGPA): PGPA Act s41 - accounts and records
PSPF - 71 (PSPF 2025): 10. Information Holdings
PSPF - 106 (PSPF 2025): 14. Cyber Security Strategies
ISM-12 (ISM): ISM - data backup and restoration guidance
E8-29 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - regular backups
ismControls: ISM data backup and restoration guidance; Essential Eight regular backups; relevant recovery, access control, encryption and integrity controls.
otherStandards: PGPA Act accounts and records; PSPF Information Holdings and Cyber Security Strategies; Essential Eight regular backups.
controlObjective: Ensure critical data, records, software and configurations can be restored to a known good state within approved recovery targets.
threat: Permanent data loss, corrupted restoration, ransomware impact on backups, untested recovery, unreconciled payments or claims, and incomplete records.
applicability: All important NDIA data, records, software, configurations, code repositories, identity data, recovery scripts and transaction records needed to restore ICT services.
excluded: Data approved for exclusion must have documented business acceptance, legal and records review, and a clear statement that it is not needed for recovery.
guidance: Classify backup needs by service criticality, protect backups from deletion or tampering, test restoration, validate integrity, and reconcile high-impact transactions before service return.
technicalControls: Backup platform; immutable or protected backup storage; encryption; privileged access control; restoration environment; integrity checks; transaction reconciliation; backup monitoring and alerts.
processSteps: 1. Define backup scope and retention. 2. Protect backup access and storage. 3. Monitor backup success. 4. Test restore. 5. Validate integrity and reconcile transactions. 6. Record results and defects.
responsible: Backup and Recovery Service Owner; Database Administrators; System Owners; Data Owners; ICT DR Manager; Cyber Security; Records Management.
consulted: Finance; Claims or payment service owners; Privacy; Risk; Business Continuity; Internal Audit.
informed: Service owners; support teams; governance forums; key suppliers.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only through formal risk acceptance and only where legal, records and business obligations are met.
exceptionProcess: Document the data or system excluded, business impact, legal/records/privacy assessment, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan.
exceptionAuthority: CIO and relevant Data Owner; Finance or business owner for financial, claims or payment data.
verification: Backup job review, restoration test, integrity validation, reconciliation review and audit sampling.
evidence: Backup schedules, success/failure reports, retention settings, access reviews, restore test results, integrity check logs, reconciliation records and remediation actions.
auditFrequency: Backup monitoring daily; restoration testing at least annually for each critical service and after major change.
relatedPolicies: ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Backup and Restore Policy; Information Management Policy; Records Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy.
relatedProcedures: Backup procedure; restore runbook; immutable backup procedure; transaction reconciliation checklist; backup access review procedure.
reviewTriggers: Backup failure trend, ransomware event, failed restore, new critical system, data model change, retention change, audit finding or regulatory change.
owner: Backup and Recovery Service Owner / Data Protection SME
notes: Restore testing should prove that data can be used, not just that files can be copied back.

title: Baseline cyber controls for recovery readiness
obligationDescription: NDIA must protect recovery capabilities with risk-based ISM, Essential Eight and ACSC cyber controls, including patching, hardening, application control, MFA, least-privilege and monitored administrative access, protected identity recovery, and heightened post-recovery monitoring before restored services are returned to normal operation.
requirement: The NDIA must protect recovery systems with cyber controls that match the risk. Recovery environments must use Essential Eight and ISM-aligned controls, including patching, hardening, application control, MFA, least privilege, protected administrator access, identity recovery and monitoring before services return to normal use.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 84 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 85 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 107 (PSPF 2025): 14. Cyber Security Strategies
E8-30 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - patch applications and operating systems
E8-31 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - restrict administrative privileges
E8-32 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - application control and Microsoft Office/macros/hardening controls
E8-33 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - multi-factor authentication
ACSC-01 (ACSC Mitigations): ACSC Strategies - prioritised mitigation strategies
ACSC-02 (ACSC Mitigations): ACSC Strategies - detect, deny and limit cyber compromise
ismControls: Essential Eight patching, restrict administrative privileges, application control, Microsoft Office and macro hardening, MFA; ACSC prioritised mitigation strategies; relevant ISM access, hardening, logging and monitoring controls.
otherStandards: PSPF Technology Lifecycle Management and Cyber Security Strategies; Essential Eight; ACSC Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents.
controlObjective: Protect recovery capability so a cyber incident does not compromise the systems, identities and data needed to restore services.
threat: Ransomware spread to recovery systems, stolen administrator access, reinfection after restore, unpatched vulnerabilities, weak identity recovery and insufficient monitoring.
applicability: All recovery environments, backup systems, administrative tools, identity services, privileged accounts, restored services and supporting endpoints used during recovery.
excluded: None for systems that support critical recovery. Any control gap must be treated as a cyber risk exception.
guidance: Apply Essential Eight and ISM-aligned controls to recovery systems, restrict and monitor administrator access, protect identity recovery, and confirm security controls before returning services to normal use.
technicalControls: MFA; privileged access management; application control; patch management; endpoint hardening; vulnerability management; secure administration workstations; logging/SIEM; EDR; identity backup and recovery controls.
processSteps: 1. Identify recovery assets and privileged paths. 2. Apply baseline hardening and patching. 3. Enforce MFA and least privilege. 4. Monitor recovery activity. 5. Validate controls before service restoration.
responsible: Cyber Security Operations; Identity and Access Management; Infrastructure and Cloud Services; System Owners; Backup Service Owner; ICT DR Manager.
consulted: Risk; Enterprise Architecture; Service Owners; Privacy; Supplier Managers; Internal Audit.
informed: CIO; executive cyber governance forums; service owners; operational support teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only as a documented cyber risk exception with compensating controls and a remediation date.
exceptionProcess: Submit a cyber control exception that states the control gap, affected services, threat exposure, compensating controls, monitoring, expiry and remediation plan.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and CIO; risk committee or Accountable Authority delegate for high residual cyber risk.
verification: Control assessment, Essential Eight maturity review, vulnerability scan, access review, monitoring review and post-restore security validation.
evidence: Essential Eight assessment, patch reports, vulnerability reports, MFA and privileged access records, logging evidence, EDR status, security validation checklist and exception records.
auditFrequency: At least quarterly for key cyber controls and after major cyber incident or recovery test.
relatedPolicies: Cyber Security Policy; Access Control Policy; Vulnerability Management Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Backup and Restore Policy.
relatedProcedures: Cyber recovery runbook; privileged access procedure; patch and vulnerability procedure; post-restore security validation checklist; logging and monitoring procedure.
reviewTriggers: Cyber threat change, Essential Eight maturity change, major vulnerability, security incident, failed recovery test, control exception or audit finding.
notes: Recovery environments need the same or stronger security than production during a crisis.

section: 6. Incident, ransomware and breach response integration
title: DR activation, cyber recovery, ransomware response and breach notification
obligationDescription: NDIA DR procedures must integrate with security incident, cyber recovery, ransomware, crisis and privacy breach processes so that activation, containment, restoration, forensic preservation, legal and external reporting assessment, stakeholder escalation and post-incident review are coordinated and evidenced.
requirement: The NDIA must connect disaster recovery procedures with security incident, ransomware, crisis and privacy breach processes. When disaster recovery is activated, containment, restoration, evidence preservation, legal and reporting decisions, stakeholder escalation and lessons learned must be coordinated and recorded.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 26 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
PSPF - 27 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
PSPF - 28 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
ISM-14 (ISM): ISM - cyber security incident response integration
CYBACT-01 (Cyber Sec Act): Cyber Security Act 2024 - cyber incident coordination and security framework
CYBACT-02 (Cyber Sec Act): Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025
CYBACT-03 (Cyber Sec Act): Cyber Security Act - Cyber Incident Review Board
PC-12 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - privacy officer/senior official roles
NDB-06 (NDB Scheme): Privacy Act Part IIIC - Notifiable Data Breaches scheme
NDB-07 (NDB Scheme): OAIC data breach preparation and response guidance
ismControls: ISM cyber security incident response integration; relevant logging, evidence preservation, containment and recovery controls.
otherStandards: PSPF Security Planning, Incidents and Training; Cyber Security Act 2024; Cyber Security (Ransomware Payment Reporting) Rules 2025; Cyber Incident Review Board; Privacy Code; Notifiable Data Breaches scheme; OAIC data breach guidance.
controlObjective: Coordinate disaster recovery with cyber incident, crisis, ransomware and privacy breach processes so recovery decisions are lawful, timely and evidenced.
threat: Uncoordinated recovery, loss of forensic evidence, missed ransomware or breach reporting, delayed escalation, reinfection, inconsistent public messaging and unresolved lessons learned.
applicability: All ICT disruptions where disaster recovery, cyber response, ransomware response, crisis management, privacy breach assessment or external reporting may be required.
excluded: Purely local operational incidents may be handled through normal incident management unless recovery targets, sensitive data, ransomware or external reporting thresholds are affected.
guidance: Define activation criteria, escalation paths, decision roles, evidence handling, breach/ransomware assessment points and post-incident review requirements in DR runbooks.
technicalControls: Incident management platform; SIEM/log preservation; evidence vault; secure communications; forensic tooling; ransomware decision records; breach assessment workflow; recovery runbooks.
processSteps: 1. Assess DR activation. 2. Coordinate containment and recovery. 3. Preserve evidence. 4. Assess breach and ransomware reporting duties. 5. Escalate decisions. 6. Complete post-incident review.
accountable: Chief Information Security Officer and ICT DR Manager
responsible: Security Incident Response Team; ICT DR Team; Privacy Officer; Legal; Communications; Business Continuity; Service Owners; Supplier Managers.
consulted: Risk; Records Management; Procurement; Internal Audit; affected business areas; external agencies where required.
informed: CIO; executive crisis forum; affected business areas; participants/providers where approved; regulators where required.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only where the incident controller or authorised delegate approves and legal/privacy obligations are not breached.
exceptionProcess: Record the exception, reason, operational impact, legal/privacy assessment, compensating controls, approval and review date in the incident record and risk register.
exceptionAuthority: Incident Controller, CISO and CIO; Privacy Officer or Legal for breach-related decisions.
verification: Incident record review, tabletop or exercise observation, post-incident review, breach assessment review and evidence sampling.
evidence: Activation records, incident tickets, decision logs, forensic preservation records, breach assessments, ransomware reporting assessments, communications approvals, PIR reports and action trackers.
auditFrequency: After each major incident or exercise, and at least annually.
relatedPolicies: Cyber Security Incident Response Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Privacy Management Policy; Crisis Management Plan; Business Continuity Policy.
relatedProcedures: DR activation procedure; cyber incident response plan; ransomware response playbook; data breach response plan; post-incident review procedure.
reviewTriggers: Cyber incident, ransomware event, privacy breach, new reporting duty, major exercise, failed escalation, audit finding or lesson learned.
owner: CISO / ICT DR Manager / Privacy Officer
notes: This requirement links technical recovery with legal, privacy and crisis decisions.

section: 7. Privacy, protected information and lawful data handling
title: Personal information, NDIS protected information, data sharing and classification controls
obligationDescription: NDIA must protect personal information, NDIS protected information, DATA Scheme data and sensitive official information throughout DR design, backup, replication, testing, restoration, temporary workarounds, disposal and support access, using only authorised locations, users, suppliers and tools, and applying privacy review, PIA screening, retention, secure disposal and protective-marking controls where required.
requirement: The NDIA must protect personal information, NDIS protected information and other sensitive information during backups, replication, testing, recovery, temporary workarounds, disposal and support access. Data must only be handled in approved locations by authorised people, suppliers and tools.
obligationRef:
NDIS-34 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act - use and disclosure of protected information
NDIS-PDI-01 (NDIS Info Rules): NDIS Information Rules - protection and disclosure of information
PA-25 (Privacy APPs): Privacy Act - Australian Privacy Principles
PA-26 (Privacy APPs): APP 11 - security of personal information
PA-27 (Privacy APPs): APP 1 - open and transparent management of personal information
PA-28 (Privacy APPs): APP 6 and APP 8 - use/disclosure and cross-border disclosure
PA-29 (Privacy APPs): APP 11 - destruction/de-identification where no longer required
PC-10 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - privacy management plan
PC-11 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - privacy impact assessments for high privacy risk projects
DAT-10 (DAT Act): DAT Act - controlled sharing of public sector data
DAT-11 (DAT Act): DAT Act - accreditation and data sharing agreements
AGPM-02 (Protective Marking): PSPF information classification and handling
ismControls: Relevant ISM information protection, access control, encryption, logging, media handling, disposal and supplier access controls as applicable.
otherStandards: NDIS Act protected information provisions; NDIS Information Rules; Privacy Act and Australian Privacy Principles; Privacy Code; DATA Scheme; PSPF protective marking and handling requirements.
controlCategory: Privacy, protected information and lawful data handling
controlObjective: Protect sensitive and protected information during every stage of disaster recovery, including backup, replication, testing, restore, workarounds and disposal.
threat: Unauthorised disclosure, unlawful use of protected information, privacy breach, insecure testing data, unapproved offshore or supplier access, over-retention and poor disposal.
applicability: All personal information, NDIS protected information, DATA Scheme data, sensitive official information, logs, backups, extracts, test data and recovery workarounds used by NDIA or suppliers.
excluded: None for protected or personal information. Use of de-identified or synthetic data must still be approved where it supports recovery testing.
guidance: Use approved data locations, authorised users and approved tools; assess privacy risk; restrict supplier access; protect test data; apply retention, disposal and protective marking controls.
technicalControls: Access control; encryption; data loss prevention where available; approved storage; audit logging; secure test data; retention and disposal controls; protective marking; secure file transfer.
processSteps: 1. Identify sensitive data in DR scope. 2. Confirm lawful basis and approved locations. 3. Restrict access. 4. Complete PIA screening where needed. 5. Protect or de-identify test data. 6. Dispose of temporary copies securely.
accountable: Chief Privacy Officer / Privacy Officer with the CIO
responsible: Data Owners; System Owners; ICT DR Manager; Cyber Security; Records Management; Supplier Managers; Test Managers.
consulted: Legal; Risk; Business Service Owners; Information Governance; Procurement; Accessibility; Internal Audit.
informed: CIO; service owners; support teams; approved suppliers; governance forums.
exceptionsPermitted: Only where permitted by law and approved through privacy, security and risk review.
exceptionProcess: Document the requested exception, legal basis, privacy impact, affected information, compensating controls, approval, expiry and remediation plan.
exceptionAuthority: Privacy Officer or Chief Privacy Officer, CIO and relevant Data Owner; Legal for high-risk disclosures or cross-border issues.
verification: Privacy impact screening, access review, data location review, supplier access review, restoration/test evidence review and audit sampling.
evidence: Data classification records, PIA screening, privacy approvals, access logs, supplier access records, data location register, retention/disposal evidence, protective marking evidence and exception approvals.
auditFrequency: At least annually and after major data, supplier, location or recovery process change.
relatedPolicies: Privacy Management Policy; Information Governance Policy; Records Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Data Sharing Policy.
relatedProcedures: PIA screening procedure; secure data handling procedure; backup data handling procedure; test data procedure; secure disposal procedure; supplier access procedure.
reviewTriggers: New data use, new supplier or location, privacy breach, change to privacy law or information rules, major recovery test, audit finding or data retention change.
notes: DR testing and temporary workarounds must not become a shortcut around privacy or protected information controls.

section: 8. Supplier, procurement and outsourced ICT continuity
title: Third-party DR assurance, contracts and supplier conduct
obligationDescription: NDIA must include proportionate DR, security, privacy, incident reporting, testing, assurance, subcontractor, evidence, remediation and exit requirements in ICT procurements and contracts, and must monitor supplier recovery capability, IRAP or equivalent assurance, critical dependencies, residual risks and supplier compliance throughout the service lifecycle.
requirement: The NDIA must include clear disaster recovery, security, privacy, testing, reporting, evidence, remediation and exit requirements in ICT procurements and contracts. Supplier recovery capability and risks must be monitored for the life of the service.
obligationRef:
NDIS-PDI-02 (NDIS Info Rules): NDIS Information Rules - secure handling by delegates, staff and service providers
PSPF - 39 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
PSPF - 40 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
PSPF - 41 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management

otherStandards: NDIS Information Rules; PSPF Third Party Risk Management and Cyber Security Programs; Australian Cyber Security Strategy; SOCI third-party notification concepts; Hosting Certification Framework; Commonwealth Procurement Rules; Commonwealth Supplier Code of Conduct.
controlCategory: Supplier, procurement and outsourced ICT continuity
controlObjective: Ensure suppliers that support NDIA ICT services can meet recovery, security, privacy, reporting and evidence obligations.
threat: Supplier outage, poor contract coverage, untested outsourced recovery, subcontractor failure, missing evidence, delayed incident reporting, weak exit arrangements and unmanaged residual risk.
applicability: All ICT suppliers, cloud providers, managed service providers, hosting providers, software vendors, support providers and subcontractors that affect NDIA recovery capability.
excluded: Low-risk suppliers with no access to NDIA systems, data or recovery processes may be excluded only after documented risk assessment.
guidance: Include DR requirements in procurement and contracts, request assurance evidence, test supplier recovery arrangements, track remediation and maintain exit or transition plans.
technicalControls: Contractual DR clauses; supplier assurance register; service level monitoring; incident reporting channels; access controls; assurance evidence repository; exit plan repository.
processSteps: 1. Define DR requirements before procurement. 2. Include obligations in contracts. 3. Collect supplier evidence. 4. Test or validate recovery capability. 5. Track issues. 6. Maintain exit plans.
accountable: Chief Information Officer and Chief Procurement Officer or delegated procurement lead
responsible: Contract Owners; Supplier Managers; Procurement; ICT DR Manager; Cyber Security; Service Owners; Legal.
consulted: Privacy; Risk; Enterprise Architecture; Business Continuity; Records Management; Internal Audit; Finance.
informed: CIO; contract governance forums; affected business service owners; operational support teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only through procurement, contract and risk approval with compensating controls.
exceptionProcess: Document the clause or assurance gap, supplier rationale, risk assessment, compensating controls, remediation date and contract or risk approval.
exceptionAuthority: Contract Owner, Procurement delegate and CIO; risk committee for high residual supplier risk.
verification: Contract review, supplier assurance review, service level review, DR test participation, evidence sampling and issue tracking review.
evidence: Contract clauses, statements of work, supplier DR plans, IRAP or assurance reports, test results, service reports, incident reports, remediation plans and exit plans.
auditFrequency: At least annually, at contract renewal and after major supplier change or incident.
relatedPolicies: Procurement Policy; Supplier Risk Management Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Privacy Management Policy; Contract Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: ICT procurement checklist; supplier DR assurance procedure; contract clause library; supplier test procedure; exit planning procedure; issue remediation process.
reviewTriggers: New procurement, contract renewal, supplier incident, subcontractor change, failed assurance, major service change, audit finding or exit trigger.
owner: ICT Supplier Assurance SME / Contract Owner
notes: Supplier recovery commitments should be measurable and supported by evidence, not just stated in contracts.

section: 9. Records, evidence, reporting and information access
title: Records continuity, audit evidence, metadata, FOI and performance reporting
obligationDescription: NDIA must create, protect and retain reliable records of DR planning, tests, incidents, recovery decisions, outage impacts, workarounds, restoration results, metadata and lessons learned so that performance, audit, FOI, public-information, records-retention and accountability obligations can be met after a disruption.
requirement: The NDIA must create, protect and keep reliable disaster recovery records. Plans, tests, incidents, recovery decisions, outage impacts, workarounds, restoration results, metadata and lessons learned must be available for audit, reporting, FOI, records retention and accountability.
obligationRef:
PGPA-35 (PGPA): PGPA Act ss35, 37 and 39 - performance information, records and performance statements
ARC-23 (Archives NAA): Archives Act 1983 - Commonwealth records
ARC-24 (Archives NAA): NAA Information Management Standard - digital information management
ARC-25 (Archives NAA): NAA standards - information continuity during system change or decommissioning
FOI-14 (FOI IPS): FOI Act - right of access to documents
FOI-15 (FOI IPS): FOI Act Part II - Information Publication Scheme
DPS-06 (Digital Performance): Digital Performance Standard - Criterion 2 availability
DPS-07 (Digital Performance): Digital Performance Standard - performance measurement and reporting
ismControls: Relevant ISM logging, audit, backup evidence and information protection controls as applicable.
otherStandards: PGPA performance and records obligations; Archives Act; National Archives Information Management Standard; FOI Act and Information Publication Scheme; Digital Performance Standard.
controlObjective: Keep trustworthy records of disaster recovery planning, decisions, tests, incidents and outcomes so the NDIA can prove what happened and meet reporting obligations.
threat: Missing audit evidence, loss of recovery decisions, inability to respond to FOI or records requests, weak performance reporting and repeated issues not tracked.
applicability: All DR plans, test records, incident records, recovery decision logs, outage and impact records, workarounds, restoration results, metadata, evidence packs and lessons learned.
excluded: Transient working notes may be excluded only if required records are captured in approved repositories.
guidance: Use approved recordkeeping repositories, define evidence requirements, protect metadata, retain records for approved periods and link lessons learned to remediation actions.
technicalControls: Records management system; evidence repository; incident management tool; document version control; audit logging; metadata controls; retention and disposal controls.
processSteps: 1. Define required DR records and evidence. 2. Capture records during tests and incidents. 3. Store in approved repositories. 4. Apply retention and disposal rules. 5. Report outcomes and track actions.
accountable: Chief Information Officer and Records Management Lead
responsible: ICT DR Manager; Records Manager; Service Owners; Incident Managers; Test Managers; Business Continuity; Cyber Security.
consulted: FOI; Legal; Privacy; Risk; Internal Audit; Communications; Performance Reporting.
informed: Executive governance forums; Audit and Risk Committee; affected business areas; operational support teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only where recordkeeping obligations are still met through an approved alternative.
exceptionProcess: Document the alternative recordkeeping approach, reason, risk, retention impact, approvals and review date.
exceptionAuthority: Records Management Lead and CIO; Legal or FOI delegate where access or disclosure obligations may be affected.
verification: Records sampling, evidence pack review, retention compliance review, audit review and action tracker review.
evidence: DR plans, test reports, incident logs, decision logs, outage reports, restoration evidence, metadata records, FOI/records decisions, lessons learned and remediation tracker.
auditFrequency: At least annually and after each major incident or exercise.
relatedPolicies: Records Management Policy; Information Governance Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Incident Management Policy; Performance Reporting Policy.
relatedProcedures: DR evidence collection procedure; recordkeeping procedure; incident decision log template; test report template; lessons learned and remediation tracking process.
reviewTriggers: Major incident or exercise, FOI or audit request, records retention change, system decommissioning, failed evidence review or reporting obligation change.
owner: Records Management SME / ICT DR Manager
notes: Good records are part of recovery because they support decisions, assurance and accountability after disruption.

section: 10. Testing, exercises, assurance and continual improvement
title: DR testing, audit, accessibility validation and remediation tracking
obligationDescription: NDIA must test and exercise DR arrangements at planned intervals and after material change or major incidents, validate technical, business, security and accessibility outcomes against approved recovery objectives, report results to assurance forums, and track defects, exceptions and lessons learned through accountable remediation plans.
requirement: The NDIA must test disaster recovery arrangements at planned intervals and after major changes or incidents. Tests must check technical recovery, business outcomes, security and accessibility against approved targets, and defects and lessons learned must be tracked to closure.
obligationRef:
PGPA-37 (PGPA): PGPA Act s45 and PGPA Rule audit committee requirements
ISM-15 (ISM): ISM March 2026 - system recovery assurance principle
DSS-12 (Digital Service Std): Digital Service Standard - ongoing service operation
DAS-07 (Digital Access): Digital Access Standard - testing and conformance
ismControls: ISM system recovery assurance principle; relevant recovery testing, logging, monitoring and control validation requirements.
otherStandards: PGPA Act audit committee requirements; Digital Service Standard ongoing operation; Digital Access Standard testing and conformance.
controlObjective: Prove that DR arrangements work, identify gaps and make sure remediation is owned, tracked and completed.
threat: Untested plans, failed recovery, inaccessible workarounds, unresolved defects, repeated audit findings and false confidence in recovery capability.
applicability: All critical NDIA ICT services, DR plans, recovery runbooks, suppliers, workarounds, accessibility outcomes and security controls that support approved recovery targets.
excluded: Services may use tabletop testing only where a live or technical recovery test is not practical and the limitation is approved and recorded.
guidance: Maintain a risk-based test schedule, include technical and business scenarios, validate RTO/RPO, security and accessibility, report results and track remediation to closure.
technicalControls: Test environments; recovery tooling; monitoring and timing evidence; defect tracker; test data controls; accessibility validation tools; reporting dashboards.
processSteps: 1. Approve the test schedule. 2. Define test scope and success criteria. 3. Run exercises. 4. Validate recovery targets, security and accessibility. 5. Report results. 6. Track defects and lessons learned to closure.
responsible: ICT DR Manager; Test Manager; Service Owners; System Owners; Cyber Security; Business Continuity; Accessibility Lead; Supplier Managers.
consulted: Risk; Internal Audit; Privacy; Records; Communications; Legal; affected business teams.
informed: Executive governance forums; Audit and Risk Committee; service owners; support teams; key suppliers.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only where risk-based test limitations are approved and compensating assurance is documented.
exceptionProcess: Record the test limitation, reason, risk, compensating assurance, approver, expiry and future test plan.
exceptionAuthority: CIO and relevant Business Service Owner; Audit and Risk Committee visibility for critical gaps.
verification: Exercise observation, test evidence review, RTO/RPO validation, accessibility check, security validation and remediation tracker review.
evidence: Approved test schedule, test plans, exercise reports, timing evidence, RTO/RPO results, accessibility test evidence, security validation, defect logs and closure evidence.
auditFrequency: At least annually for critical services, after major change and after major incidents.
relatedPolicies: ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Business Continuity Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Digital Accessibility Policy; Internal Audit and Assurance Policy.
relatedProcedures: DR test procedure; exercise plan template; post-test report template; accessibility testing procedure; remediation tracking process.
reviewTriggers: Major incident, significant system or supplier change, failed test, audit finding, accessibility change, new critical service or unresolved remediation risk.
notes: Testing should validate business outcomes, not only technical restoration steps.

title: Accessible, inclusive and properly marked DR communications and workarounds
obligationDescription: NDIA must provide timely, accessible, inclusive and appropriately protectively marked communications and continuity workarounds during ICT disruptions, including participant, provider, staff, supplier and inter-agency messages, alternate channels for users with disability or low digital access, and controls to prevent sensitive recovery information being shared through unapproved channels.
requirement: The NDIA must provide timely, accessible and inclusive communications during ICT disruptions. Messages and workarounds for participants, providers, staff, suppliers and agencies must use approved channels, meet accessibility needs and protect sensitive recovery information.

controlObjective: Provide clear, accessible and secure communications and workarounds during ICT disruptions.
threat: Participants, providers or staff cannot access services or information; inaccessible updates; inconsistent messages; sensitive recovery information shared through unapproved channels.

excluded: None for communications affecting participants, providers or critical service continuity. Internal technical-only communications may follow incident channels if classification controls are met.
guidance: Prepare communication templates and channels, apply protective markings, include accessibility and inclusion checks, approve alternate channels and coordinate messages with incident and business continuity teams.
technicalControls: Approved communication channels; secure collaboration tools; protective marking; template repository; accessibility checking tools; contact lists; status page or service update mechanisms.
processSteps: 1. Identify audiences and channels. 2. Draft accessible messages. 3. Apply protective markings. 4. Approve and send communications. 5. Provide alternate channels or workarounds. 6. Record decisions and updates.
accountable: Communications Lead with the Chief Information Officer
responsible: Communications Team; ICT DR Manager; Service Owners; Business Continuity; Accessibility Lead; Cyber Security; Service Delivery teams.
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Risk; Participant service areas; Supplier Managers; Records Management; External liaison teams.
informed: Participants; providers; NDIA staff; suppliers; executive governance forums; relevant agencies where approved.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only for approved alternate channels that meet accessibility, privacy and protective marking requirements.
exceptionProcess: Document the alternate communication approach, reason, audience, information classification, accessibility check, privacy/security assessment, approver and review point.
exceptionAuthority: Communications Lead and CIO; Privacy or Legal where personal or protected information is involved.
verification: Communication exercise review, template review, accessibility validation, protective marking review and incident communication record sampling.
evidence: Communication plans, templates, approvals, audience lists, accessibility checks, protective marking records, sent messages, workaround approvals and lessons learned.
auditFrequency: At least annually and after major incident or communications exercise.
relatedPolicies: Communications Policy; Accessibility and Inclusion Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy; Business Continuity Policy; Protective Marking Policy; Privacy Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: DR communications procedure; accessible communications checklist; protective marking procedure; alternate channel procedure; stakeholder notification templates.
reviewTriggers: Major incident, changed service channel, accessibility finding, privacy or security incident, stakeholder feedback, communications exercise or updated marking standard.
owner: Communications and Accessibility SME / ICT DR Manager
notes: Disruption communications must be accessible to the people who rely on NDIA services.

controlObjective: Make cyber security ownership, risk decisions, escalation and reporting clear and accountable.
threat: Unclear accountability, untreated cyber risks, delayed escalation and weak executive oversight.
applicability: All NDIA cyber security governance, ICT risk decisions, ICT systems, information assets, personnel and third parties that affect NDIA security.
excluded: None by default. Any exclusion must be risk-assessed and approved through the exception process.
guidance: Maintain approved cyber security roles, committees, delegations, risk appetite, risk register, reporting cycle and strategy. Use an ISMS-aligned approach to plan, prioritise and improve controls.
technicalControls: GRC platform or register, risk workflow, reporting dashboards, document repository, issue and action tracking.
processSteps: Define roles and delegations; assess cyber risks; assign owners and treatments; report material risks; escalate overdue actions; review strategy and ISMS performance.
responsible: Cyber Security GRC; Enterprise Risk; System Owners; Business Owners; Technology Operations.
consulted: CIO; Chief Risk Officer; Agency Security Adviser; Legal; Privacy; Internal Audit.

section: 2. Secure technology lifecycle, architecture and operations
title: Secure technology lifecycle, architecture, cloud, gateways and secure configuration
obligationDescription: NDIA systems must be designed, built, procured, authorised, configured, changed and operated using secure architecture patterns, approved technology lifecycle controls, cloud and gateway safeguards, and secure configuration baselines proportionate to classification, data sensitivity and business risk.

controlObjective: Ensure systems are securely designed, configured, changed, operated and retired.
threat: Insecure design, unauthorised technology, cloud or gateway misconfiguration, unsafe change and technology lifecycle failure.
applicability: All NDIA ICT systems, applications, platforms, infrastructure, cloud services, gateways, networks and technology changes.
excluded: None by default. Any exclusion must be risk-assessed and approved through the exception process.
guidance: Use approved patterns and reference architectures, perform security design reviews, apply secure baselines, validate cloud and gateway settings, and include security in change and release gates.
technicalControls: Secure configuration baselines, architecture review tooling, cloud security posture management, gateway controls, change management and configuration management database.
processSteps: Identify security requirements; review architecture; approve design; build to secure baseline; test controls; approve change; monitor and retire safely.
responsible: Cyber Architecture; Security Engineering; Technology Operations; Cloud Platform Owners; Change and Release Management.
consulted: CIO; CISO; Enterprise Architecture; Procurement; Privacy; Legal; Business Owners.
informed: System Owners; Service Owners; Change Advisory Board; relevant suppliers.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved risk acceptance only.
exceptionProcess: Document the business reason, affected systems, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan. Record the exception in the risk/exception register and review it before expiry.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and relevant risk owner. CIO or executive risk forum approval is required for high or critical residual risk.
verification: Review architecture decisions, security design assessments, change records, configuration baseline compliance and authorisation records.
evidence: Security architecture review, threat model, approved design, configuration baseline, change approvals, test results, authorisation to operate and decommissioning records.
auditFrequency: At each major design/change and annually.
relatedPolicies: ICT Change Management Policy; Cloud Security Policy; ICT Asset Management Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Security design review procedure; secure configuration standard; cloud onboarding guide; change and release procedure; system authorisation procedure.
reviewTriggers: Major system change, new cloud service, new gateway, significant configuration change, incident or audit finding.
notes: Use this requirement to ensure disaster recovery solutions are secure by design and recover to approved configurations.

title: ISM and supporting cyber security control baseline
obligationDescription: NDIA systems must select, implement, maintain and evidence the applicable ISM and supporting cyber security control baseline before operational use; any control gap must have an approved treatment, compensating control or residual risk acceptance.
requirement: Each NDIA system must know which ISM controls apply and must implement those controls before the system is used. Any control that cannot be met must have an approved risk treatment, compensating control or risk acceptance.

controlObjective: Reduce common cyber compromise pathways using measured and prioritised control uplift.
threat: Malware, ransomware, application exploitation, weak administrative control, delayed patching and preventable compromise.
applicability: All NDIA endpoints, servers, applications, cloud services and platforms covered by the Essential Eight or related hardening controls.
excluded: None by default. Any exclusion must be risk-assessed and approved through the exception process.
guidance: Set target maturity levels, assess current maturity, prioritise gaps, fund uplift work, track remediation and report progress to governance forums.
technicalControls: Application control, patch management, macro control, user application hardening, administrative privilege controls, MFA, regular backups and maturity reporting tools.
processSteps: Assess maturity; identify gaps; agree target levels; plan uplift; remediate controls; test effectiveness; report results and residual risks.
responsible: Essential Eight Uplift Lead; Endpoint and Server Teams; IAM Team; Backup Service Owner; Application Owners.
consulted: CISO; CIO; Cyber Security GRC; Technology Operations; Business Owners; Internal Audit.
informed: NDIA Executive; system owners; service owners.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved risk acceptance only.
exceptionProcess: Document the business reason, affected systems, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan. Record the exception in the risk/exception register and review it before expiry.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and relevant risk owner. CIO or executive risk forum approval is required for high or critical residual risk.
verification: Review Essential Eight maturity assessments, technical evidence, remediation plans and progress reporting.
evidence: Maturity assessment results, control test evidence, uplift roadmap, remediation tickets, exception register, backup test results and executive reports.
auditFrequency: Quarterly maturity review and annual independent assurance.
relatedPolicies: ICT Cyber Security Policy; Patch Management Policy; Access Control Policy; Backup and Recovery Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Essential Eight assessment procedure; hardening standards; patching procedure; privileged access procedure; backup testing procedure.
reviewTriggers: Essential Eight maturity target change, ISM update, major incident, audit finding, new technology platform or significant control gap.
notes: This requirement supports both cyber risk reduction and resilience outcomes.

title: Identity, access, privileged access, remote access and joiner-mover-leaver controls
obligationDescription: Access to NDIA systems must use unique identities, least privilege, multi-factor authentication, controlled privileged access, secure remote access, timely joiner-mover-leaver processes and regular access review, with exceptions approved and monitored.

ismControls: 164 ISM controls listed in the Obligation Reference, including ISM-0133, ISM-0260, ISM-0261, ISM-0267, ISM-0269, ISM-0343, ISM-0347, ISM-0372, ISM-0380, ISM-0382, ISM-0383, ISM-0405, ISM-0408, ISM-0409, ISM-0411, ISM-0414, ISM-0415, ISM-0418, ISM-0422, ISM-0428. See Obligation Reference for the full mapping.
otherStandards: Source references include: Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF); ASD Information Security Manual (ISM); Essential Eight; CIS Controls; PCI DSS; OWASP; Privacy Act; NDIS-related requirements.
controlObjective: Ensure only authorised people and services can access NDIA systems and information.
threat: Unauthorised access, account compromise, privilege misuse, orphaned accounts, weak remote access and identity fraud.
applicability: All NDIA workforce, privileged, service, break-glass, remote, supplier and third-party accounts across NDIA systems and services.
excluded: None by default. Emergency access is in scope and must be logged, approved and reviewed.
guidance: Use standard joiner-mover-leaver workflows, MFA, role-based access, privileged access management, access reviews and timely disablement for changed or departed users.
technicalControls: Identity provider, MFA, single sign-on, PAM, conditional access, access certification tool, logging and account lifecycle automation.
processSteps: Request access; verify need and approval; assign least privilege; monitor privileged use; review access regularly; remove or change access promptly; investigate anomalies.
responsible: IAM Team; HR; System Owners; Service Desk; PAM Administrators; Technology Operations.
consulted: CIO; Business Owners; Privacy; Legal; Procurement; Supplier Managers.
informed: All users; managers; system owners; suppliers with access.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved risk acceptance only.
exceptionProcess: Document the business reason, affected systems, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan. Record the exception in the risk/exception register and review it before expiry.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and relevant risk owner. CIO or executive risk forum approval is required for high or critical residual risk.
verification: Sample access requests, MFA/PAM reports, joiner-mover-leaver records, quarterly access reviews and privileged access logs.
evidence: Access request approvals, role definitions, MFA coverage reports, PAM session logs, user recertification records, leaver disablement evidence and exception records.
auditFrequency: Quarterly access review and annual IAM assurance.
relatedPolicies: Access Control Policy; Acceptable Use Policy; Remote Access Policy; Third-Party Security Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Joiner-mover-leaver procedure; privileged access procedure; remote access standard; access review procedure; service account standard.
reviewTriggers: IAM platform change, new supplier access, privileged access incident, audit finding, role restructure or material access control failure.
notes: Use plain-language access rules so managers and users understand their responsibilities.

title: Cryptographic standards, certificates, secrets and key lifecycle management
obligationDescription: NDIA must use approved cryptography and securely manage keys, certificates, secrets, cryptographic equipment and algorithms across their lifecycle to protect information at rest, in transit and during authentication.
requirement: NDIA must use approved encryption to protect sensitive information and communications. Keys, certificates, secrets and passwords must be created, stored, rotated, revoked and destroyed securely.

controlObjective: Protect the confidentiality, integrity and authenticity of NDIA information and services.
threat: Data disclosure, tampering, impersonation, service compromise, expired certificates and exposed secrets.
applicability: All NDIA systems, applications, networks, cloud services, databases, backups, APIs and devices that use encryption, certificates, secrets or keys.
excluded: None by default. Legacy cryptography can only be used with approved compensating controls and a time-bound remediation plan.
guidance: Use approved algorithms and protocols, centralise key and certificate management where possible, restrict access to secrets, automate expiry monitoring and remove weak or deprecated cryptography.
technicalControls: Key management service, HSM or equivalent, certificate management, TLS, secrets vault, encryption at rest and in transit, and cryptographic configuration scanning.
processSteps: Classify data; select approved cryptography; issue keys/certificates; store secrets securely; rotate and revoke credentials; monitor expiry; review access; securely destroy keys when no longer needed.
responsible: Security Architecture; Platform Owners; Application Owners; PKI/Certificate Administrators; Cloud Operations.
consulted: CISO; CIO; Privacy; Legal; Enterprise Architecture; Technology Operations.
informed: System owners; application owners; operational support teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved risk acceptance only.
exceptionProcess: Document the business reason, affected systems, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan. Record the exception in the risk/exception register and review it before expiry.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and relevant risk owner. CIO or executive risk forum approval is required for high or critical residual risk.
verification: Review encryption configurations, key and certificate inventories, secrets management records, access logs and expiry/rotation reports.
evidence: Cryptographic standards, key inventory, certificate register, secrets vault records, rotation evidence, configuration scan results and exception approvals.
auditFrequency: Annual cryptography review and after key/certificate changes.
relatedPolicies: ICT Cyber Security Policy; Information Classification Policy; Data Protection Policy; Backup and Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Cryptography standard; certificate management procedure; secrets management procedure; key rotation procedure; secure disposal procedure.
reviewTriggers: New cryptographic guidance, certificate expiry event, exposed secret, major system change, incident or audit finding.
notes: Requirement includes backup and recovery data because protected backups must remain accessible and trustworthy.

section: 7. Information, privacy, assets and data lifecycle
title: Information protection, privacy, classification, asset, media and data lifecycle
obligationDescription: NDIA information and ICT assets must be identified, classified, marked, collected, used, disclosed, shared, stored, retained, transferred, sanitised, destroyed and disposed of lawfully and securely according to sensitivity, privacy, records, NDIS, FOI and protective security obligations.
requirement: NDIA must know what information and ICT assets it holds, classify them correctly and protect them throughout their life cycle from collection and storage through sharing, archiving, disposal and media handling.
