controlObjective: Protect NDIA information and assets according to value, sensitivity, privacy and classification.
threat: Data loss, privacy breach, unauthorised disclosure, poor asset visibility, mishandled media and records non-compliance.
applicability: All NDIA information holdings, datasets, records, ICT assets, media, endpoints, applications, cloud services and environments.
excluded: None by default. Publicly released information is only excluded after authorised publication and records requirements are met.
guidance: Maintain information and asset inventories, apply classifications and markings, restrict handling and sharing, protect media, manage retention and securely dispose of data and assets.
technicalControls: Asset register/CMDB, data catalogue, classification labels, DLP where applicable, encryption, secure media handling, disposal logging and backup classification controls.
processSteps: Identify assets and information; classify and label; assign owners; apply handling rules; review access and storage; retain or dispose according to schedule; record transfers and destruction.
responsible: Information Governance; ICT Asset Management; Privacy; Cyber Security GRC; System Owners; Records Management.
consulted: CISO; Chief Data Officer; Legal; Procurement; Business Owners; Archives/Records.
informed: All personnel; information owners; asset custodians; suppliers handling NDIA information.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved risk acceptance only.
exceptionProcess: Document the business reason, affected systems, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan. Record the exception in the risk/exception register and review it before expiry.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and relevant risk owner. CIO or executive risk forum approval is required for high or critical residual risk.
verification: Review asset and information registers, classification samples, handling records, disposal certificates and privacy/security control evidence.
evidence: Data and asset inventories, classification records, information handling approvals, media transfer/destruction records, privacy impact assessments and disposal evidence.
auditFrequency: Annual and after major information or asset changes.
relatedPolicies: Information Management Policy; Privacy Policy; Records Management Policy; ICT Asset Management Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Information classification procedure; media handling procedure; secure disposal guide; asset lifecycle procedure; data retention schedule.
reviewTriggers: New information holding, privacy incident, asset discovery gap, records requirement change, major system change or audit finding.
owner: Information Governance and Privacy with Cyber Security GRC.
notes: Recovery plans must account for the classification and handling rules for restored data and media.

title: Vulnerability management, patching, remediation and exception handling
obligationDescription: NDIA must continuously identify, prioritise, remediate and verify vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and unsupported technology through risk-based scanning, patching, hardening, exception management and accountable remediation tracking.
requirement: NDIA must find, prioritise and fix vulnerabilities, missing patches, misconfigurations and unsupported technology within agreed timeframes. Exceptions must be risk-assessed, time-bound and tracked until closed.

controlCategory: Security monitoring, logging and threat management

notes: Logs must remain available during and after recovery activities to support investigation and assurance.

controlObjective: Minimise harm from cyber incidents and restore critical services and data within agreed expectations.
threat: Poor incident handling, delayed breach notification, ransomware impact, data loss, extended outages and repeated incidents.
applicability: All NDIA systems, data, services, business areas, suppliers and third parties involved in cyber incident response, backup, continuity or recovery.
excluded: None. Legal, privacy and statutory notification obligations must always be assessed.
guidance: Keep incident playbooks, breach assessment steps, communication paths, backup/restore procedures, recovery priorities and lessons-learned processes aligned and tested.
technicalControls: Incident management platform, SIEM/SOC tooling, EDR containment, backup and restore platform, immutable/offline backups where required, and crisis communications tools.

evidence: Incident response plan, breach assessment records, incident tickets, communication logs, backup schedules, restore test evidence, recovery runbooks, exercise outcomes and post-incident reviews.
auditFrequency: Annual exercise, annual restore testing and after every material incident.

relatedProcedures: Cyber incident response plan; data breach response procedure; ransomware playbook; backup and restore procedure; disaster recovery test procedure; communications protocol.
reviewTriggers: Material incident, ransomware threat, major system change, failed restore test, lessons learned, regulatory change or audit finding.
owner: Cyber Incident Response and ICT Resilience Lead.

controlObjective: Ensure suppliers that handle NDIA systems or information meet NDIA security and resilience expectations.
threat: Supplier compromise, insecure outsourced services, contract gaps, data exposure, service interruption and unmanaged subcontractor risk.
applicability: All suppliers, contractors, cloud providers, hosting providers, subcontractors and managed service providers that access, process, store or support NDIA information or systems.
excluded: None by default. Low-risk suppliers may use a proportionate assurance pathway approved by procurement and cyber security.
guidance: Embed security in procurement, perform risk-based due diligence, include contract clauses, require incident notification, monitor assurance, manage subcontractors and plan safe exit or transition.
technicalControls: Supplier risk register, procurement workflow controls, third-party assurance questionnaires, contract clause library, access controls, monitoring and incident notification channels.
processSteps: Classify supplier risk; conduct due diligence; include security requirements in contracts; onboard securely; monitor performance; manage incidents; review renewals; execute exit plan.
responsible: Third-Party Security Risk Team; Procurement; Contract Managers; Supplier Managers; System Owners; Cyber Security GRC.
consulted: CISO; CIO; Legal; Privacy; Enterprise Risk; Business Owners; Finance.
informed: Suppliers; service owners; contract owners; affected business areas.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved risk acceptance only.
exceptionProcess: Document the business reason, affected systems, risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan. Record the exception in the risk/exception register and review it before expiry.
exceptionAuthority: CISO, Procurement/Contract Owner and relevant risk owner. CIO or executive risk forum approval is required for high or critical residual risk.
verification: Review supplier due diligence, contracts, assurance reports, risk treatments, incident notifications, access records and exit/transition plans.
evidence: Supplier risk assessments, contract security clauses, assurance attestations, security questionnaires, incident notification records, subcontractor approvals, exit plans and risk acceptances.
auditFrequency: At onboarding, annually for higher-risk suppliers, before renewal and before exit.
relatedPolicies: Third-Party Risk Management Policy; Procurement Policy; Cloud Security Policy; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Supplier security assessment procedure; contract security schedule; supplier incident notification procedure; supplier exit checklist; third-party assurance guide.
reviewTriggers: New supplier, contract renewal, supplier incident, service change, subcontractor change, regulator/audit finding or exit/transition event.
notes: Supplier recovery obligations should align with NDIA recovery priorities and incident notification needs.

controlObjective: Build security behaviours and readiness across NDIA and its relevant third parties.
threat: User error, phishing, social engineering, poor reporting, unclear responsibilities and unprepared response teams.

notes: Training should include how to report incidents quickly and where to find recovery and continuity instructions.

controlObjective: Demonstrate that security controls are effective, risks are managed and systems remain authorised.
threat: Unproven control effectiveness, unsupported authorisation, unmanaged exceptions, poor auditability and inaccurate security reporting.
applicability: All NDIA systems, controls, cyber risks, exceptions, assurance activities, audits, authorisation decisions and management reporting.
excluded: None by default. Any reduced assurance activity must be approved and documented with the reason and alternate evidence.
guidance: Define useful metrics, collect repeatable evidence, keep audit trails, track actions and exceptions, and report control performance and authorisation status to governance forums.
technicalControls: GRC/assurance platform, evidence repository, dashboard/reporting tools, audit logging, control testing tools, exception register and action tracking.
processSteps: Define metrics; collect evidence; test controls; report status; track exceptions and actions; review authorisation evidence; escalate overdue or high-risk issues; retain records.
responsible: Cyber Assurance Team; Cyber Security GRC; System Owners; Control Owners; Internal Audit Liaison; Technology Operations.
consulted: CISO; CIO; Enterprise Risk; Internal Audit; Business Owners; Legal; Privacy.
informed: NDIA Executive; system owners; control owners; risk owners; audit and assurance forums.

verification: Review metric definitions, assurance test results, evidence samples, audit trails, exception register, management reports and authorisation packages.
evidence: Metrics dashboard, assurance plan, control test evidence, audit logs, exception register, risk treatment updates, authorisation decision records and management review minutes.
auditFrequency: Quarterly reporting and annual assurance review.
relatedPolicies: Cyber Security Assurance Policy; System Authorisation Policy; Risk Management Policy; Internal Audit Charter; ICT Disaster Recovery Policy.
relatedProcedures: Security metrics procedure; control testing procedure; evidence management guide; system authorisation procedure; exception reporting procedure.
reviewTriggers: New control requirement, system authorisation change, audit finding, assurance failure, exception trend, incident or material risk change.
notes: Evidence should be understandable and sufficient for audit, authorisation and management review.

title: Statutory purpose and lawful information exchange
obligationDescription: NDIA integrations must be used only where they support NDIA statutory functions or an approved data sharing purpose, have a documented lawful authority, and enforce technical and procedural controls that prevent unauthorised collection, use, disclosure, caching, transformation, reuse or exchange of protected Agency information and barred data.
requirement: NDIA must only build, run or use an integration when it supports an NDIA function or an approved data sharing purpose and has a clear legal authority. Integrations must not collect, use, disclose, store, transform or share protected information unless that authority and the approved purpose allow it.

controlObjective: Ensure each integration only exchanges data for lawful and approved NDIA purposes.
threat: Unlawful disclosure, unauthorised secondary use, misuse of protected Agency information and loss of public trust.
applicability: All NDIA ICT integrations, APIs, data feeds, file transfers, event streams, middleware, gateways and partner interfaces.
excluded: None for ICT integrations. Non-ICT manual processes remain covered by the relevant information, privacy and business policies.
guidance: Confirm the business purpose, legal authority and approved sharing purpose during intake. Map each data field to that purpose and configure controls so data cannot be collected, cached, reused or shared outside the approved scope.
technicalControls: Purpose and field allow lists; API gateway rules; data loss prevention; encryption in transit and at rest; access controls; audit logging; retention and cache controls.
processSteps: Record lawful authority; approve data fields; document partner and recipient; complete privacy and security review; test controls before go-live; review access and sharing annually.
responsible: System Owner; Data Owner; Integration Delivery Lead; Security Architect
consulted: Legal; Privacy Officer; Chief Data Officer; Cyber Security; Records Management
informed: Connected partner; Service Owner; Audit and Assurance
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to legal authority requirements.
exceptionProcess: Where authority is unclear, pause the integration and obtain Legal, Privacy and Data Governance advice before design, release or further sharing.
exceptionAuthority: General Counsel or delegate, with Privacy Officer and Chief Data Officer endorsement
verification: Review integration intake record, legal authority mapping, data flow design and test evidence.
evidence: Lawful authority assessment; data sharing approval; data inventory; data flow diagram; security and privacy assessment; audit logs.
auditFrequency: At each new integration or material change, and annually for active integrations
relatedPolicies: ICT Integration Policy; Privacy Policy; Data Governance Policy; Information Security Policy
relatedProcedures: Integration Intake Procedure; Data Sharing Assessment Guide; Privacy Impact Assessment Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New or amended legislation; new data set or recipient; material integration change; incident; audit finding.
notes: No policy exception can create a legal authority to share information.

title: Governance, risk ownership and shared accountability
obligationDescription: Every integration must have named business, system and security risk owners, be assessed against NDIA's approved governance arrangements and enterprise risk appetite, and allocate shared risk, control, monitoring, training, escalation and review responsibilities across NDIA and connected partners.
requirement: Each integration must have a named business owner, system owner and security risk owner before design or operation starts. Owners must understand the shared risks, agree controls with partners, monitor those controls and review accountability regularly.

excluded: None for ICT integrations. Non-ICT manual processes remain covered by the relevant information, privacy and business policies.
guidance: Use a governance gate before design and release. Record a RACI, shared-risk assessment, risk appetite decision, control owner mapping and review schedule for every integration.
technicalControls: Authorised interface register; risk register workflow; control owner mapping; approval workflow; monitoring dashboard; training and attestation records.
processSteps: Assign owners; identify shared risks; agree controls and service levels; approve risk treatment; monitor key controls; escalate overdue or failed controls.

responsible: Business Owner; System Owner; Security Risk Owner; Partner Manager
consulted: Enterprise Architecture; Cyber Security; Privacy; Legal; Data Governance; Procurement
informed: Connected partners; service operations; internal audit; affected business areas
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, only for time-bound governance gaps with formal risk acceptance.
exceptionProcess: Document the gap, risk impact, compensating controls, owner and expiry date in the risk register before the integration proceeds.

verification: Check governance records, risk register entries, RACI, partner agreements and review minutes.
evidence: RACI; shared-risk assessment; risk acceptance; control owner matrix; partner agreement; governance meeting minutes.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for critical integrations and annually for all active integrations
relatedPolicies: ICT Governance Policy; Enterprise Risk Management Policy; Third Party Risk Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Integration Governance Procedure; Shared Risk Assessment Template; Control Owner Review Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: Change in owner, partner, risk appetite, control performance, system criticality, audit finding or incident.
notes: Shared accountability should be explicit before any partner or supplier connection is approved.

obligationDescription: Integrations must follow an ISM-aligned secure lifecycle from design to decommissioning, document architecture, control mapping and risk assessment, meet the approved Essential Eight target or obtain formal risk acceptance, and must not operate or materially change until residual risk is accepted by the Authorising Officer and the integration is recorded in the authorised systems or interface register.
requirement: Every integration must follow a secure lifecycle from design to retirement. It must be documented, risk assessed, recorded in the approved register, meet the agreed Essential Eight target or have a formal risk acceptance, and receive authorisation before it goes live or materially changes.

applicability: All new, changed, migrated, replatformed, decommissioned or materially reconfigured NDIA integrations.

guidance: Apply secure lifecycle gates for concept, design, build, test, release, operate, change and decommissioning. Keep architecture, control mapping, risk acceptance and register records current.
technicalControls: CI/CD security gates; architecture patterns; vulnerability scans; configuration baselines; change controls; authorisation workflow; system and interface register.
processSteps: Complete security design review; map controls; assess residual risk; record the integration; obtain authorisation; approve changes; plan secure decommissioning.
responsible: Integration Delivery Lead; Security Architect; Change Manager; Platform Owner
consulted: CISO delegate; Enterprise Architecture; Privacy; Data Owner; Business Owner
informed: Operations teams; service desk; connected partners; audit and assurance
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, only with time-bound risk acceptance and compensating controls.
exceptionProcess: Raise a security risk exception before go-live or change approval. Include the gap, business reason, residual risk, controls, expiry date and remediation plan.
exceptionAuthority: Authorising Officer, with CISO or delegated security authority endorsement
verification: Review lifecycle gate evidence, risk acceptance, change records, security test results and register entry.
evidence: Architecture design; control mapping; security risk assessment; Essential Eight assessment; authority to operate; change record; asset or interface register entry.
auditFrequency: At each release gate and annually for active integrations
relatedPolicies: Information Security Policy; Change Management Policy; ICT Integration Policy; Asset Management Policy
relatedProcedures: Secure Delivery Lifecycle Procedure; Security Assessment and Authorisation Procedure; Change Control Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: Major design change; new threat; failed control; change in Essential Eight target; decommissioning; audit finding.
notes: The integration should not operate without a current authorisation decision.

title: Classification, protective markings, metadata and caveat handling
obligationDescription: Integration payloads, messages, records, logs and metadata must preserve security classifications, protective markings, caveats and access-restriction metadata, and must enforce need-to-know, clearance or eligibility, routing and recipient controls appropriate to the highest sensitivity or classification of the data, including AUSTEO, AGAO and foreign-origin information.
requirement: Integrations must keep security classifications, protective markings, caveats and access restrictions with the data as it moves between systems. Access, routing, recipients and logging must be based on the most sensitive data in the integration.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 67 (PSPF 2025): 09. Classifications and Caveats
PSPF - 68 (PSPF 2025): 09. Classifications and Caveats
PSPF - 69 (PSPF 2025): 09. Classifications and Caveats
PSPF - 75 (PSPF 2025): 12. Information Sharing
PSPF - 80 (PSPF 2025): 12. Information Sharing
PSPF - 81 (PSPF 2025): 12. Information Sharing
PSPF - 82 (PSPF 2025): 12. Information Sharing
ismControls: ASD ISM domains: information classification; access control; data transfers; gateways; logging and monitoring.
otherStandards: PSPF Classifications and Caveats; PSPF Information Sharing; Australian Government protective security requirements.
controlObjective: Prevent sensitive or caveated information from being sent to the wrong system, person or partner.
threat: Loss of markings, misrouted data, inappropriate recipient access, mishandled AUSTEO, AGAO or foreign-origin information.
applicability: All integrations that process NDIA information with a security classification, protective marking, caveat, eligibility restriction or partner handling condition.
excluded: Only public information flows with no access restrictions may be excluded, and the Data Owner must record that assessment.
guidance: Classify the data flow before design. Preserve markings and access metadata in payloads, messages, records and logs, and apply routing and recipient rules to the highest sensitivity in the flow.
technicalControls: Metadata tagging; label propagation; API and message schema fields; access groups; clearance or eligibility checks; gateway routing rules; DLP; audit logging.
processSteps: Classify data; identify caveats and handling rules; configure access and routing; test marking preservation; review recipients and logs during operation.
responsible: System Owner; Integration Architect; Security Architect; Information Manager
consulted: Protective Security; Legal; Records; Privacy; connected partner security lead
informed: Integration operations; partner administrators; audit and assurance
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to mandatory classification, caveat or need-to-know handling.
exceptionProcess: Any alternative handling must be assessed by the Data Owner and Protective Security before implementation and must not reduce legal or security obligations.
exceptionAuthority: Data Owner and Protective Security authority, with CISO endorsement for technical controls
verification: Inspect data schemas, sample payloads, routing rules, access reviews and logs for marking and caveat preservation.
evidence: Classification assessment; data schema; metadata mapping; access control design; test results; access review; audit logs.
auditFrequency: At design approval, after material change and at least annually
relatedPolicies: Protective Security Policy; Information Security Policy; Data Governance Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Classification and Marking Procedure; Secure Data Transfer Procedure; Access Review Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New data classification; new caveat; partner change; incident; routing change; audit finding.
notes: Controls should follow the most sensitive data in the integration, not the average sensitivity.

title: Information-sharing agreements, DATA Scheme controls and foreign/cross-border exchange
obligationDescription: Before sharing data through an integration with another government, external, foreign or international party, NDIA must confirm the lawful sharing pathway, approved agreement or Data Sharing Agreement, participant accreditation where required, cross-border safeguards, foreign-interference and sovereignty risk treatment, authorised recipients, purpose, controls, retention and incident obligations, and must implement these requirements in technical release gates.
requirement: NDIA must not share data with an external, foreign or international party through an integration until the lawful pathway, approved agreement, recipients, purpose, retention, safeguards and incident obligations are documented and built into the integration controls.
obligationRef:

otherStandards: PSPF Information Sharing; PSPF Countering Foreign Interference; Privacy Act APP 8; DATA Scheme; ONDC Data Sharing Agreement guidance.
controlObjective: Ensure data sharing through integrations is lawful, agreed, controlled and monitored.
threat: Unauthorised cross-border disclosure, foreign interference risk, weak partner controls, unclear retention or incident responsibilities.
applicability: All NDIA integrations that share data with other government entities, suppliers, external partners, foreign entities or international parties.
excluded: No ICT sharing integration is excluded. Public open data releases must follow approved open data and information release processes.
guidance: Confirm the sharing pathway and agreement before release. Convert agreement requirements into technical rules for allowed recipients, fields, purposes, locations, retention, logging and incident notification.
technicalControls: Partner allow lists; API gateway and transfer rules; encryption; recipient and location restrictions; retention controls; monitoring; secure file transfer; release gates.
processSteps: Complete sharing assessment; approve agreement or DSA; assess privacy and sovereignty risks; configure controls; test enforcement; monitor partner compliance.
responsible: Business Owner; Data Owner; Partner Manager; Integration Delivery Lead; Security Architect
consulted: Legal; Privacy Officer; Chief Data Officer; Protective Security; Procurement; partner security lead
informed: Connected partner; Service Owner; Cyber Security Operations; Audit and Assurance
exceptionsPermitted: No data exchange before lawful pathway and agreement requirements are confirmed.
exceptionProcess: Pause release and escalate to Legal, Privacy, Data Governance and Protective Security where the sharing pathway or recipient controls are uncertain.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Data Officer or delegate, with Legal and Privacy endorsement
verification: Review approved agreement, data flow, recipient controls, privacy assessment, cross-border assessment and release gate evidence.
evidence: Data sharing agreement; recipient list; field mapping; privacy assessment; cross-border or sovereignty assessment; control test results; logs.
auditFrequency: Before each external sharing release, after material change and annually
relatedPolicies: Data Sharing Policy; Privacy Policy; Third Party Risk Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Data Sharing Agreement Procedure; External Partner Onboarding Procedure; Secure Transfer Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New recipient; new country or hosting location; new purpose; agreement change; partner incident; legal change.
notes: Agreement obligations should be translated into enforceable technical controls, not left as contract text only.

title: Privacy, personal information, identifiers and sensitive health/identity data
obligationDescription: Integrations involving personal information, health information, healthcare identifiers, government identifiers, Digital ID attributes or biometric and restricted identity data must complete privacy-by-design assessment, collect, use or disclose only approved fields for an authorised purpose, issue required notices or consent controls, protect information in transit, at rest and in logs, limit retention or de-identify it, restrict and review access, and prohibit My Health Record or restricted data handling unless expressly authorised and approved.
requirement: Integrations that handle personal, health, identity, Digital ID, biometric or other sensitive data must apply privacy by design. They must use only the minimum approved fields, give required notices or consent choices, protect data in transit, at rest and in logs, restrict access, and retain or de-identify data only as approved.
obligationRef:

otherStandards: Privacy Act APPs; Digital ID Act 2024; Healthcare Identifiers Act 2010; My Health Records Act 2012; OAIC guidance.
controlObjective: Protect personal and sensitive information across the full integration lifecycle.
threat: Privacy breach, over-collection, unauthorised identifier use, exposure of health or biometric data, consent failure and excessive retention.
applicability: All integrations that handle personal information, health information, government identifiers, Digital ID attributes, biometrics or other sensitive participant, provider or staff data.
excluded: Only integrations that have a documented assessment confirming no personal or sensitive information is processed.
guidance: Complete privacy-by-design assessment early. Minimise fields, document notices and consents, protect logs, restrict access, define retention, and prohibit restricted data handling unless expressly authorised.
technicalControls: Data minimisation rules; consent or notice controls; tokenisation or masking; encryption; role-based or attribute-based access; secure logging; retention and de-identification controls.
processSteps: Complete privacy threshold assessment or PIA; approve field list; configure notices or consent; test access and logging; review retention and access regularly.
responsible: Business Owner; Data Owner; System Owner; Integration Delivery Lead; Security Architect
consulted: Legal; Chief Data Officer; Cyber Security; Records; Digital ID or health information SME
informed: Service Owner; connected partner; complaints and incident teams; audit and assurance
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to Privacy Act, Digital ID, healthcare identifier or My Health Record restrictions.
exceptionProcess: For implementation control gaps, document equivalent safeguards, residual risk, expiry date and remediation. Do not proceed where use or disclosure is not authorised.
exceptionAuthority: Privacy Officer and General Counsel or delegate, with CISO endorsement for security controls
verification: Review PIA or privacy assessment, field mapping, consent or notice evidence, access reviews, retention settings and log samples.
evidence: Privacy threshold assessment or PIA; data minimisation record; consent or notice design; access review; retention schedule; encryption and logging evidence.
auditFrequency: Before go-live, after material change and at least annually for integrations with sensitive data
relatedPolicies: Privacy Policy; Data Governance Policy; Information Security Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Privacy Impact Assessment Procedure; Data Minimisation Guide; Sensitive Information Handling Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New personal data field; change in purpose; new recipient; consent model change; privacy incident; legal change.
notes: Privacy requirements apply to logs, test data, caches and analytics copies as well as primary payloads.

title: Secure engineering controls, identity, secrets, encryption and monitoring
obligationDescription: Integration code, platforms, identities, credentials, endpoints and data flows must implement secure engineering and control baselines, including secure development, dependency and configuration checks, unique least-privilege identities, approved secret and token handling, encryption and managed keys, gateway and boundary protections, logging and monitoring, Protective DNS or equivalent malicious-endpoint controls, vulnerability disclosure and remediation, cryptography readiness and cyber threat intelligence integration where applicable.
requirement: Integration platforms, code and interfaces must be securely designed, built, tested and operated. They must use approved identity, least privilege, secrets management, encryption, gateway controls, logging, monitoring, vulnerability management and threat detection.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 108 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
PSPF - 115 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs

threat: Credential theft, insecure APIs, weak encryption, exploitable code, malicious endpoints, unpatched components and undetected compromise.
applicability: All integration code, middleware, APIs, gateways, service accounts, secrets, endpoints, data stores and monitoring components.
excluded: None for ICT integrations. Approved legacy constraints must be documented as risk exceptions with compensating controls.
guidance: Apply secure design and threat modelling, then enforce security checks in build and release pipelines. Use approved patterns for identity, secrets, encryption, gateways, logging and vulnerability remediation.
technicalControls: Secure SDLC; SAST, DAST and dependency scanning; secrets vault; OAuth/OIDC or mTLS as approved; API gateway; encryption; SIEM logging; vulnerability and threat monitoring.
processSteps: Complete threat model; review design; scan code and dependencies; remediate critical findings; approve secrets and keys; test logging and alerts; monitor in production.
responsible: Integration Engineering Lead; Platform Owner; Cyber Security Operations; Security Architect
consulted: CISO delegate; Enterprise Architecture; Privacy; Data Owner; Supplier security lead
informed: Service operations; incident response team; connected partners; audit and assurance
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, only with documented compensating controls and risk acceptance.
exceptionProcess: Record the unmet control, compensating control, risk rating, remediation plan and expiry date before release or continued operation.
exceptionAuthority: CISO or delegated security authority, with System Owner acceptance of residual risk
verification: Review pipeline results, security design, penetration test or assurance outcomes, configuration checks, vulnerability status and monitoring evidence.
evidence: Threat model; security test reports; scan results; key and secret register; gateway configuration; logging and alert evidence; vulnerability remediation record.
auditFrequency: At each major release, monthly for vulnerabilities and annually for control assurance
relatedPolicies: Information Security Policy; Secure Development Policy; Vulnerability Management Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Secure Coding Standard; API Security Standard; Secrets Management Procedure; Logging and Monitoring Standard
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New threat; critical vulnerability; architecture change; new authentication pattern; security incident; control failure.
notes: Security controls should be automated in delivery pipelines wherever practical.

title: API design, interoperability, reuse and service consistency
obligationDescription: NDIA integrations and APIs must use approved Australian Government and NDIA design patterns, including OpenAPI specifications, catalogue registration, reusable interfaces where safe and lawful, consistent naming, payload, pagination, error, versioning and lifecycle patterns, controlled change and deprecation, and connection patterns that reduce repeat data requests and support reliable digital services.
requirement: APIs and integrations must use approved government and NDIA design patterns so they are secure, consistent, reusable and easy to support. They must be registered, documented with OpenAPI or equivalent specifications, versioned, tested and decommissioned using a controlled process.
obligationRef:

otherStandards: Australian Government API Standard; Digital Experience Policy; Digital Service Standard; Digital Access Standard.

threat: Duplicated interfaces, inconsistent error handling, unmanaged versions, poor discoverability, weak service reliability and avoidable data collection.
applicability: All NDIA APIs, service interfaces, event integrations and reusable integration patterns, including supplier-built interfaces.
excluded: Temporary or one-off interfaces still require approval, documentation and a retirement date before exclusion from reusable API standards.
guidance: Use approved API patterns, naming, schema, pagination, error handling, versioning and lifecycle rules. Register APIs in the catalogue and document them before release.
technicalControls: OpenAPI specification; API catalogue entry; schema validation; versioning; throttling; gateway policies; standard error codes; deprecation and retirement controls.
processSteps: Design to approved patterns; complete architecture review; publish specification; test contract and backward compatibility; approve deprecation; notify consumers.
responsible: API Product Owner; Integration Architect; Delivery Lead; Platform Owner
consulted: Enterprise Architecture; Cyber Security; Data Owner; Service Design; Accessibility Lead
informed: API consumers; operations teams; connected partners; service desk
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, only where a different pattern is justified and approved before release.
exceptionProcess: Document the design variance, reason, risks, consumer impact, support model and retirement plan in the architecture decision record.
exceptionAuthority: Architecture Review Board or delegated Chief Architect, with Cyber Security endorsement where controls are affected
verification: Review API catalogue, specification, architecture decision records, test results, version history and deprecation notices.
evidence: OpenAPI or interface specification; catalogue entry; design review; test results; version plan; consumer notification; deprecation plan.
auditFrequency: At release, at deprecation and annually for published APIs
relatedPolicies: ICT Integration Policy; Enterprise Architecture Policy; Digital Service Policy; Information Security Policy
relatedProcedures: API Design Standard; API Catalogue Procedure; Architecture Review Procedure; Service Design Guide
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New API standard; new integration pattern; major consumer impact; version change; reliability issue; audit finding.
notes: Reuse must remain lawful and safe; do not reuse interfaces in ways that create new data sharing purposes without approval.

title: Cloud, hosting, gateway, regulated infrastructure and resilience
obligationDescription: Integrations using cloud, hosting, gateways, Security Service Edge, data centres, connected devices or regulated critical infrastructure services must use approved or certified providers where required, review current IRAP or equivalent assurance, define shared cloud controls and sovereignty or data residency risks, protect internet-connected and classified flows through approved gateway or SSE capabilities, maintain exit, portability and continuity arrangements, identify SOCI and Systems of Government Significance obligations and third-party data processing notifications, and include critical assets in required risk management programs.
requirement: Integrations hosted in cloud, gateway, data centre, regulated infrastructure or connected-device environments must use approved hosting and security arrangements. NDIA must confirm assurance, shared controls, data location, resilience, exit and continuity requirements before use.

guidance: Confirm approved hosting, current assurance and shared responsibility before onboarding. Define data location, gateway controls, resilience, backup, exit, portability and SOCI or cyber reporting obligations.
technicalControls: Approved hosting; IRAP or equivalent assurance; network segmentation; secure gateway or SSE; encryption and key management; backup and recovery; monitoring; exit and portability controls.
processSteps: Assess hosting model; review assurance; define shared controls; record data location; complete resilience and exit plan; test recovery; monitor provider obligations.
responsible: Cloud Service Owner; Infrastructure Lead; Security Architect; Supplier Manager; Business Continuity Lead
consulted: CISO delegate; Enterprise Architecture; Procurement; Legal; Data Owner; Protective Security
informed: Operations teams; incident response; connected partners; audit and assurance

exceptionProcess: Document the hosting or resilience gap, business impact, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation before onboarding or continued operation.

verification: Review hosting approval, assurance reports, architecture, shared responsibility model, resilience test and exit plan.
evidence: Hosting approval; IRAP or assurance report; shared controls matrix; data residency assessment; resilience test; backup evidence; exit plan; SOCI assessment if applicable.
auditFrequency: Before onboarding, after material change and annually; resilience testing at least annually for critical integrations
relatedPolicies: Cloud and Hosting Policy; Information Security Policy; Business Continuity Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Cloud Security Assessment Procedure; Hosting Approval Process; Disaster Recovery Test Procedure; Exit Planning Guide
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: Provider assurance change; hosting location change; outage; cyber incident; SOCI classification change; major architecture change.
notes: Cloud responsibility should be explicit so control gaps are not assumed to be covered by the provider.

title: Supplier, procurement, contract and assurance controls
obligationDescription: Procurement, contracts, interface agreements and supplier onboarding for integration services must assess whole-of-life value and security, privacy, hosting, records, accessibility and supply-chain risks; use secure and verifiable suppliers; include proportionate control clauses and flow-down requirements; require evidence, audit rights and IRAP or equivalent assurance where relevant; manage foreign ownership, control or influence, subcontracting, offshore access and lifecycle risk; and define secure transition, termination, data return or destruction and access revocation.
requirement: Supplier and procurement arrangements for integrations must include security, privacy, records, accessibility, hosting and supply-chain controls for the full lifecycle. Contracts must require evidence, audit rights, flow-down obligations, incident notification, secure transition, data return or destruction and access removal.

excluded: None for supplier-delivered or supplier-supported integrations. Low-value procurements may use a proportionate assessment but must still address mandatory controls.
guidance: Assess whole-of-life risk before purchase and include control clauses that can be verified. Require supplier evidence and apply flow-down obligations to subcontractors and offshore access.
technicalControls: Supplier security assessment; contract control clauses; audit rights; subcontractor approval; privileged access controls; secure transition; data return or destruction; access revocation.
processSteps: Complete procurement risk assessment; include required clauses; assess supplier evidence; approve subcontractors; monitor performance; confirm secure exit and access removal.
responsible: Procurement Lead; Supplier Manager; System Owner; Integration Delivery Lead; Security Architect
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Records; Cyber Security; Accessibility Lead; Business Owner
informed: Supplier; operations teams; connected partners; audit and assurance
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, only with documented procurement, legal and security risk acceptance.
exceptionProcess: Record the contract or supplier control gap, compensating controls, business justification, expiry date and remediation or exit plan.
exceptionAuthority: Procurement delegate and Contract Owner, with CISO endorsement for security gaps and Legal endorsement for contract gaps
verification: Review procurement records, contract clauses, supplier assurance evidence, subcontractor approvals, access reviews and exit evidence.
evidence: Procurement risk assessment; signed contract or agreement; supplier assurance report; clause checklist; audit evidence; access review; data return or destruction certificate.
auditFrequency: Before contract award, at onboarding, annually and before contract exit or renewal
relatedPolicies: Procurement Policy; Third Party Risk Policy; Information Security Policy; Privacy Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Supplier Security Assessment Procedure; Contract Clause Checklist; Supplier Offboarding Procedure; Access Revocation Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New supplier; contract variation; subcontractor change; offshore access; incident; renewal; exit; audit finding.
notes: Contract controls should be measurable so NDIA can request evidence and enforce remediation.

requirement: Integration owners and suppliers must be able to detect, report, contain and recover from security, privacy, data quality, ransomware, safeguarding and critical infrastructure incidents. They must preserve evidence, meet notification timeframes and close lessons learned.

controlObjective: Ensure integration incidents are found, escalated, contained, reported and remediated on time.
threat: Delayed incident response, missed statutory notifications, lost evidence, repeated control failures and unmanaged supplier or partner incidents.
applicability: All active NDIA integrations and suppliers or partners that operate, host, monitor or support those integrations.
excluded: None. Incident and notification obligations apply to all integration-related events, including supplier and partner events.

technicalControls: Centralised logs; SIEM alerts; incident runbooks; evidence preservation; immutable or protected logs; backup and recovery; contact lists; notification workflow.
processSteps: Monitor events; triage incidents; preserve evidence; contain impact; assess notification obligations; notify required parties; recover; complete lessons learned and remediation.
