responsible: System Owner; Cyber Security Operations; Privacy Officer; Supplier Manager; Business Continuity Lead
consulted: Legal; CISO delegate; Communications; Records; Data Owner; NDIS Commission liaison if relevant
informed: Senior Responsible Officer; connected partners; service desk; audit and assurance; affected business areas
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to statutory reporting or evidence preservation obligations.
exceptionProcess: Escalate immediately to the Incident Manager, Legal, Privacy and CISO delegate where notification obligations or timeframes are uncertain.
exceptionAuthority: CISO or delegated Incident Executive, with Privacy Officer and Legal authority for reportability decisions
verification: Review incident plans, notification workflow, log coverage, supplier clauses, exercise outcomes and closed remediation actions.
evidence: Incident response plan; runbook; contact list; logging evidence; supplier notification clauses; exercise report; incident record; lessons learned closure evidence.
auditFrequency: At least annually through exercises and after every major incident
relatedPolicies: Cyber Incident Response Policy; Privacy Policy; Business Continuity Policy; Third Party Risk Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Incident Response Procedure; Notifiable Data Breach Procedure; Supplier Incident Notification Procedure; Post-Incident Review Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: Incident; exercise finding; new supplier; new statutory reporting obligation; logging change; critical infrastructure status change.
notes: Supplier and partner incident timeframes should be shorter than NDIA statutory notification deadlines.

title: Records, retention, FOI, auditability and transparency
obligationDescription: Integrations must create and preserve reliable records and audit trails showing exchanged data, source, recipient, timestamp, purpose, authority, sensitivity, version, outcome and system or user activity; retain or dispose of records only under approved authorities; support export, FOI, privacy, audit and legal retrieval and explanations; and publish appropriate operational information without exposing sensitive security, privacy, commercial or partner information.
requirement: Integrations must create reliable records and audit trails that show what data was exchanged, why, by whom, when and under what authority. Records must be retained, disposed of, exported and retrieved in line with Archives, FOI, privacy, audit and legal requirements.
obligationRef:
ARC-31 (Archives Act): Archives Act 1983; NAA Information Management Standard
ARC-32 (Archives Act): Archives Act 1983 - disposal
ARC-33 (Archives Act): Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard
ARC-34 (Archives Act): NAA information management expectations for interoperability
FOI-20 (FOI Act): Freedom of Information Act 1982
FOI-21 (FOI Act): OAIC FOI Guidelines under s 93A
FOI-22 (FOI Act): FOI Act - Information Publication Scheme
FOI-23 (FOI Act): FOI Act exemptions
ismControls: ASD ISM domains: event logging; audit trails; time synchronisation; backup and recovery; access control; system administration.
otherStandards: Archives Act 1983; National Archives information management standards; Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard; Freedom of Information Act 1982; OAIC FOI Guidelines.
controlObjective: Create trustworthy integration records that can support audit, FOI, privacy, legal and operational needs.
threat: Missing records, inability to explain decisions or data flows, unauthorised disposal, weak audit trails and inappropriate disclosure of sensitive records.
applicability: All NDIA integrations that exchange, transform, create, update, store or delete Agency records or evidence of system and user activity.
excluded: No production integration is excluded. Logging details may be minimised only where privacy or security requires it and Records approves the recordkeeping approach.
guidance: Define recordkeeping and audit requirements during design. Capture source, recipient, timestamp, purpose, authority, sensitivity, version, outcome and system or user activity without exposing unnecessary sensitive data.
technicalControls: Audit logging; time synchronisation; retention labels; protected log storage; export capability; search and retrieval; tamper-evident evidence store; backup controls.
processSteps: Identify records; map metadata; approve retention and disposal; configure logs; test retrieval and export; review logs and retention compliance.
responsible: System Owner; Data Owner; Integration Delivery Lead; Operations Lead; Records Officer
consulted: FOI Officer; Privacy; Legal; Cyber Security; Audit and Assurance
informed: Business Owner; service operations; connected partners where records are shared
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to statutory records and FOI obligations.
exceptionProcess: If logging or retention creates privacy, security or feasibility issues, seek Records, Privacy, Legal and Cyber Security agreement on an alternative approach before release.
exceptionAuthority: Records Authority or delegate, with Legal and Privacy endorsement where required
verification: Review metadata mapping, retention settings, disposal authority, retrieval tests, audit trail samples and FOI support evidence.
evidence: Recordkeeping assessment; metadata mapping; retention schedule; disposal authority; audit logs; retrieval test; FOI search evidence if applicable.
auditFrequency: Annually and after any major change to data flows, retention or logging
relatedPolicies: Records Management Policy; FOI Policy; Privacy Policy; Information Security Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Recordkeeping Metadata Procedure; Retention and Disposal Procedure; FOI Search Procedure; Logging Standard
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New record type; retention authority change; FOI issue; audit finding; logging architecture change; legal hold.
notes: Audit trails should explain data movement without storing unnecessary sensitive payload content.

title: Accessibility, inclusive communications and non-discrimination
obligationDescription: Participant or public-facing integration journeys, generated content, notices and authentication flows must be accessible, inclusive and easy to understand, meet applicable WCAG and Australian Government accessibility requirements, provide clear support paths and approved alternatives, and include accessibility requirements in design, testing, procurement and acceptance criteria.
requirement: Participant and public-facing integration journeys, messages, notices and sign-in flows must be accessible, inclusive and easy to understand. They must meet applicable accessibility standards, include support and alternative channels, and be tested before release.
obligationRef:
NDIS-46 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act 2013, s 7
DSS-26 (Digital Service Standard): Digital Service Standard - user-centred and inclusive design
DSS-27 (Digital Service Standard): Digital Access Standard
DID-13 (Digital ID Act): Digital ID Act 2024 - accessibility and alternatives
DDA-14 (Disability Discrimination Act): Disability Discrimination Act 1992
DDA-15 (Disability Discrimination Act): Australian Government web accessibility requirements / WCAG 2.2
DDA-16 (Disability Discrimination Act): Australian Government Style Manual - accessibility and inclusion
DDA-17 (Disability Discrimination Act): AHRC equal access guidance
DDA-18 (Disability Discrimination Act): Digital accessibility in procurement
ismControls: ASD ISM domains where applicable: authentication; session management; access control; logging for accessible digital channels.
otherStandards: NDIS Act 2013 section 7; Digital Service Standard; Digital Access Standard; Digital ID Act 2024; Disability Discrimination Act 1992; WCAG 2.2; Australian Government Style Manual.
controlObjective: Ensure integrations do not exclude participants, providers or the public from accessible digital services.
threat: Inaccessible service journeys, discrimination risk, failed authentication, unclear notices, poor support paths and reduced participant trust.
applicability: All participant, provider, public or staff-facing integration touchpoints, notifications, generated content, consent flows and authentication journeys.
excluded: Back-end system-to-system integrations with no user-facing journey are excluded from accessibility presentation requirements but still need accessible support and incident communications where relevant.
guidance: Include accessibility and plain English acceptance criteria from design. Test with assistive technologies and real user needs, and provide supported alternatives where digital access is not suitable.
technicalControls: WCAG testing; accessible forms and errors; accessible MFA or sign-in options; plain English content; captions or alternatives; support channel links; procurement acceptance checks.
processSteps: Assess user impact; include accessibility requirements; design and test with assistive technology; remediate issues; approve alternative channels; confirm supplier evidence.
responsible: Service Designer; Product Owner; Integration Delivery Lead; Accessibility Lead; Supplier Manager
consulted: Participants or user representatives; Legal; Privacy; Digital ID SME; Communications; Cyber Security
informed: Contact centre; service desk; operations teams; connected partners
exceptionsPermitted: Only where an equivalent accessible alternative is approved for a time-bound period.
exceptionProcess: Record the accessibility gap, affected users, alternative channel, remediation plan and expiry date before release or continued operation.
exceptionAuthority: Service Owner and Accessibility Lead, with Legal input where discrimination risk is present
verification: Review accessibility test results, plain English content review, user testing, procurement evidence and alternative channel approval.
evidence: Accessibility assessment; WCAG test report; user testing evidence; content review; supplier conformance evidence; alternative channel plan.
auditFrequency: Before public release, after material user journey change and annually for high-use services
relatedPolicies: Accessibility Policy; Digital Service Policy; Privacy Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Accessibility Testing Procedure; Plain English Content Guide; Inclusive Service Design Guide; Digital Identity User Support Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: Accessibility standard change; user complaint; journey redesign; new authentication method; supplier change; audit finding.
notes: Accessibility is a release criterion, not a post-release enhancement.

title: Data governance, quality, matching and Indigenous data safeguards
obligationDescription: Integration datasets must have accountable data owners, approved definitions, schemas, validation rules, lineage and lifecycle controls; critical integrations must reconcile failed, duplicate, stale or conflicting records; data matching must have an approved purpose, authority, protocol, minimum fields, secure transfer, quality thresholds, transparency, human review and statutory-regime compliance; and integrations involving Indigenous data must apply culturally safe governance and safeguards.
requirement: Integration data must have a clear owner, approved definitions, schemas, validation rules, lineage and lifecycle controls. Critical data flows must check for failed, duplicate, stale or conflicting records, and any data matching must be lawful, transparent, fair and reviewable.
obligationRef:
PA-45 (Privacy Act APPs): APPs 10, 12 and 13
AGDGF-01 (AG Data Governance Framework): Australian Government Data Governance Framework
AGDGF-02 (AG Data Governance Framework): Data lifecycle governance
AGDGF-03 (AG Data Governance Framework): Metadata and common definitions
AGDGF-04 (AG Data Governance Framework): Data quality governance
AGDGF-05 (AG Data Governance Framework): Framework for Governance of Indigenous Data
OAIC-DMG-01 (OAIC Data Matching Guidelines): OAIC data matching guidelines
OAIC-DMG-02 (OAIC Data Matching Guidelines): OAIC data matching protocol expectations
OAIC-DMG-03 (OAIC Data Matching Guidelines): APPs and OAIC matching controls
OAIC-DMG-04 (OAIC Data Matching Guidelines): OAIC fairness expectations
OAIC-DMG-05 (OAIC Data Matching Guidelines): Data-matching Program (Assistance and Tax) Act 1990
ismControls: ASD ISM domains: access control; input validation; data integrity; logging and monitoring; backup and recovery; security documentation.
otherStandards: Privacy Act APPs 10, 12 and 13; Australian Government Data Governance Framework; Framework for Governance of Indigenous Data; OAIC Data Matching Guidelines; Data-matching Program Act where applicable.
controlObjective: Keep integration data accurate, understandable, traceable and fit for approved use.
threat: Poor data quality, duplicate or stale records, incorrect matching, unfair outcomes, weak lineage and culturally unsafe handling of Indigenous data.
applicability: All integration datasets, schemas, reference data, data matching processes, reconciliation routines and critical data exchanges.
excluded: None for integration data. Low-risk data flows may use proportionate controls approved by the Data Owner.
guidance: Assign data ownership and define data quality rules before build. Use validation, reconciliation and human review where decisions, payments, eligibility or participant outcomes may be affected.
technicalControls: Data catalogue; schema registry; validation rules; lineage capture; reconciliation; duplicate detection; exception queues; matching protocol controls; audit logging.
processSteps: Approve data definitions; document lineage; set quality thresholds; test validation; approve matching protocol; monitor exceptions; review corrections and complaints.
accountable: Chief Data Officer or delegated Data Owner
responsible: Data Steward; System Owner; Integration Delivery Lead; Business Owner; Analytics or Matching Lead
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Indigenous Data Governance SME; Cyber Security; Records; affected business areas
informed: Operations teams; data consumers; connected partners; audit and assurance
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, only for proportionate data quality controls; no exception to lawful and fair data matching requirements.
exceptionProcess: Document the data quality or matching gap, affected decisions, compensating controls, monitoring, owner and remediation date.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Data Officer or delegate, with Privacy and Legal endorsement for data matching exceptions
verification: Review data catalogue, schema, quality rules, matching protocol, reconciliation results, exception handling and lineage evidence.
evidence: Data owner record; data dictionary; schema; quality rules; lineage map; reconciliation reports; matching protocol; exception and correction records.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for critical data flows and annually for all active integration datasets
relatedPolicies: Data Governance Policy; Privacy Policy; Records Management Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Data Quality Procedure; Data Matching Protocol Template; Metadata Standard; Indigenous Data Governance Guide
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New data source; quality threshold breach; matching change; complaint; Indigenous data use; legal or policy change; audit finding.
notes: Data quality controls should be stronger where the integration affects payments, eligibility or participant outcomes.

section: 15. Provider, partner and Digital ID access lifecycle
title: Provider, partner and Digital ID onboarding/access lifecycle
obligationDescription: Provider, partner and Digital ID integrations must verify identity, eligibility, accreditation or approval, authority, relying-party obligations and assurance level before access; connected users must use channels only for authorised NDIS purposes, protect participant rights and privacy, maintain required records, access identity verification services only via approved facilities, and support prompt suspension, restriction or revocation when status, consent, conduct, security or safeguarding risk changes.
requirement: Provider, partner and Digital ID integrations must verify identity, eligibility, accreditation, approval, authority and assurance level before access is granted. Access must be limited to approved NDIS purposes and quickly suspended, restricted or revoked when status, consent, conduct or risk changes.
obligationRef:
DID-10 (Digital ID Act): Digital ID Act 2024 - accreditation and approval
DID-14 (Digital ID Act): Identity Verification Services Act 2023
NDIS-QSC-01 (NDIS QSC Provider Rules): Provider Registration and Practice Standards Rules 2018
NDIS-QSC-02 (NDIS QSC Provider Rules): NDIS Code of Conduct Rules 2018
NDIS-QSC-03 (NDIS QSC Provider Rules): NDIS Practice Standards - governance and operational management
NDIS-QSC-05 (NDIS QSC Provider Rules): NDIS Code of Conduct - privacy and participant rights
NDIS-QSC-06 (NDIS QSC Provider Rules): NDIS provider compliance monitoring
ismControls: ASD ISM domains: authentication; authorisation; privileged access; identity lifecycle management; logging and monitoring; cryptography.
otherStandards: Digital ID Act 2024; Identity Verification Services Act 2023; NDIS Provider Registration and Practice Standards; NDIS Code of Conduct; NDIS provider compliance monitoring.
controlCategory: Provider, partner and Digital ID access lifecycle
controlObjective: Ensure only verified and authorised providers, partners and Digital ID parties access NDIA integrations for approved purposes.
threat: Unauthorised provider access, identity fraud, excessive privileges, stale access, consent failure, participant rights impacts and partner misuse.
applicability: All integrations used by providers, partners, relying parties, identity verification services, Digital ID services or external users with NDIA access.
excluded: None where external or federated identities can access NDIA data or services.
guidance: Verify identity, eligibility, accreditation and authority before access. Bind access to approved purpose, assurance level and status, and automate suspension or revocation when risk changes.
technicalControls: Identity proofing; federation or approved identity integration; MFA; RBAC or ABAC; entitlement checks; consent and status checks; lifecycle automation; audit logging.
processSteps: Onboard approved parties; verify authority and assurance; assign least privilege; monitor conduct and status; review access; suspend or revoke promptly when triggers occur.
responsible: Provider Relationship Owner; System Owner; Integration Delivery Lead; Access Administrator; Security Operations
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Digital ID SME; NDIS Commission liaison; Data Owner; Cyber Security
informed: Providers or partners; service desk; operations teams; audit and assurance
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to identity, accreditation, approval or authority checks.
exceptionProcess: Use approved emergency access only where necessary, time-bound, logged, monitored and reviewed after use. Do not bypass statutory Digital ID or identity verification restrictions.
exceptionAuthority: IAM Owner and System Owner, with CISO and Privacy endorsement for emergency or high-risk access
verification: Review onboarding evidence, identity assurance, entitlement rules, access reviews, suspension records and audit logs.
evidence: Identity and eligibility verification; accreditation record; access approval; entitlement matrix; consent or authority evidence; access review; suspension or revocation logs.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for external access and after any provider, partner or Digital ID status change
relatedPolicies: Identity and Access Management Policy; Privacy Policy; Provider Access Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: External User Onboarding Procedure; Access Review Procedure; Digital ID Integration Guide; Emergency Access Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: Provider status change; accreditation change; consent change; conduct issue; identity incident; Digital ID law or standard change.
notes: Access lifecycle controls should be automated where external status or consent changes can be detected.

title: Fraud, transaction integrity and investigation
obligationDescription: High-risk integrations that create, change, validate or analyse provider, financial, entitlement, payment or participant data must include fraud, corruption and integrity controls by design, including input validation, segregation of duties, exception handling, anomaly detection, monitoring, recovery support, tamper-evident investigation records and authorised investigator access.
requirement: High-risk integrations that affect payments, entitlements, providers, financial data or participant data must include fraud and integrity controls from the start. They must validate inputs, separate duties, manage exceptions, detect unusual activity, preserve evidence and support authorised investigations.
obligationRef:
CFCCF-01 (Fraud and Corruption Framework): PGPA Rule 2014, s 10
CFCCF-02 (Fraud and Corruption Framework): Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024
CFCCF-03 (Fraud and Corruption Framework): Fraud control good practice - segregation and validation
CFCCF-04 (Fraud and Corruption Framework): Fraud detection and analytics controls
CFCCF-05 (Fraud and Corruption Framework): Evidence preservation for investigations
ismControls: ASD ISM domains: access control; segregation of duties; event logging; monitoring and alerting; evidence protection; data integrity.
otherStandards: PGPA Rule 2014 section 10; Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024; fraud control good practice for validation, segregation, analytics and evidence preservation.
controlObjective: Prevent, detect and investigate fraud, corruption and integrity risks in high-risk integration transactions.
threat: Fraudulent payment or entitlement changes, provider misconduct, manipulated data, collusion, false claims, weak investigation evidence and undetected anomalies.
applicability: All high-risk integrations that create, change, validate or analyse provider, financial, entitlement, payment or participant data.
excluded: Low-risk read-only integrations may use proportionate controls if the Fraud Control Owner and Data Owner record the assessment.
guidance: Assess fraud and integrity risk during design. Build controls into transaction flows, exception handling, monitoring and evidence capture rather than relying only on after-the-fact review.
technicalControls: Input validation; segregation of duties; transaction limits; exception queues; anomaly detection; tamper-evident logs; restricted investigator access; evidence retention.
processSteps: Complete fraud risk assessment; define controls and thresholds; test exception handling; monitor anomalies; investigate alerts; preserve evidence; remediate control weaknesses.
responsible: Business Owner; System Owner; Data Owner; Analytics Lead; Security Operations; Investigation Lead
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Chief Risk Officer; Internal Audit; Cyber Security; Records
informed: Executive risk committee; operations teams; audit and assurance; relevant partner controls teams
exceptionsPermitted: No exception where a control bypass would create unacceptable fraud or corruption risk.
exceptionProcess: Document the control gap, fraud risk, compensating monitoring, expiry date and remediation plan. Emergency bypasses must be logged and reviewed after use.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Risk Officer or delegated Fraud Control authority, with Business Owner and CISO endorsement where ICT controls are affected
verification: Review fraud risk assessment, control design, transaction monitoring, exception handling, access reviews and investigation evidence handling.
evidence: Fraud risk assessment; control matrix; validation rules; segregation of duties review; anomaly reports; exception logs; investigation evidence register.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for high-risk transaction integrations and after any major fraud or integrity incident
relatedPolicies: Fraud and Corruption Control Policy; Risk Management Policy; Information Security Policy; ICT Integration Policy
relatedProcedures: Fraud Risk Assessment Procedure; Transaction Monitoring Guide; Investigation Evidence Handling Procedure; Access Review Procedure
reviewFrequency: At least annually and before material change
reviewTriggers: New fraud typology; payment or entitlement change; anomaly spike; investigation finding; audit finding; control bypass.
notes: Fraud controls should be designed with privacy and fairness safeguards, especially where analytics or matching is used.

title: Service governance, portfolio, value and performance
obligationDescription: NDIA must govern each ICT service through a defined owner, delegated decision rights, service purpose, portfolio roadmap, transition approval, performance measures and benefits evidence that support executive, Board and whole-of-government reporting.
requirement: NDIA must have a named owner for every ICT service. The owner must define the service purpose, expected value, performance measures, roadmap and decision points, and must keep evidence that the service is meeting business, participant and government reporting needs.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 22 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
NDIS-51 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act 2013 section 118 - NDIA functions
NDIS-52 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act 2013 section 177 - delegation
PGPA-52 (PGPA): PGPA Act 2013 section 15 - duty to govern the entity
PGPA-55 (PGPA): PGPA Act 2013 sections 35 and 37-39 - corporate planning and performance
PGPA-57 (PGPA): PGPA Act 2013 section 46 and PGPA Rule annual reporting requirements
IOF-09 (IOF): Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework - whole-of-government investment lifecycle
IOF-10 (IOF): IOF states - strategic planning and prioritisation
IOF-11 (IOF): IOF states - contestability and assurance
IOF-12 (IOF): IOF states - sourcing and operations
IOF-13 (IOF): Digital Capability Assessment Process and ICT Investment Approval Process
BMP-01 (Benefits Management): Benefits Management Policy - purpose and application
BMP-02 (Benefits Management): Benefits Management Policy Standard
BMP-03 (Benefits Management): Benefits Management Process - Identify, Analyse, Plan, Monitor and Realise, Review
BMP-04 (Benefits Management): Benefits Management Policy guidance - benefits are measurable and observable
BMP-05 (Benefits Management): Benefits Management Policy and IOF assurance
ismControls: ASD ISM control areas for cyber security governance, system authorisation, security documentation, audit logging and monitoring.
otherStandards: PGPA Act and Rule; PSPF; NDIS Act; Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework; Benefits Management Policy; ITIL 4; ISO/IEC 20000.
controlObjective: Ensure every ICT service has clear ownership, purpose, value, performance measures and governance evidence.
threat: Unclear ownership, duplicated services, poor value, weak performance reporting and unmanaged service retirement.
applicability: All NDIA ICT services, platforms, products and service portfolio decisions, including services delivered by suppliers.
excluded: None for services in the NDIA service portfolio. Shadow IT must be brought into scope when identified.
guidance: Maintain a service catalogue; assign a service owner; define purpose, value and performance measures; review roadmap decisions and benefits in governance forums.
technicalControls: Service catalogue; portfolio dashboard; KPI and SLA monitoring; benefits tracking; decision and approval records; audit logs.
processSteps: Create or update the service record; appoint the owner; agree measures; review the roadmap and benefits; report performance and decisions.
responsible: Service owners; ICT Service Management; Portfolio Management Office; Enterprise Architecture; supplier managers.
consulted: Business owners; Finance; Risk and Assurance; Cyber Security; Privacy; Procurement; suppliers where relevant.
informed: Executive governance forums; business stakeholders; service users; suppliers supporting the service.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved service governance exception.
exceptionProcess: Record the exception with reason, impact, compensating controls, owner and expiry date; review it through the ICT governance forum.
exceptionAuthority: CIO or delegated ICT governance forum.
verification: Review service catalogue records, governance minutes, KPI and benefits reports, roadmap evidence and service review outcomes.
evidence: Named service owner; service catalogue entry; service charter; KPIs and SLAs; roadmap; benefits register; governance decisions; service review report.
auditFrequency: Six-monthly and during the annual service review.
relatedPolicies: ICT Service Management Policy; Enterprise Portfolio Management Policy; Benefits Management Policy; ICT Governance Policy.
relatedProcedures: Service catalogue and service owner standard; portfolio governance procedure; benefits management guidance; performance reporting procedure.
reviewTriggers: New service, major change, service retirement, material performance issue, investment decision, audit finding or government reporting change.
notes: Use this requirement to make service ownership, value and reporting expectations clear in the policy.

title: Risk management, assurance, internal control and fraud prevention
obligationDescription: ICT service risks, including security, shared, supplier, residual, fraud and corruption risks, must be identified, assessed, assigned, treated, tested, monitored and reported within NDIA risk appetite, with exceptions and control gaps formally accepted and tracked.
requirement: NDIA must manage risks for every ICT service. Service owners must identify, assess, treat and report security, supplier, fraud, control and residual risks, and must record who accepts any risk that remains.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 36 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 37 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 38 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PGPA-53 (PGPA): PGPA Act 2013 section 16 - risk oversight and internal controls
CRMP-14 (Risk Management): PGPA Act 2013 section 16
CRMP-15 (Risk Management): Commonwealth Risk Management Policy - embedding risk management
CRMP-16 (Risk Management): Commonwealth Risk Management Policy - capability and accountability
CRMP-17 (Risk Management): RMG 211 - implementing the Commonwealth Risk Management Policy
CFCCF-06 (Fraud and Corruption): PGPA Rule 2014 section 10 - preventing, detecting and dealing with fraud and corruption
CFCCF-07 (Fraud and Corruption): Fraud and Corruption Rule - regular risk assessments
CFCCF-08 (Fraud and Corruption): Fraud and Corruption Rule - control plans and controls review
CFCCF-09 (Fraud and Corruption): Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework - awareness, reporting and response
CFCCF-10 (Fraud and Corruption): RMG 201 - preventing, detecting and dealing with fraud and corruption
ismControls: ASD ISM control areas for security risk management, control testing, exceptions, risk acceptance, audit logging and security reporting.
otherStandards: PGPA Act; Commonwealth Risk Management Policy; Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework; PSPF; ITIL 4 risk practices.
controlObjective: Ensure ICT service risks and controls are actively managed, tested, accepted and reported.
threat: Unmanaged risk, control failure, fraud or corruption, supplier weakness and unaccepted residual risk.
applicability: All NDIA ICT services and supporting suppliers, processes, risks, controls, exceptions and assurance activities.
excluded: None for ICT service risks. Risks outside ICT are managed under enterprise risk but must be linked where relevant.
guidance: Use the NDIA risk process; keep a service risk profile; test key controls; record fraud, supplier and security risks; escalate gaps and accepted residual risk.
technicalControls: Risk register; control testing records; issue register; fraud control plan linkage; supplier assurance records; exception tracking.
processSteps: Identify risks; assess rating; assign an owner; define treatment; test controls; accept residual risk; report and review.
accountable: CIO, with enterprise risk accountability supported by the Chief Risk Officer.
responsible: Service owners; Risk and Assurance; Cyber Security; Supplier Management; Fraud Control; ICT process owners.
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Internal Audit; Procurement; business owners; suppliers where relevant.
informed: Risk committees; executive sponsors; service governance forums; affected business areas.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by risk acceptance only.
exceptionProcess: Record the risk, treatment gap, compensating controls, residual rating, owner and review date in the risk and exception registers.
exceptionAuthority: CIO with Chief Risk Officer or delegated Risk Committee approval.
verification: Review the risk register, control tests, exception records, assurance reports and treatment plans.
evidence: Service risk profile; control test results; fraud and corruption risk assessment; supplier risk assessment; accepted risk record; assurance report.
auditFrequency: Quarterly, with formal assurance at least annually.
relatedPolicies: Enterprise Risk Management Policy; Fraud and Corruption Control Policy; ICT Security Policy; Supplier Risk Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: ICT risk assessment procedure; control testing plan; exception and risk acceptance procedure; fraud control plan.
reviewTriggers: New or changed service, control failure, fraud indicator, supplier issue, cyber incident, audit finding or risk appetite change.
notes: The policy should make risk acceptance visible and time limited, not informal or open ended.

title: Digital service design, accessibility, inclusion and user outcomes
obligationDescription: ICT services must be designed, delivered and improved around participant and user needs, accessibility, inclusion, safe digital experience, reliable support channels and reasonable alternatives where digital access is unsuitable.
requirement: NDIA must design and run ICT services around participant and user needs. Services must be accessible, inclusive, safe to use, reliable to support and have reasonable alternatives when digital channels are not suitable.
type: Digital service design and accessibility requirement
obligationRef:
NDIS-48 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act 2013 sections 3 and 4 - objects and general principles
DIG-11 (Digital Experience): Digital Experience Policy - coverage and supporting standards
DIG-12 (Digital Experience): Digital Service Standard criteria 1 and 2 - clear intent and know your user
DIG-13 (Digital Experience): Digital Service Standard criterion 3 - leave no one behind
DIG-14 (Digital Experience): Digital Service Standard criteria 4, 5 and 7 - connect services, build trust and do no harm
DIG-15 (Digital Experience): Digital Service Standard criteria 9 and 10 - monitor service and keep relevant
DIG-16 (Digital Experience): Digital Access, Inclusion and Performance Standards
DDA-19 (DDA Accessibility): DDA sections 5 and 6 - direct and indirect disability discrimination
DDA-20 (DDA Accessibility): DDA section 24 - goods, services and facilities
DDA-21 (DDA Accessibility): DDA section 29 - administration of Commonwealth laws and programs
DDA-22 (DDA Accessibility): Australian Human Rights Commission digital access guidelines
DDA-23 (DDA Accessibility): DDA section 60 - Action plans
ismControls: ASD ISM control areas for secure-by-design services, access control, privacy protection, availability, monitoring and service support.
otherStandards: NDIS Act; Digital Experience Policy; Digital Service Standard; Digital Access, Inclusion and Performance Standards; Disability Discrimination Act; WCAG.
controlObjective: Ensure ICT services are accessible, inclusive, safe and aligned to participant and user outcomes.
threat: Digital exclusion, inaccessible services, unsafe user journeys, poor participant outcomes and loss of trust.
applicability: All participant, provider, staff and public-facing ICT services and support channels.
excluded: Back-office technical components with no user impact may use simplified design evidence, but accessibility still applies where users interact.
guidance: Use user research, accessibility testing, plain language, assisted digital pathways and service analytics; include participants and support staff in design and improvement.
technicalControls: Accessibility testing tools; service analytics; assisted channel controls; feedback management; secure design checklists.
processSteps: Research users; design an accessible service; test with users; provide alternatives; monitor experience; improve the backlog.
accountable: CIO, with the responsible business owner for the service.
responsible: Digital service owners; UX and accessibility specialists; service desk; product managers; delivery teams.
consulted: Participants and representatives; Disability and Inclusion advisers; Privacy; Cyber Security; Legal; communications teams.
informed: Service users; support teams; business stakeholders; suppliers supporting user-facing services.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only where an accessible alternative is documented.
exceptionProcess: Document the accessibility or digital inclusion gap, user impact, alternative channel, remediation plan, owner and review date.
exceptionAuthority: CIO with Digital Experience and Accessibility Lead endorsement.
verification: Review service design evidence, accessibility tests, user feedback, service analytics and alternative channel arrangements.
evidence: User research findings; accessibility test results; service design assessment; feedback records; alternative channel plan; improvement backlog.
auditFrequency: At least annually and before any major service release.
relatedPolicies: Digital Experience Policy; Accessibility and Inclusion Policy; ICT Service Management Policy; Privacy Policy.
relatedProcedures: Digital service design procedure; accessibility testing checklist; user research and service performance guidance.
reviewTriggers: New user-facing service, major digital release, accessibility issue, complaint trend, policy change or service performance decline.
notes: The policy should require accessibility and inclusion to be built in, not checked only at the end.

section: 4. Information protection, privacy and lawful handling
title: Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure
obligationDescription: ICT services must protect classified, caveated, protected, personal and critical infrastructure information by applying lawful collection, access, use, disclosure, sharing, privacy governance, PIA, metadata, consent, security and disposal controls.
requirement: NDIA must protect personal, protected, classified and critical information handled by ICT services. Information must only be collected, accessed, used, shared, retained and disposed of where it is lawful, authorised, secure and auditable.
obligationRef:

ismControls: ASD ISM control areas for information classification, access control, cryptography, logging, data transfer, monitoring and secure disposal.
otherStandards: PSPF information classification and holdings; NDIS protected information rules; Privacy Act APPs; Australian Government Privacy Code; SOCI Act.
controlObjective: Ensure information handled by ICT services is lawful, secure, private and traceable.
threat: Privacy breach, unlawful disclosure, misuse of protected information, data loss and regulatory non-compliance.
applicability: All ICT services that collect, store, process, transmit, share or dispose of NDIA information.
excluded: None for NDIA information. Public information may use simplified controls but still needs integrity and records management.
guidance: Classify information; complete privacy assessment where needed; define lawful purpose; limit collection, access and sharing; log access; dispose under approved records and security rules.
technicalControls: Information classification; role-based access; MFA; encryption; logging; DLP or monitoring; secure transfer; secure disposal; privacy controls.
processSteps: Confirm authority; classify data; complete PIA where needed; approve access and sharing; monitor use; retain or dispose correctly.
accountable: CIO, with the Chief Privacy Officer for privacy obligations.
responsible: Service owners; Data owners; Privacy team; Cyber Security; Records Management; ICT Operations; suppliers where relevant.
consulted: Legal; Information Management; business owners; Security Adviser; data governance forums.
informed: Users handling the information; executive sponsors; affected business areas; suppliers that process NDIA information.
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to legal duties; operational exceptions require approval.
exceptionProcess: Document the legal basis, privacy and security risk, compensating controls, expiry date and remediation plan before any operational exception is used.
exceptionAuthority: CIO with Chief Privacy Officer and Legal endorsement.
verification: Review PIAs, access logs, classification records, sharing approvals, monitoring records and disposal evidence.
evidence: PIA or privacy threshold assessment; data handling record; classification; access approval; disclosure authority; audit logs; disposal certificate.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for high-risk services and annually for all others.
relatedPolicies: Privacy Policy; Information Security Policy; Records Management Policy; Data Governance Policy.
relatedProcedures: Privacy impact assessment procedure; information classification and handling guide; access control standard; disclosure approval process.
reviewFrequency: Annual or after privacy, security or information law change.
reviewTriggers: New data use, new integration, privacy complaint, data breach, classification change, legal change or audit finding.
notes: This requirement should be treated as a core policy obligation because NDIA services handle sensitive participant information.

title: Records, knowledge, FOI, publication, retention and evidence management
obligationDescription: ICT service records, knowledge articles, CMDB data, service decisions, FOI material, publication content and archival records must be accurate, searchable, secure, accessible, retained, transferred or disposed of only under approved records and information management controls.
requirement: NDIA must keep accurate and usable records for ICT services. Service records, knowledge articles, configuration data, decisions and FOI or publication material must be searchable, protected, retained and disposed of under approved records rules.
obligationRef:

FOI-27 (FOI and IPS): FOI Act section 10 - operational information
FOI-28 (FOI and IPS): FOI Act section 11C - disclosure log

otherStandards: FOI Act; Archives Act; National Archives records authorities; PSPF information disposal; PGPA records requirements; ITIL knowledge and configuration practices.
controlObjective: Ensure ICT service records and knowledge are accurate, findable, retained and disposed of correctly.
threat: Lost records, inaccurate service data, FOI failures, poor evidence, unauthorised disposal and knowledge loss.
applicability: All ICT service records, knowledge, CMDB data, FOI and publication material, operational decisions and archival records.
excluded: Transient system logs may follow approved log-retention schedules. Official records remain in scope.
guidance: Use approved recordkeeping tools; keep CMDB and knowledge data current; apply retention authorities; maintain FOI and publication evidence; control disposal.
technicalControls: EDRMS or approved records system; CMDB; knowledge base; retention labels; access controls; audit logs; disposal certificates.
processSteps: Capture the record; tag and classify it; keep it current; respond to FOI or publication needs; retain, transfer or dispose with approval.
accountable: CIO, with the Chief Records Officer or records delegate for records obligations.
responsible: Service owners; Knowledge Manager; Configuration Manager; Records Management; FOI team; ICT Operations.
consulted: Legal; Privacy; Information Management; business areas; suppliers holding service records.
informed: Service desk; support teams; business owners; governance forums.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only under an approved records authority or disposal rule.
exceptionProcess: Record the proposed exception, retention authority, risk, approval, disposal or transfer evidence and review date.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Records Officer or CIO delegate.
verification: Review records schedules, CMDB and knowledge audits, FOI evidence, retention labels and disposal logs.
evidence: Service record; CMDB item; knowledge article; retention schedule; FOI decision record; publication evidence; disposal or transfer record.
auditFrequency: Annual records and knowledge audit.
relatedPolicies: Records Management Policy; Information Management Policy; FOI Policy; ICT Service Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: Records management procedure; CMDB management procedure; knowledge management procedure; FOI and publication process; disposal guide.
reviewTriggers: Records authority change, FOI issue, audit finding, service retirement, system migration or knowledge quality issue.
notes: This requirement links service management evidence with NDIA records, FOI and knowledge obligations.

title: Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance
obligationDescription: ICT procurement and supplier arrangements must define and monitor value-for-money, security, privacy, accessibility, fraud, continuity, incident reporting, assurance, subcontractor, exit, performance and service-level obligations throughout the supplier lifecycle.
requirement: NDIA must manage ICT suppliers from planning to exit. Contracts and service arrangements must clearly state security, privacy, accessibility, continuity, performance, reporting and assurance obligations, and NDIA must monitor whether suppliers meet them.
obligationRef:

CPR-25 (Procurement CPRs): CPRs Division 1 - efficient, effective, economical and ethical procurement
CPR-26 (Procurement CPRs): CPRs accountability and transparency requirements
CPR-27 (Procurement CPRs): CPRs Division 2 - additional rules for procurements above relevant thresholds
CPR-28 (Procurement CPRs): CPRs and contract management expectations
ismControls: ASD ISM control areas for supplier security, third-party access, outsourced services, cloud services, contract controls and assurance.
otherStandards: Commonwealth Procurement Rules; PGPA Act; PSPF third-party risk management; contract management guidance; ITIL supplier management.
controlObjective: Ensure suppliers and contracts meet NDIA service, security, privacy, value and continuity obligations.
threat: Supplier failure, unmanaged subcontractors, poor value, weak contract controls, privacy or security gaps and failed exits.
applicability: All ICT procurements, contracts, managed services, cloud and third-party service arrangements.
excluded: Low-value purchases may use simplified procurement steps but must still meet security, privacy and records obligations.
guidance: Include mandatory clauses; complete supplier risk assessment; monitor SLAs and KPIs; review subcontractors; test incident, continuity and exit obligations.
technicalControls: Supplier risk register; contract controls; SLA and KPI reports; security questionnaires; third-party access controls; exit plan evidence.
processSteps: Plan procurement; assess risk; include clauses; onboard supplier; monitor performance; manage incidents; review or exit.
accountable: Chief Procurement Officer for procurement, with CIO accountable for ICT service outcomes.
responsible: ICT Commercial; supplier managers; service owners; Procurement; Cyber Security; Privacy; contract managers.
consulted: Legal; Risk and Assurance; Finance; Records; business owners; Architecture; suppliers.
informed: Governance forums; service users; operational support teams; affected business areas.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only for an approved procurement or contract variation.
exceptionProcess: Document the variation, risk, value-for-money impact, compensating controls, approval and review date in the contract or procurement record.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Procurement Officer with CIO delegate approval for ICT service risk.
verification: Review procurement records, contracts, supplier assurance, SLA reports, incident records and exit plans.
evidence: Procurement plan; contract clauses; supplier risk assessment; SLA or KPI report; assurance evidence; incident obligations; exit plan.
auditFrequency: Quarterly supplier review and annual assurance.
relatedPolicies: Procurement Policy; Contract Management Policy; ICT Security Policy; Privacy Policy; Supplier Risk Policy.
relatedProcedures: ICT procurement procedure; supplier assurance checklist; contract management plan; third-party access procedure; exit planning guide.
reviewTriggers: New procurement, contract renewal, supplier incident, poor SLA performance, subcontractor change, exit event or control gap.
owner: ICT Commercial and Supplier Management Lead
notes: The policy should make clear that outsourcing does not transfer NDIA accountability.

title: Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance
obligationDescription: Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway, Secure Service Edge and related infrastructure services must have approved architecture, certification or assurance, security, privacy, sovereignty, logging, cost, exit and operational controls before production and during service reviews.
requirement: NDIA must only use cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure services that have approved architecture, security, privacy, sovereignty, logging, cost and exit controls. These controls must be checked before production and during reviews.

controlObjective: Ensure infrastructure services are secure, approved, resilient, cost-aware and exit-ready.
threat: Cloud or hosting misconfiguration, sovereignty breach, insecure infrastructure, outages, unexpected cost and lock-in.
applicability: All cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway, network, Secure Service Edge and infrastructure services.
excluded: Non-production experiments may use a lighter gate only if they hold no protected or personal information and do not connect to production.
guidance: Confirm architecture approval, hosting or cloud assurance, sovereignty, logging, encryption, backup, cost and exit arrangements; review at service gates.
technicalControls: Architecture records; certified hosting or cloud evidence; encryption; logging and SIEM; network controls; backup and restore; FinOps reports; exit plans.
processSteps: Approve design; validate certification and controls; transition to service; monitor operations and cost; review exit or decommissioning.
accountable: CIO, with CISO accountable for security assurance.
responsible: Cloud and Infrastructure teams; Enterprise Architecture; Cyber Security; Service owners; Supplier Management; FinOps or Finance.
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Data Governance; Procurement; business owners; suppliers and hosting providers.
informed: Operations teams; service desk; governance forums; affected business areas.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - by approved architecture or security risk exception.
exceptionProcess: Record the exception with risk, data impact, compensating controls, owner, expiry date and exit or remediation plan.
exceptionAuthority: CIO with CISO and Architecture Review Board endorsement.
verification: Review architecture approvals, certification evidence, security assessments, logs, cost reports and service review minutes.
evidence: Architecture decision record; hosting or cloud certification evidence; security assessment; operational readiness checklist; cost report; exit plan.
auditFrequency: Before go-live, quarterly for critical services and annually for all others.
relatedPolicies: ICT Security Policy; Cloud Policy; Hosting Policy; Enterprise Architecture Policy; Business Continuity Policy.
relatedProcedures: Cloud onboarding procedure; architecture review checklist; hosting certification evidence checklist; operational readiness and decommissioning guide.
reviewFrequency: Annual, with six-monthly review for critical services.
reviewTriggers: New hosting model, cloud migration, data classification change, supplier change, material cost issue, incident, outage or certification change.
notes: This requirement should be applied before production approval and repeated during service reviews.

title: Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management
obligationDescription: New, changed and retired ICT services must pass controlled change, release and operational acceptance gates, with current CMDB/service catalogue records, authorisation status, asset custody, classification, residual risk, support readiness, disposal and retirement evidence maintained.
requirement: NDIA must control how ICT services are changed, released, configured, transitioned and retired. Changes must be approved, tested and recorded, and service catalogue, CMDB, asset, support, risk and disposal records must stay current.
type: Change, release and configuration management requirement

otherStandards: PSPF technology lifecycle management; ASD ISM; ITIL 4 change, release and configuration practices; ISO/IEC 20000.
controlObjective: Ensure changes and service transitions are authorised, tested, traceable and reflected in service records.
threat: Unauthorised changes, failed releases, inaccurate configuration data, service disruption and unmanaged asset disposal.
applicability: All new, changed, transitioned, configured, retired and decommissioned ICT services and assets.
excluded: Emergency changes may follow expedited approval but must be recorded and reviewed after implementation.
guidance: Use standard change and release gates; update service catalogue, CMDB and asset records; test support readiness; record approvals, backout plans and retirement evidence.
technicalControls: Change and release workflows; CAB records; CMDB; asset register; test evidence; deployment logs; backout and retirement records.
processSteps: Raise change; assess risk; approve; test and release; update records; verify support; close or retire with evidence.
accountable: CIO, with delegated authority to the Change Advisory Board for standard change governance.
responsible: Change Manager; Release Manager; Configuration Manager; Service owners; Delivery teams; Operations; suppliers.
consulted: Cyber Security; Architecture; Privacy; Records; business owners; service desk; suppliers.
informed: Affected users; support teams; governance forums; business stakeholders.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - emergency changes allowed with post-implementation review.
exceptionProcess: Record the emergency reason, approver, risk, test or backout evidence, implementation outcome and post-change review.
exceptionAuthority: Change Advisory Board Chair, with CIO approval for high-risk exceptions.
verification: Sample changes and releases; compare approvals, test evidence, CMDB updates, communications and retirement records.
evidence: Change record; release plan; test results; approval; deployment log; CMDB update; communication record; retirement or disposal evidence.
auditFrequency: Monthly sample review and after any major release.
relatedPolicies: Change Management Policy; Configuration Management Policy; Asset Management Policy; ICT Security Policy.
relatedProcedures: Change enablement procedure; release management procedure; configuration management procedure; asset disposal and retirement guide.
reviewTriggers: Failed change, major release, emergency change trend, audit finding, CMDB quality issue or technology lifecycle update.
notes: The policy should link change approval with service, risk, records and asset evidence.

title: Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
obligationDescription: ICT services must implement and maintain risk-based ISM and Essential Eight controls, including approved software, patching, hardening, macro controls, vulnerability disclosure, cryptography, threat intelligence, monitoring and cyber uplift actions managed through ITSM workflows.
requirement: NDIA must maintain cyber security controls for each ICT service. Services must use approved software, patching, hardening, vulnerability management, secure configuration, monitoring and remediation through ITSM processes.

ismControls: ASD ISM and Essential Eight control areas for application control, patching, hardening, macro controls, vulnerability management, logging, monitoring and incident response.
otherStandards: ASD Information Security Manual; Essential Eight Maturity Model; PSPF cyber strategies and programs; Cyber Security Act; ACSC guidance.
controlObjective: Ensure cyber controls reduce known vulnerabilities and support timely detection and remediation.
threat: Compromise through unpatched systems, insecure configuration, malware, exploitable vulnerabilities and weak monitoring.
applicability: All NDIA ICT systems, services, endpoints, applications, platforms, cloud workloads and supplier-managed components.
excluded: None for security controls. Temporary exceptions require risk acceptance and compensating controls.
guidance: Baseline against ISM and Essential Eight; track patching and vulnerabilities; manage exceptions; verify hardening; monitor uplift work through service boards.
technicalControls: Patch management; vulnerability scanning; application control; secure baseline; macro controls; EDR and SIEM; threat intelligence; exception register.
processSteps: Baseline controls; scan and patch; remediate vulnerabilities; record exceptions; monitor threats; report control status.
responsible: Cyber Security; platform owners; application owners; infrastructure teams; service owners; suppliers.
consulted: Risk and Assurance; Architecture; Change Manager; Privacy; business owners; ACSC liaison where relevant.
informed: CIO; service governance forums; affected users or business areas when risk or outages may occur.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - temporary only with CISO-approved compensating controls.
exceptionProcess: Record the control gap, threat exposure, compensating controls, risk acceptance, treatment plan, expiry date and review schedule.
exceptionAuthority: CISO or delegated cyber risk authority.
verification: Review vulnerability and patch reports, baseline compliance, monitoring evidence, uplift plans and exception register.
evidence: Patch reports; vulnerability scan results; Essential Eight assessment; secure baseline evidence; SIEM or EDR alerts; remediation tickets; exception records.
auditFrequency: Monthly for vulnerability and patch status, with quarterly control assurance.
relatedPolicies: ICT Security Policy; Vulnerability Management Policy; Change Management Policy; Risk Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: Patch and vulnerability management standard; secure configuration baseline; Essential Eight assessment procedure; cyber exception process.
reviewTriggers: New threat, vulnerability, exploit, cyber incident, Essential Eight maturity change, audit finding or major technology change.
notes: This requirement should make cyber uplift and vulnerability remediation part of routine service management.

title: Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
obligationDescription: Access to ICT services must be requested, approved, authenticated, authorised, reviewed, changed and revoked through controlled workflows, with stronger controls for privileged access, MFA, remote access, separation, Digital ID integrations, consent, identity incidents and fraud risk.
requirement: NDIA must control access to ICT services across the full user lifecycle. Access must be requested, approved, authenticated, reviewed, changed and removed through agreed workflows, with stronger controls for privileged, remote and Digital ID access.

technicalControls: IAM workflow; MFA; privileged access management; role-based access; access reviews; remote access controls; Digital ID logs; offboarding integration.

responsible: IAM team; service owners; people managers; HR onboarding/offboarding; Cyber Security; suppliers with access.
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Digital ID specialists; Risk and Assurance; business owners; service desk.
informed: Users; managers; service owners; governance forums; suppliers where their staff access NDIA services.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - temporary only for approved break-glass or operational need.
exceptionProcess: Record the access exception, reason, approver, controls, start and end date, activity logs and post-use review.

verification: Sample access requests, approvals, MFA and privileged access records, access reviews and offboarding evidence.
evidence: Access request; approval; role mapping; MFA record; privileged access log; access recertification; offboarding record; Digital ID event log.
auditFrequency: Monthly privileged access review and quarterly access recertification.

reviewTriggers: Role model change, privileged access issue, offboarding failure, identity incident, fraud indicator, Digital ID change or audit finding.
notes: The policy should make access removal as important as access approval.

title: Incident, problem, breach, cyber extortion and statutory reporting
obligationDescription: ICT incidents, security incidents, suspected breaches, supplier incidents, ransomware/extortion events and reportable cyber or privacy events must be logged, classified, contained, escalated, investigated, reported within required timeframes and followed by problem, lessons and remediation actions.
requirement: NDIA must record and manage ICT incidents, security incidents, suspected privacy breaches, supplier incidents and cyber extortion events. Events must be classified, contained, escalated, reported when required, investigated and followed by fix and learning actions.

controlObjective: Ensure incidents and breaches are managed quickly, lawfully and with accountable remediation.

applicability: All ICT incidents, cyber incidents, suspected privacy breaches, supplier incidents, extortion events and problem records.
excluded: None for reportable or high-impact incidents. Minor service requests are handled under request fulfilment.
guidance: Use one incident process; apply severity and breach criteria; involve privacy, security, legal and suppliers; meet reporting deadlines; complete root cause analysis and lessons.

processSteps: Log event; triage; contain; escalate; notify or report; investigate; fix root cause; close with lessons.
accountable: CIO, with CISO and Chief Privacy Officer accountable for cyber and privacy reporting decisions.
responsible: Incident Manager; Cyber Security; Privacy team; service owners; problem manager; supplier managers; communications team.
consulted: Legal; Risk and Assurance; business owners; Procurement; ACSC or OAIC liaison where relevant; suppliers.
informed: Executive crisis forums; affected business areas; support teams; participants or users where notification is required.
exceptionsPermitted: No for mandatory reporting; process deviations require incident controller approval.
exceptionProcess: Record the deviation, reason, legal or reporting impact, decision maker, compensating actions and post-incident review outcome.
exceptionAuthority: Incident Controller, with CISO and Chief Privacy Officer for reportable events.
verification: Sample incidents and problem records; verify reporting decisions, notifications, root cause analysis, remediation and closure evidence.
evidence: Incident ticket; severity assessment; breach assessment; notification record; supplier report; RCA; problem record; remediation plan; lessons learned.
auditFrequency: After each major incident and quarterly sample review.
relatedPolicies: Incident Management Policy; Cyber Security Incident Response Policy; Privacy Breach Policy; Problem Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: Major incident procedure; cyber incident response plan; data breach response plan; problem management procedure; supplier incident guide.
reviewTriggers: Major incident, reportable breach, ransomware or extortion event, supplier incident, repeated problem, exercise finding or legal change.
notes: The policy should join service, cyber, privacy and supplier incident pathways so events are not handled in silos.

section: 12. Continuity, backup and critical service resilience
title: Service continuity, backup, resilience, critical services and emergency integration
obligationDescription: Critical ICT services must maintain tested continuity, backup, restore, disaster recovery, emergency, critical infrastructure and SOGS support arrangements that define dependencies, ownership, RTO/RPO, restoration priorities, resilience controls and evidence of successful exercises.
requirement: NDIA must keep critical ICT services resilient. Critical services must have tested continuity, backup, restore and disaster recovery arrangements that identify owners, dependencies, RTO/RPO targets, priorities and evidence of successful exercises.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 27 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
PSPF - 55 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning
PSPF - 56 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning

PSPF - 217 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs

SOCI-30 (SOCI Act): SOCI Act data storage or processing obligations
ismControls: ASD ISM and Essential Eight control areas for backups, restoration, disaster recovery, availability, monitoring, incident response and critical system resilience.
otherStandards: PSPF contingency planning; NDIS Act participant support obligations; SOCI Act; Essential Eight backups; business continuity practices such as ISO 22301.
controlObjective: Ensure critical ICT services can continue or be restored within agreed business needs.
threat: Extended outage, failed restore, loss of critical data, inability to support participants and emergency disruption.
applicability: All business-critical and participant-critical ICT services, dependencies, suppliers and recovery arrangements.
excluded: Non-critical services may use proportionate recovery targets, but dependencies on critical services remain in scope.
guidance: Identify critical services and dependencies; agree RTO and RPO; maintain backups; test restore and disaster recovery; run exercises; record gaps and remediation.
technicalControls: Backup platform; immutable or offline backup where required; DR runbooks; monitoring; dependency map; restore test reports; continuity exercise records.
processSteps: Classify criticality; map dependencies; set RTO/RPO; backup; test restore and DR; exercise; remediate gaps.
accountable: CIO, with accountable business owners for critical services.
responsible: Continuity Manager; Infrastructure; Service owners; Disaster Recovery teams; Cyber Security; Supplier Management; business continuity team.
consulted: Risk and Assurance; business owners; emergency management; Legal; Privacy; suppliers and hosting providers.
informed: Executive crisis forums; service desk; affected business areas; suppliers; users where continuity arrangements affect service access.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only with approved risk acceptance and business owner agreement.
exceptionProcess: Record the recovery gap, business impact, risk acceptance, compensating controls, interim arrangements, owner and remediation date.
exceptionAuthority: CIO with business service owner and Risk Committee approval for high risk.
verification: Review continuity plans, backup jobs, restore tests, disaster recovery exercises and dependency maps.
evidence: Critical service register; BIA; RTO/RPO agreement; backup report; restore test result; DR exercise report; remediation tracker.
auditFrequency: At least annually, with restore tests as scheduled for the service criticality.
relatedPolicies: Business Continuity Policy; Disaster Recovery Policy; ICT Security Policy; Critical Infrastructure Policy.
relatedProcedures: ICT continuity plan; backup and restore procedure; disaster recovery runbook; critical service exercise plan.
reviewTriggers: Service criticality change, dependency change, failed backup, failed exercise, major incident, SOCI change or business continuity update.
notes: The policy should require evidence that recovery has been tested, not only planned.

section: 13. Electronic transactions, integration and data sharing
title: Electronic transactions, integrations, DATA Scheme and lawful data exchange
obligationDescription: Electronic transactions, service integrations and data-sharing exchanges must have documented legal authority, approved purpose, consent or attribution controls, accessible electronic records, audit evidence, agreements, accreditation, incident escalation and safeguards that prevent unauthorised reuse.
requirement: NDIA must ensure electronic transactions, integrations and data exchanges are lawful, authorised and traceable. Each exchange must have an approved purpose, required consent or attribution controls, agreements, audit evidence and safeguards against unauthorised reuse.
type: Electronic transaction, integration and data sharing requirement

DAT-15 (DATA Scheme): DATA Scheme reporting requirements
DAT-16 (DATA Scheme): DATA Scheme interaction with privacy, secrecy and records laws

otherStandards: Electronic Transactions Act; Data Availability and Transparency Act and DATA Scheme; PGPA cooperation duty; Privacy Act; records laws; API and data governance standards.
controlObjective: Ensure integrations and electronic transactions are lawful, secure, auditable and purpose limited.
threat: Unauthorised data sharing, invalid electronic records, weak attribution, privacy breach and unlawful reuse.
applicability: All electronic transactions, APIs, integrations, data sharing, digital forms and automated service exchanges.
excluded: Internal data movements without external sharing are still in scope where they affect records, privacy or security.
guidance: Document legal authority and purpose; use approved agreements and APIs; apply authentication, encryption and logging; review data-sharing and electronic record evidence.
technicalControls: API gateway; encryption; authentication; access logging; data-sharing agreements; consent or attribution records; electronic transaction audit trails.
processSteps: Confirm legal basis; approve data exchange; implement secure channel; log activity; review use; stop if authority ends.
accountable: Chief Data Officer or delegated Data Governance authority, with CIO accountable for ICT integration controls.
responsible: Integration teams; data owners; service owners; architecture; Cyber Security; Privacy; records teams.
consulted: Legal; business owners; Risk and Assurance; partner agencies; suppliers; data governance forum.
informed: Receiving and providing business areas; operational support teams; partner agencies where relevant.
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to legal authority; technical exceptions require approval.
exceptionProcess: Record the legal authority, technical issue, risk, compensating controls, expiry date, data owner approval and remediation plan.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Data Officer or delegated Data Governance authority, with CISO for security exceptions.
verification: Review agreements, legal authority records, API and access logs, data-sharing approvals and audit trails.
evidence: Legal authority assessment; data sharing agreement; API design approval; consent or attribution evidence; transaction log; access review; audit trail.
auditFrequency: Annual review and after any new or changed integration.
relatedPolicies: Data Governance Policy; Privacy Policy; Information Sharing Policy; Integration Policy; Records Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: Integration design standard; API security standard; data sharing agreement procedure; electronic records and transaction evidence guide.
reviewTriggers: New integration, changed data use, data-sharing law change, partner change, privacy issue, audit finding or access anomaly.
notes: The policy should require legal authority and audit evidence before data is exchanged through ICT services.

title: AI governance, transparency, training, lifecycle controls and impact assessment
obligationDescription: AI-enabled ICT services must have accountable owners, approved purposes, transparency and register records, trained users, lifecycle controls, testing, monitoring, human oversight, impact assessment and review before production and when use, data or risk materially changes.
requirement: NDIA must manage AI-enabled ICT services responsibly. Each AI use must have an accountable owner, approved purpose, transparency record, trained users, lifecycle controls, testing, monitoring, human oversight and impact assessment before use and when risk changes.
obligationRef:

applicability: All AI-enabled ICT services, tools, integrations and supplier solutions used for NDIA business.
excluded: Simple automation without AI capability may be outside AI-specific controls but remains subject to standard ICT controls.
guidance: Register AI use cases; complete impact assessment; set human oversight; test model and data risks; train users; monitor outputs and review changes.
technicalControls: AI register; impact assessment; access controls; test logs; monitoring; human review workflow; model and data change records; training evidence.
processSteps: Register use; assess impact; approve purpose; train users; test and monitor; review changes; retire when unsafe.

responsible: AI product owner; service owner; data scientists or vendors; Cyber Security; Privacy; Risk and Assurance; delivery teams.
consulted: Legal; Data Governance; Ethics or AI governance forum; business owners; Records; accessibility advisers; suppliers.
informed: Users of the AI-enabled service; support teams; governance forums; affected business areas.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - only through AI governance and risk acceptance.
exceptionProcess: Record the AI control gap, user and participant impact, compensating controls, accountable owner, expiry date and review plan.
exceptionAuthority: Accountable AI Official with CIO and risk delegate approval.
verification: Review AI register, impact assessments, approvals, test and monitoring results, training records and change records.
evidence: AI use case register entry; impact assessment; approval record; transparency statement; test report; monitoring log; user training record; change history.
auditFrequency: Six-monthly and after any material AI change.
relatedPolicies: Responsible AI Policy; Data Governance Policy; ICT Security Policy; Privacy Policy; Risk Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: AI use case registration procedure; AI impact assessment guide; model monitoring and change procedure; AI training guide.
reviewTriggers: New AI use case, changed model or data, incident, complaint, bias concern, policy change, supplier change or risk rating change.
notes: The policy should make AI accountability visible before an AI-enabled service is used in production.

title: Child safety, safeguarding, access controls and compliance evidence
obligationDescription: ICT services used by or about children must apply child-safe design, privacy, communication, consent, access, complaint, training, escalation, risk assessment and compliance evidence controls that support safe participation and annual child-safety reporting.
requirement: NDIA must make ICT services used by or about children safe by design. Services must apply privacy, consent, access, communication, complaint, training, escalation, risk assessment and evidence controls that support safe participation.

processSteps: Assess child-safety risk; design controls; train teams; monitor access and complaints; escalate issues; report compliance.

responsible: Service owners; Child Safety and Safeguarding leads; Privacy; Cyber Security; support teams; suppliers handling child information.
consulted: Legal; Records; business owners; complaints team; participant engagement; Risk and Assurance.
informed: Executive safeguarding forums; service users where appropriate; support teams; suppliers and business areas handling child information.
exceptionsPermitted: No exception to legal or child-safety duties; operational exceptions require executive approval.

evidence: Child safety risk assessment; control checklist; training record; access review; complaint and escalation records; annual compliance statement.

reviewTriggers: New child-facing service, child-safety incident, complaint trend, legal change, annual statement cycle or audit finding.

responsible: Infrastructure service owners, platform owners, enterprise architecture, cyber security and risk teams
consulted: CISO, Chief Risk Officer, Privacy Officer, Legal, Procurement, Internal Audit and business system owners
informed: Executive governance bodies, service owners, operational teams and affected business areas

verification: Governance evidence review, risk register review and control self-assessment.

section: 2. Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset control

obligationDescription: NDIA must manage each infrastructure system and asset through an ISM-aligned lifecycle from planning and procurement to operation, change and disposal; systems must be authorised or reauthorised before production or material change, recorded in asset and authorised-system registers, comply with applicable Commonwealth technology standards, and restrict prohibited, legacy, smart and IoT technologies unless risk-approved.
requirement: The NDIA must keep an accurate register of infrastructure assets and authorised systems, manage them through their full life, and approve new, changed, legacy, smart or IoT technology before use.

obligationDescription: NDIA infrastructure must identify the classification, caveat, sensitivity and business impact of information it stores, processes or transmits, apply protective markings and metadata where required, and enforce approved access, storage, transmission, disclosure, offshore-access, privacy-governance, PIA and training controls for personal and protected NDIS information.
requirement: The NDIA must know what information each infrastructure service holds or moves, classify and protect it correctly, and apply privacy, access, storage, transmission and disclosure controls before use.

section: 6. Records, retention, FOI, migration and secure disposal
title: Commonwealth records, legal holds, retrieval, decommissioning and media sanitisation
obligationDescription: NDIA infrastructure must create, preserve, retrieve and export required Commonwealth records, logs, metadata and service records; deletion, migration, cloud exit, sanitisation, destruction, de-identification or disposal of data, media and assets must occur only under approved retention, FOI, legal hold, Archives Act, privacy and ISM processes, with evidence retained.
requirement: The NDIA must keep required infrastructure records, logs and metadata, make them retrievable, and only delete, migrate, sanitise or dispose of data, media and assets under approved records, privacy and security processes.
