technicalControls: Retention labels, backup and archive controls, legal hold, immutable logging, eDiscovery/export, secure erase/sanitisation tools and disposal tracking.
processSteps: Identify records; apply retention and legal hold; approve migration or deletion; export when required; sanitise or destroy media; retain certificates and approvals.
responsible: Records management, infrastructure operations, service owners, data custodians and disposal coordinators
consulted: Legal, Privacy Officer, FOI team, CISO, Procurement, Risk and business information owners
informed: Service owners, business areas, Internal Audit and operational support teams
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - risk approved only
exceptionProcess: Record the exception with business need, risk assessment, compensating controls, owner and expiry date in the exception register.
exceptionAuthority: CIO with Records Manager, Legal and CISO endorsement
verification: Retention control review, disposal evidence sampling, FOI/retrieval test and decommissioning review.
evidence: Retention schedules, legal hold records, export tests, deletion approvals, sanitisation certificates, destruction records and decommissioning reports.
auditFrequency: Annual records/disposal assurance and at each material migration or decommissioning event

section: 7. Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight, backups and cryptography
title: Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls
obligationDescription: NDIA infrastructure must implement the approved cyber security strategy, ISM controls and Essential Eight target maturity, including timely patching, application control, macro restrictions, user application hardening, protected and tested backups, relevant ASD mitigation strategies, and approved cryptography including post-quantum requirements where applicable.
requirement: The NDIA must protect infrastructure with approved cyber controls, including Essential Eight maturity, timely patching, secure configuration, application control, hardened user applications, tested backups and approved cryptography.

section: 8. Network, gateway, DNS and boundary security
title: Gateway/SSE, Protective DNS, segmentation and security visibility
obligationDescription: NDIA networks and internet-connected infrastructure must use approved gateway, Secure Service Edge, Protective DNS or equivalent boundary controls; gateway services must be authorised, appropriately assessed, supply-chain assured, hosted, monitored, logged, vulnerability-managed and continuously tested commensurate with the information they protect.
requirement: The NDIA must protect networks and internet-connected infrastructure with approved gateways, segmentation, DNS/security edge controls, monitoring, logging and testing that match the sensitivity of the information handled.

requirement: The NDIA must physically protect infrastructure sites, rooms, racks, cabinets, media and outsourced locations with security zones, access controls, monitoring and visitor controls that match classification and business impact.

section: 12. Incident response, breach, extortion and evidence
title: Supplier, privacy, fraud, cyber extortion and reporting response
obligationDescription: Infrastructure incident response processes must support prompt escalation, containment, investigation, evidence preservation, supplier direction, privacy breach assessment, cyber-extortion payment governance, mandatory reporting readiness and lawful information sharing with authorised cyber, legal and executive stakeholders.
requirement: The NDIA must respond quickly to infrastructure incidents, preserve evidence, involve suppliers when needed, assess privacy and fraud impacts, meet mandatory reporting needs, and govern any cyber extortion decisions.
obligationRef:

controlObjective: Infrastructure incidents are contained, investigated, reported and learned from in a lawful and coordinated way.
threat: Delayed containment, evidence loss, privacy breach, ransomware/extortion impact, supplier failure, fraud loss or missed statutory reporting.
applicability: All actual or suspected cyber, privacy, supplier, fraud, physical or operational incidents affecting NDIA infrastructure, data, services or suppliers.
excluded: Minor service requests with no security, privacy, fraud or continuity impact may follow normal service management.
guidance: Maintain incident playbooks, escalation paths, supplier contact arrangements, breach assessment steps, evidence handling, executive/legal notification and reporting decision points.
technicalControls: SIEM/SOAR, incident ticketing, secure communications, forensic tooling, immutable logs, backup recovery, evidence repository and supplier notification channels.
processSteps: Detect and triage; contain; preserve evidence; assess privacy/fraud/extortion impacts; notify required stakeholders; recover; complete post-incident review.
responsible: Incident response team, SOC, infrastructure operations, service owners, suppliers and business continuity team
consulted: CIO, Privacy Officer, Legal, Fraud Control, Risk, Procurement, Communications and executive leadership
informed: Affected business owners, service desk, Internal Audit, regulators or government bodies where approved
exceptionsPermitted: Limited - mandatory notification and evidence obligations cannot be waived
exceptionProcess: For control deviations, record risk and compensating controls; for incidents, follow the incident escalation and reporting process without delay.
exceptionAuthority: CISO with CIO, Legal and Privacy Officer approval where applicable
verification: Incident exercise, incident record review, reporting decision review and post-incident action tracking.
evidence: Incident tickets, timelines, evidence logs, forensic records, supplier communications, breach assessments, reporting decisions and lessons learned actions.
auditFrequency: After each major incident, quarterly tabletop exercise and annual incident response test
relatedPolicies: NDIA Cyber Incident Response Policy; NDIA Privacy Policy; NDIA Fraud Control Policy; NDIA Supplier Management Policy
relatedProcedures: Cyber Incident Response Plan; Data Breach Response Procedure; Evidence Handling Procedure; Ransomware Response Playbook
reviewTriggers: Major incident; new reporting obligation; tabletop finding; supplier incident; privacy breach; ransomware/extortion event.
notes: Mandatory reporting and evidence preservation requirements take priority over convenience or supplier preferences.

title: Fraud risk assessment, preventive controls, detection and asset accountability
obligationDescription: NDIA infrastructure governance must prevent, detect and respond to fraud, corruption and misuse through activity risk assessments, control plans, separation of duties, monitoring of billing, usage, inventory and privileged activity, and complete records of hardware movements, losses, returns and disposals.
requirement: The NDIA must design and operate infrastructure controls that reduce fraud, corruption and misuse risks, including separation of duties, monitoring of privileged activity, billing and inventory checks, and records of asset movements.
type: Mandatory fraud and misuse control requirement
obligationRef:
FRAUD-07 (Fraud and Corruption): PGPA Rule 2014, s10 - Fraud and Corruption Rule
FRAUD-08 (Fraud and Corruption): Framework Element 1 - Fraud and corruption risk assessments
FRAUD-09 (Fraud and Corruption): Framework Element 2 - Fraud and corruption control plans
FRAUD-10 (Fraud and Corruption): Framework Element 5 - Prevention
FRAUD-11 (Fraud and Corruption): Framework Element 6 - Detection
FRAUD-13 (Fraud and Corruption): Framework Element 8 - Recording and reporting
ismControls: ASD ISM: access control, privileged activity logging, asset management, audit logs and separation of duties
otherStandards: PGPA Fraud and Corruption Rule; Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework; PSPF and ISM supporting access and asset controls
controlObjective: Infrastructure assets, access and services are used properly and suspicious activity can be detected, investigated and reported.
threat: Fraudulent use, asset theft, billing abuse, procurement misuse, privileged misuse, false records or corruption.
applicability: All infrastructure assets, privileged accounts, supplier access, billing records, inventory movements, service consumption and disposal activities.
excluded: None by default. Low-value consumables may use proportionate inventory controls where approved.
guidance: Include fraud risk in infrastructure activities, apply separation of duties, monitor high-risk transactions and privileged activity, and retain asset and billing records.
technicalControls: PAM logs, SIEM alerts, asset/inventory system, billing analytics, segregation-of-duties rules, approval workflows and audit trails.
processSteps: Assess fraud risk; design controls; approve duties and access; monitor usage and billing; record asset movements; escalate suspicious activity; retain evidence.
accountable: Chief Risk Officer with Chief Information Officer (CIO)
responsible: Fraud control team, infrastructure operations, asset managers, procurement, finance and cyber security
consulted: CISO, Legal, Privacy, Internal Audit, business owners and supplier managers
informed: Executive governance, asset custodians, managers and affected service owners
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - risk approved only
exceptionProcess: Record the exception with business need, risk assessment, compensating controls, owner and expiry date in the exception register.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Risk Officer with CIO and CISO endorsement
verification: Fraud control self-assessment, asset reconciliation, billing review, privileged activity sampling and incident reporting review.
evidence: Fraud risk assessments, control plans, SoD approvals, billing reports, inventory reconciliations, PAM/SIEM logs, loss reports and investigation records.
auditFrequency: Quarterly monitoring review and annual fraud control assurance
relatedPolicies: NDIA Fraud Control Policy; NDIA ICT Asset Management Policy; NDIA Access Control Policy; NDIA Procurement Policy
relatedProcedures: Fraud Risk Assessment Procedure; Asset Movement Procedure; Privileged Activity Review Procedure; Billing Review Guideline
reviewTriggers: Fraud risk assessment change; inventory or billing anomaly; privileged misuse; procurement concern; investigation or audit finding.
owner: Fraud Control and Infrastructure Accountability SME
notes: Focuses on misuse of infrastructure assets, services, privileged access and supplier arrangements.

title: Accessible infrastructure, assistive technology and inclusive service delivery
obligationDescription: NDIA infrastructure must support accessible digital service delivery and workplace participation by assessing cloud, hardware, network and service designs for assistive technology compatibility, WCAG-compatible delivery needs and proportionate alternatives where security controls may affect accessibility.
requirement: The NDIA must make infrastructure services and workplaces accessible by checking designs for assistive technology, accessible digital delivery and reasonable alternatives where security controls affect accessibility.
obligationRef:
NDIS-58 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act 2013, principles on accessible communication and participation
DDA-24 (DDA): Disability Discrimination Act 1992
DDA-25 (DDA): Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - Disability Services and Inclusion Act 2023 for assistive technology compatibility
DDA-26 (DDA): Digital Inclusion Standard - Criterion 4 Make it accessible
DDA-27 (DDA): DDA and inclusive workplace/service access obligations
DDA-28 (DDA): DDA and remote access/service access
ismControls: ASD ISM: secure configuration, remote access, endpoint controls and access management applied in ways that support approved accessibility adjustments
otherStandards: NDIS Act accessible communication principles; Disability Discrimination Act; Disability Services and Inclusion Act; Digital Inclusion Standard; Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy
controlObjective: Infrastructure enables accessible service delivery and workplace participation without weakening required security controls.
threat: Exclusion of participants or staff, inaccessible services, failed assistive technology, discrimination risk or insecure workarounds.
applicability: Infrastructure supporting NDIA digital services, workplaces, endpoints, remote access, networks, cloud services, collaboration tools and assistive technology.
excluded: Systems with no user interaction may be excluded from user accessibility testing but must still support accessible downstream services where relevant.
guidance: Assess accessibility during design, procurement and change; test assistive technology compatibility; provide reasonable alternatives; document security-safe adjustments.
technicalControls: Accessible configuration profiles, assistive technology compatibility testing, endpoint management, accessible remote access, service monitoring and approved adjustment tracking.
processSteps: Identify users and accessibility needs; test designs; resolve barriers; approve adjustments; communicate support paths; review after major changes.
responsible: Digital accessibility team, infrastructure operations, workplace technology, service owners and procurement
consulted: Disability and inclusion advisors, Privacy, CISO, Legal, HR/workplace teams, users and business owners
informed: Affected staff, participants, service desk, service owners and executive governance
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - risk approved only
exceptionProcess: Record the exception with business need, accessibility impact, risk assessment, compensating controls, owner and expiry date.
exceptionAuthority: CIO with Accessibility Lead and CISO endorsement where security controls are affected
verification: Accessibility assessment review, procurement evidence review, assistive technology test results and user feedback review.
evidence: Accessibility assessments, AT test results, procurement requirements, design decisions, adjustment approvals, user feedback and remediation records.
auditFrequency: At each major change and annual accessibility assurance review
relatedPolicies: NDIA Accessibility Policy; NDIA Digital Service Standard; NDIA ICT Security Policy; NDIA Workplace Adjustment Policy
relatedProcedures: Accessibility Testing Procedure; Assistive Technology Compatibility Guideline; Secure Accessibility Adjustment Process
reviewTriggers: New digital service; workplace technology change; accessibility complaint; assistive technology change; security control change.
owner: Accessibility and Infrastructure Service Design SME
notes: Security controls should be designed to support accessibility rather than force insecure workarounds.

section: 15. Critical infrastructure, SOGS and regulated-provider obligations
title: SOCI, Systems of Government Significance and critical data services
obligationDescription: Where SOCI, Systems of Government Significance or critical-data obligations may apply, NDIA must assess triggers before infrastructure or provider changes, confirm provider regulatory status, issue required notifications, apply risk program and enhanced cyber obligations, protect regulated information, and maintain executive, legal and security escalation for incident or government assistance obligations.
requirement: When critical infrastructure, critical data storage or Systems of Government Significance obligations may apply, the NDIA must assess the trigger, meet notification and risk program duties, protect regulated information and escalate incidents quickly.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 217 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
SOCI-32 (SOCI Act): Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018
SOCI-33 (SOCI Act): SOCI Act - critical data storage or processing assets
SOCI-34 (SOCI Act): SOCI Act, s12F(3) provider notification obligation
SOCI-35 (SOCI Act): SOCI Act - incident and government assistance powers
SOCI-36 (SOCI Act): SOCI risk management program considerations
ismControls: ASD ISM: critical system security, supply chain security, logging and monitoring, incident response, access control and vulnerability management
otherStandards: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018; SOCI critical data storage or processing obligations; PSPF 2025 Cyber Security Programs; Systems of Government Significance obligations
controlObjective: Regulated infrastructure and data services meet government notification, risk, incident and information-protection obligations.
threat: Regulatory breach, unmanaged critical data service, national security risk, delayed incident reporting or failure to comply with government assistance obligations.
applicability: Infrastructure, cloud, hosting, data storage, processing, supplier or service arrangements that may support critical NDIA services, critical data or SOGS obligations.
excluded: Infrastructure that has been assessed and documented as outside SOCI/SOGS/critical data triggers.
guidance: Assess regulatory triggers before change; confirm provider status; record obligations; maintain risk program controls; protect regulated information; test escalation and notification paths.
technicalControls: Critical asset register flags, supplier/regulatory due diligence, SIEM monitoring, secure evidence repository, incident notification workflow and protected information channels.
processSteps: Screen changes; obtain Legal/CISO assessment; update register; notify as required; apply controls; rehearse incident escalation; review after supplier or architecture change.
accountable: Chief Information Officer (CIO) with General Counsel and CISO
responsible: Infrastructure owners, Legal, CISO, supplier managers, cloud/hosting teams and incident response team
consulted: Risk, Privacy, Procurement, Records, executive governance, business owners and government liaison roles
informed: Relevant executives, service owners, SOC and affected operational teams
exceptionsPermitted: Limited - statutory notification, reporting and assistance obligations cannot be waived
exceptionProcess: Escalate any proposed exception to Legal, CISO and CIO; document decision, residual risk, compensating controls and statutory impact.
exceptionAuthority: CIO and General Counsel with CISO endorsement
verification: Regulatory trigger assessment review, critical asset register review, supplier status review and incident escalation exercise.
evidence: Legal assessments, SOCI/SOGS trigger records, asset register, provider notifications, risk program evidence, incident runbooks and escalation test results.
auditFrequency: At each material change and annual regulatory compliance review
relatedPolicies: NDIA Critical Infrastructure Compliance Policy; NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Supplier Management Policy; NDIA Cloud Policy
relatedProcedures: SOCI Trigger Assessment Procedure; Critical Data Handling Guideline; Regulated Incident Escalation Playbook
reviewTriggers: New or changed critical service, data store, provider or legislation; government direction; incident; regulatory assessment finding.
owner: Critical Infrastructure and Regulatory Compliance SME
notes: Use when SOCI, SOGS or critical-data obligations may apply to infrastructure or providers.

section: 16. Sustainability, environmental performance and cost management
title: Financial sustainability, cloud cost control and environmental procurement
obligationDescription: NDIA infrastructure owners must forecast, monitor and optimise infrastructure capacity, cloud consumption and lifecycle costs, and procure ICT goods and services with evidence-based environmental performance, emissions, durability, repair, reuse, recycling and supplier compliance considerations where applicable.
requirement: The NDIA must plan, monitor and optimise infrastructure capacity, cloud spend and lifecycle costs, and consider environmental performance, reuse, repair, recycling and supplier compliance when buying or retiring ICT assets.
obligationRef:
NDIS-56 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act 2013, functions relating to financial sustainability and managing risks/issues
WGCP-21 (WOG Cloud Policy): Cloud policy - cost management and visibility
ESPP-01 (ESPP / APS Net Zero): Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy - ICT goods from 1 July 2025
ESPP-02 (ESPP / APS Net Zero): ESP Policy - products should minimise greenhouse gas emissions, be safe for the environment and retain value for longer
ESPP-03 (ESPP / APS Net Zero): APS Net Zero 2030 Target - computing and data systems
ESPP-04 (ESPP / APS Net Zero): Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy - APS Net Zero alignment
ESPP-05 (ESPP / APS Net Zero): ESP Policy - APS entities and suppliers required to demonstrate compliance
ismControls: ASD ISM: asset lifecycle, cloud service management, capacity monitoring and secure disposal where sustainability actions affect ICT assets or data
otherStandards: NDIS Act financial sustainability functions; Whole-of-Government Cloud Computing Policy cost visibility; Environmentally Sustainable Procurement Policy; APS Net Zero 2030
controlObjective: Infrastructure remains financially sustainable, efficiently used and procured with responsible environmental outcomes.
threat: Uncontrolled cloud spend, over-provisioning, waste, poor environmental compliance, premature replacement, unsupported assets or insecure disposal.
applicability: All infrastructure budgets, capacity plans, cloud consumption, data centre services, hardware procurement, lifecycle refresh, reuse, recycling and disposal activities.
excluded: Emergency purchases may use accelerated approval but must still record cost, security and environmental considerations after the event.
guidance: Use forecasting, tagging, chargeback/showback, lifecycle planning, procurement criteria and disposal planning to optimise cost and environmental outcomes.
technicalControls: Cloud cost management, resource tagging, capacity monitoring, asset lifecycle tracking, procurement evidence repository, energy/emissions data where available and secure disposal tracking.
processSteps: Forecast demand; tag and monitor resources; review spend and capacity; optimise usage; apply environmental procurement criteria; record reuse/recycling/disposal evidence.
accountable: Chief Information Officer (CIO) with Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
responsible: Infrastructure finance, cloud operations, procurement, asset management, sustainability and service owners
consulted: CISO, Enterprise Architecture, Risk, suppliers, business owners and records/disposal teams
informed: Executive governance, budget owners, service owners and operational teams
exceptionsPermitted: Yes - risk approved only
exceptionProcess: Record the exception with business need, cost impact, environmental impact, risk assessment, compensating controls, owner and expiry date.
exceptionAuthority: CIO and CFO with Procurement and CISO endorsement where security or disposal is affected
verification: Cost and capacity review, cloud consumption reporting, procurement evidence review and disposal/recycling evidence sampling.
evidence: Forecasts, budgets, cloud cost reports, tagging compliance, optimisation actions, procurement evaluation records, environmental evidence and disposal certificates.
auditFrequency: Monthly cost/capacity review and annual sustainability/procurement assurance
relatedPolicies: NDIA Financial Management Policy; NDIA Procurement Policy; NDIA ICT Asset Management Policy; NDIA Cloud Policy
relatedProcedures: Cloud Cost Management Procedure; Capacity Management Procedure; Sustainable ICT Procurement Guideline; Asset Reuse and Recycling Procedure
reviewTriggers: Budget pressure; cloud spend anomaly; capacity change; procurement rule change; environmental policy change; audit finding.
owner: Infrastructure Cost, Capacity and Sustainability SME
notes: Balances value for money, operational resilience, environmental performance and secure disposal.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Portfolio Planning Policy
title: Statutory accountability and portfolio governance
obligationDescription: The NDIA must assign clear decision rights and accountable roles for technology portfolio planning so statutory, security and procurement obligations are met.
requirement: NDIA must govern its ICT technology portfolio through approved forums with clear scope, delegated decision rights, named owners and documented decisions.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 7 (PSPF 2025): 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
PSPF - 11 (PSPF 2025): 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
PSPF - 16 (PSPF 2025): 02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
PSPF - 217 (PSPF 2025): 15. Cyber Security Programs
PGPA-65 (PGPA Act Rule): PGPA Act 2013 ss 15, 18 and 52
CPR-30 (Cth Procurement Rules): PGPA Rule 2014 s 30 prescribed CCEs; Finance PGPA instruments table
NDIS-59 (NDIS Info Rules): NDIS Act 2013
ismControls: ISM cyber security program governance; detailed controls to be mapped for each system.
otherStandards: PSPF; PGPA Act and Rule; Commonwealth Procurement Rules; NDIS Act.
controlObjective: Ensure accountable governance and documented decision making for technology portfolio planning.
threat: Unclear ownership, unauthorised decisions, unmanaged security obligations and non-compliance with legislation.
applicability: All ICT strategy, architecture, investment, sourcing, lifecycle and portfolio decisions for NDIA systems and technology services.
excluded: Non-ICT business policy decisions, unless they create, change or retire technology.
guidance: Maintain approved terms of reference, delegations, decision records and a portfolio governance calendar.
technicalControls: Portfolio workflow or register; access-controlled decision repository; records management controls.
processSteps: Define forums and delegations; assign owners; record decisions; track actions; escalate unresolved risks.
responsible: Chief Technology Officer; Chief Architect; Head of ICT Portfolio Management; Chief Information Security Officer.
consulted: Legal; Procurement; Finance; Risk; Data Governance; business capability owners.
informed: Executive Leadership Team; technology service owners; project sponsors.
exceptionsPermitted: Limited
exceptionProcess: Document the proposed exception, risk, compensating controls and expiry date in the portfolio exception register.
exceptionAuthority: Chief Information Officer, with CISO endorsement where security risk is involved.
verification: Governance review and sample checks of decision records, delegations and meeting minutes.
evidence: Governance framework, terms of reference, delegation records, meeting papers, minutes, action logs and exception records.
auditFrequency: Annual
relatedPolicies: ICT Governance Policy; Information Security Policy; Enterprise Risk Management Policy; Procurement Policy.
relatedProcedures: Technology Portfolio Planning Procedure; ICT Governance Terms of Reference; Delegations Procedure.
reviewTriggers: Machinery of government changes; PSPF, PGPA or CPR changes; portfolio governance changes; material audit findings.
notes: Use this requirement to set scope, authority and escalation paths for the policy.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Portfolio Planning Policy

title: Annual planning, capability alignment and roadmaps
obligationDescription: The NDIA must plan its ICT portfolio on a regular cycle aligned to business capabilities, security planning, annual performance and digital investment plans.
requirement: NDIA must run an annual technology portfolio planning cycle and keep capability roadmaps that show current state, target state, dependencies, funding needs and security risks.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 18 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
PSPF - 19 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
PSPF - 20 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
PSPF - 21 (PSPF 2025): 03. Security Planning, Incidents and Training
PGPA-67 (PGPA Act Rule): PGPA Act 2013 s 35; PGPA Rule 2014 s 16E
DIP-01 (Digital Investment Plans): DIP Policy - authority from 1 July 2025
DIP-02 (Digital Investment Plans): DIP Guidebook - annual endorsed DIP from June 2026
DIP-03 (Digital Investment Plans): DIP Guidebook - 2026-27 Budget context
DIP-04 (Digital Investment Plans): DIP Policy - minimum standards for future-focused digital planning

guidance: Set annual planning milestones linked to budget, Digital Investment Plan and architecture planning.
technicalControls: Roadmap repository; dependency and milestone tracking; portfolio reporting tool.
processSteps: Gather demand; assess capability gaps; update roadmaps; prioritise initiatives; obtain governance endorsement.

relatedProcedures: Annual Portfolio Planning Procedure; Capability Roadmapping Guideline; Demand Management Procedure.
reviewTriggers: Budget cycle changes; new government priorities; material change to capability needs; portfolio performance issues.
notes: Link the planning cycle to the Australian Government Architecture and endorsed Digital Investment Plan.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Portfolio Planning Policy
section: 3. Authoritative portfolio register and asset metadata
title: Application portfolio management and asset inventory
obligationDescription: The NDIA must maintain reliable, current metadata for applications, platforms, cloud services and technology assets.
requirement: NDIA must keep a single authoritative technology portfolio register that records each asset owner, purpose, lifecycle status, risk, classification, supplier, cost and roadmap dependency.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 89 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PSPF - 211 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
WGCP-27 (Cloud Computing Policy): Cloud Policy - planning, procuring and managing cloud environments
DIR-011 (PSPF Directions): PSPF Direction 002-2024 Technology Asset Stocktake
ISM-1103 (Info Security Manual): ISM guidance for cyber security documentation and system owners
ARC-49 (Archives Records): Information Management Standard for Australian Government
ismControls: ISM cyber security documentation and system owner guidance.
otherStandards: PSPF Technology Lifecycle Management; Whole-of-Government Cloud Policy; PSPF Direction 002-2024; National Archives Information Management Standard.
controlObjective: Provide trusted information for planning, risk management, investment and reporting.
threat: Unknown assets, duplicate services, unmanaged ownership, unsupported technology and inaccurate portfolio decisions.
applicability: All NDIA applications, platforms, infrastructure, cloud services, integrations and major technology components.
excluded: End-user consumables, unless they are part of an enterprise technology asset baseline.
guidance: Use agreed mandatory fields and a data owner for each asset record.
technicalControls: CMDB or portfolio register; access controls; automated data feeds where available; audit trail.

consulted: Finance; Procurement; Records Management; Data Governance.
informed: Portfolio governance forums; project teams; operations teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Limited

evidence: Portfolio register extract, CMDB records, asset owner attestations, stocktake reports and reconciliation logs.
auditFrequency: Quarterly
relatedPolicies: ICT Asset Management Policy; Information Security Policy; Cloud Policy; Records Management Policy.
relatedProcedures: Asset Metadata Standard; Configuration Management Procedure; Technology Asset Stocktake Procedure.
reviewTriggers: PSPF directions; new technology types; audit findings; asset data quality threshold breaches.
notes: Minimum metadata should be mandatory at concept, build, operate and retire stages.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Portfolio Planning Policy

requirement: NDIA must assess portfolio risk and technical debt, assign accountable owners, agree remediation plans and formally accept any residual risk that remains.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 36 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 37 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 38 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management
PSPF - 52 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning
PSPF - 53 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning
PSPF - 54 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning
PSPF - 93 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
PGPA-66 (PGPA Act Rule): PGPA Act 2013 s 16
CRMP-18 (Cth Risk Mgmt): Commonwealth Risk Management Policy; PGPA Act 2013 s 16
CRMP-19 (Cth Risk Mgmt): Commonwealth Risk Management Policy - entity risk appetite and tolerance
CRMP-20 (Cth Risk Mgmt): Commonwealth Risk Management Policy - risk ownership and controls
DIR-012 (PSPF Directions): PSPF technology directions on specific products and vulnerabilities
E8-72 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight maturity exceptions
ismControls: Essential Eight maturity exceptions; ISM risk management and vulnerability remediation controls to be mapped by system.

informed: Portfolio Governance Board; Executive Leadership Team; delivery and operations teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, controlled exceptions only

exceptionAuthority: CIO for portfolio risk; CISO for cyber risk; Accountable Executive for residual business risk.
verification: Review risk and exception registers, overdue remediation items and governance approvals.
evidence: Portfolio risk register, technical debt register, exception approvals, remediation plans, risk acceptance records and dashboard reports.
auditFrequency: Quarterly
relatedPolicies: Enterprise Risk Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Vulnerability Management Policy; ICT Governance Policy.
relatedProcedures: Portfolio Risk Management Procedure; Technical Debt Management Guideline; Security Exception Procedure.
reviewTriggers: New PSPF directions; incidents; major vulnerabilities; technology end-of-life; risk appetite changes.

processSteps: Register use case; assess risk and impact; approve pilot; implement controls; monitor performance and harms; review before scaling or retirement.
responsible: AI Governance Lead; Data Owners; Product Owners; Cyber Security; Privacy; Enterprise Architecture.
consulted: Legal; Ethics/Responsible AI Forum; Risk; Procurement; Business Owners; participant representative groups where appropriate.
informed: Portfolio Governance Board; affected users; Executive Leadership Team.
exceptionsPermitted: Limited
exceptionProcess: AI exceptions must include risk assessment, human oversight plan, transparency controls, expiry and senior approval.
exceptionAuthority: AI Governance Committee or CIO; Privacy Officer/CISO approval for privacy or security risk.
verification: Review AI register, risk assessments, approvals, monitoring reports and outcome evidence.
evidence: AI use case register, impact assessment, risk assessment, approval record, model/data documentation, transparency statement, monitoring logs and review outcomes.
auditFrequency: Quarterly for high-risk AI; annually for other AI
relatedPolicies: Responsible AI Policy; Data Governance Policy; Privacy Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Enterprise Architecture Policy.
relatedProcedures: AI Assessment Procedure; AI Technical Standard Checklist; Model Monitoring Procedure; Emerging Technology Intake Procedure.
reviewTriggers: AI policy or technical standard changes; new high-risk use case; incident or harm report; model drift; procurement of AI capability.
notes: AI requirements apply to prototypes when NDIA data or users are involved.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy
title: Governance, risk, internal control and exceptions
obligationDescription: Technology-enabled projects must operate under approved NDIA governance that assigns accountable owners, manages delivery, security, shared and emerging risks against NDIA risk appetite, maintains internal controls, and records any approved exceptions, compensating controls, expiry dates and escalation decisions.
requirement: Each technology-enabled project must have approved governance before work starts. It must name accountable owners, manage delivery, security and shared risks, keep key controls, and record any exception with an owner, controls and end date.

PSPF - 36 (PSPF 2025): 05. Security Risk Management

PSPF - 54 (PSPF 2025): 08. Contingency Planning

CRMP-24 (CRMP): Commonwealth Risk Management Policy - shared and emerging risks
CRMP-25 (CRMP): Risk controls, treatment and monitoring
ismControls: ISM-aligned security risk management and authorisation, where technology risks apply.
otherStandards: PSPF 2025; PGPA Act; Commonwealth Risk Management Policy.
controlObjective: Make sure each project is governed, risks are known, and exceptions are controlled.
threat: Unclear accountability, unmanaged delivery or security risks, weak controls, or uncontrolled exceptions.
applicability: All NDIA technology-enabled projects, programs and material changes.
excluded: None. Tailoring needs an approved exception.
guidance: Set up the right governance forum, confirm risk appetite, keep a risk register, and track controls, decisions and exceptions.
technicalControls: Risk register, issue and decision logs, exception register, and access-controlled evidence repository.
processSteps: Confirm sponsor; appoint owners; complete risk assessment; record controls; review exceptions at each gate.
responsible: Project Manager; Business Owner; Technology Owner.
consulted: Risk; Cyber Security; Enterprise Architecture; Legal; Procurement.
informed: Portfolio Governance; Policy Owner; delivery teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, limited
exceptionProcess: Submit a written exception with reason, risk assessment, compensating controls, owner and expiry date.
exceptionAuthority: Project Sponsor and relevant risk or control owner; Policy Owner for material exceptions.
verification: Project gate review and audit sampling of governance records.
evidence: Project charter; governance minutes; risk register; controls register; exception approvals.
auditFrequency: Each project gate and annual sample.
relatedPolicies: ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy; Enterprise Risk Management Policy; Internal Control Policy.
relatedProcedures: Project governance procedure; risk assessment guide; exception management procedure.
reviewTriggers: Policy, PSPF or PGPA changes; audit findings; material incident; major delivery model change.
notes: Use the simplest governance model that still manages the risk and impact of the project.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy
title: Portfolio investment, assurance, gate decisions and benefits
obligationDescription: Project proposals and gate decisions must align with NDIA corporate, digital investment and portfolio priorities; document options, costs, benefits, dependencies and risks; complete required IOF, DTA, contestability and assurance reviews; and track benefits, conditions and assurance actions through implementation and post-implementation review.
requirement: Project proposals and gate decisions must show that the project supports NDIA strategy and digital investment priorities. They must record options, costs, benefits, dependencies, risks, assurance actions and benefit tracking through delivery and review.

controlObjective: Confirm projects are affordable, justified, aligned to strategy, assured and able to realise benefits.

applicability: Projects that need funding, investment approval, assurance review, portfolio prioritisation or benefits tracking.
excluded: Minor operational activities with no investment decision or assurance requirement, as agreed by Portfolio Governance.
guidance: Use the NDIA investment pathway, prepare a business case, agree the assurance plan, and keep benefits and conditions visible.
technicalControls: Benefits tracking tool, decision log, assurance action register, and portfolio reporting dashboard.
processSteps: Prepare proposal; confirm tier and assurance needs; get gate approval; track conditions; complete benefits review.

evidence: Business case; IOF assessment; assurance plan; gate decisions; benefits map; conditions and action log; post-implementation review.

relatedProcedures: Business case guide; assurance planning guide; benefits management procedure.
reviewTriggers: New investment thresholds; DTA assurance changes; material scope, cost, benefit or risk change.
notes: Gate decisions should be based on current evidence, not earlier assumptions.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy
title: Architecture review, reuse, interoperability and integration
obligationDescription: Projects must complete architecture review before procurement or build, reuse existing NDIA, Commonwealth or market capabilities where practical, and design new solutions with reusable components, APIs, interoperability, integration standards, supportability and clear operational ownership.
requirement: Before buying or building technology, the project must complete architecture review. It must reuse existing NDIA, Commonwealth or market capabilities where practical, and design any new component so it can integrate, be supported and be reused.
obligationRef:
DIGRP-09 (Digital ICT Reuse): Australian Government Architecture - review before investment, ICT capability development or digital procurement
DIGRP-10 (Digital ICT Reuse): Digital and ICT Reuse Policy - reuse wherever possible
DIGRP-11 (Digital ICT Reuse): Digital and ICT Reuse Policy - design and build for reuse
DIGRP-12 (Digital ICT Reuse): AGA - consistent, interoperable and lower-risk digital outcomes
ismControls: ISM secure design, system boundary and security architecture practices, where applicable.
otherStandards: Australian Government Architecture; Digital and ICT Reuse Policy.
controlObjective: Promote reuse, interoperability, supportability and lower-risk digital outcomes.
threat: Duplicate systems, poor integration, unsupported technology, vendor lock-in or inconsistent user and data flows.
applicability: Projects that introduce, buy, build, integrate or materially change ICT capability.
excluded: Minor configuration changes with no architecture, integration or support impact, as agreed by Enterprise Architecture.
guidance: Check the reuse catalogue and approved patterns, complete solution design, and get design authority endorsement before procurement or build.
technicalControls: Approved architecture patterns, API and integration standards, reusable components, support model and service ownership records.
processSteps: Run reuse assessment; prepare architecture pack; review integration and data impacts; obtain design approval; update service ownership records.
responsible: Solution Architect; Project Manager; Integration Lead; Service Owner.
consulted: Enterprise Architecture; Cyber Security; Data; Operations; Business Owner; Procurement.
informed: Project Board; affected service owners; delivery teams.
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, limited
exceptionProcess: Document why reuse or the approved pattern is not suitable, with cost, risk, support and integration impacts.
exceptionAuthority: Enterprise Architecture Design Authority and Technology Owner.
verification: Architecture review and design authority decision.
evidence: Reuse assessment; solution architecture; integration design; support model; design approval record.
auditFrequency: Before procurement or build and at major design gates.
relatedPolicies: ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy; Enterprise Architecture Policy; Digital Reuse Policy.
relatedProcedures: Architecture review procedure; API and integration standards; service transition procedure.
reviewTriggers: New architecture standards; major design change; new integration; unsupported technology risk.
notes: Reuse is preferred, but it must still meet participant, business, security and support needs.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy
title: Participant-centred legal authority, privacy and protected Agency information
obligationDescription: Projects must confirm legal authority and business ownership, assess participant, provider and staff impacts, maintain traceable Scheme business rules and review pathways, and apply privacy-by-design and protected Agency information controls to all personal or NDIS information handling, including supplier handling.
requirement: Projects must confirm they have legal authority and a business owner for any use of participant, provider or staff information. Privacy must be built in from the start, including clear business rules, review pathways and controls for NDIA and supplier handling of protected information.
obligationRef:
NDIS-63 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act ss3-4 - objects and general principles
NDIS-64 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act ss117-119 - establishment, functions and powers of the Agency

PA-67 (Privacy Act APPs): Privacy Act s15 and Schedule 1 - Australian Privacy Principles

PA-69 (Privacy Act APPs): Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code s15 - PIA register
PA-71 (Privacy Act APPs): Privacy Act and APP contractual handling obligations
ismControls: ISM access control, logging, encryption and data protection practices, where personal or protected information is handled.
otherStandards: NDIS Act; NDIS Protection and Disclosure of Information Rules; Privacy Act and Australian Privacy Principles; Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code.
controlObjective: Make sure information is used lawfully, fairly, securely and in ways that protect participants, providers and staff.
threat: Unauthorised information use, privacy breach, harm to participants, unlawful disclosure or weak supplier handling.
applicability: Projects that handle personal information, NDIS information, protected Agency information or affect participants, providers or staff.
excluded: Projects with no personal or protected information and no participant, provider or staff impact, confirmed by Privacy and Legal.
guidance: Confirm legal authority, complete privacy screening or a PIA, map data flows, document business rules, and apply controls to suppliers.
technicalControls: Role-based access, least privilege, audit logging, encryption, masking, secure transfer, retention controls and supplier access controls.
processSteps: Confirm legal basis; appoint information owner; complete privacy assessment; approve data flows; include supplier privacy terms; test controls.
responsible: Project Manager; Privacy Officer; Data Owner; Product Owner; Supplier Manager.
consulted: Legal; Cyber Security; Records; Participant Experience; Procurement.
informed: Project Board; affected business areas; support teams.
exceptionsPermitted: No for legal authority. Limited for control implementation.
exceptionProcess: Legal and privacy obligations cannot be waived. Any control variation must record risk, compensating controls and end date.
exceptionAuthority: Privacy Officer and General Counsel for privacy or legal matters; CISO for security control variations.
verification: Privacy, legal and security review before go-live and after material change.
evidence: Legal authority statement; privacy threshold assessment or PIA; data flow map; privacy notices; business rules; supplier clauses.
auditFrequency: At privacy checkpoints, go-live and annual sample.
relatedPolicies: ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy; Privacy Policy; Protected Information Policy; Data Governance Policy.
relatedProcedures: Privacy impact assessment procedure; information handling guide; supplier privacy checklist.
reviewTriggers: New data use; new supplier; privacy incident; change to NDIS or Privacy Act obligations; high privacy risk finding.
notes: Privacy and protected information controls should be designed before data is collected or shared.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy
title: Information classification, caveats, external sharing and DATA Scheme controls
obligationDescription: Projects must classify information and data holdings, apply required markings, caveats and handling controls, restrict access and external, offshore or international sharing to authorised need-to-know arrangements, and use DATA Scheme data sharing agreements and safeguards only where approved.
requirement: Projects must classify information and data, mark it correctly, and limit access or sharing to people and organisations with an authorised need to know. External, offshore or international sharing must be approved before it happens, and DATA Scheme sharing must use approved agreements and safeguards.

exceptionAuthority: Data Owner and Information Security delegate; Privacy and Legal for external or protected information sharing.

evidence: Classification assessment; data inventory; access model; access review; data sharing agreement; offshore or external sharing approval.

notes: Access should be granted to the minimum people needed to deliver and operate the service.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy
title: Records, FOI readiness, metadata, retention, disposal and decommissioning
obligationDescription: Projects must create, store and maintain complete auditable records, metadata, FOI-searchable evidence and decision trails in approved systems, and retain, transfer, decommission or dispose of information and technology assets only under approved records, security and disposal authorities.
requirement: Projects must create and keep accurate records of decisions, approvals, designs, testing and operations in approved NDIA systems. Records must be searchable for FOI and audit, and data or technology assets must only be retained, transferred, decommissioned or disposed of under approved authorities.

guidance: Use approved repositories, agree metadata, keep key decisions and approvals, and plan retention and disposal before decommissioning.
technicalControls: Approved records repository, metadata, retention labels, audit logs, backup, secure sanitisation and disposal records.
processSteps: Set up records plan; store evidence; tag metadata; support FOI search; approve retention, transfer, disposal and decommissioning.
responsible: Project Manager; Records Manager; Product Owner; Service Owner.
consulted: Legal; FOI; Cyber Security; Data Owner; Operations.
informed: Project Board; affected business areas; audit and assurance teams.

exceptionProcess: Record the temporary arrangement, risk, owner, end date and migration plan to an approved records system.
exceptionAuthority: Records Manager or Information Governance delegate; Legal for FOI or statutory matters; CISO for secure disposal.
verification: Records and decommissioning review at gates, go-live and closure.
evidence: Records management plan; decision log; evidence repository; FOI search approach; disposal approvals; decommissioning plan.
auditFrequency: At project closure and annual sample.
relatedPolicies: ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy; Records Management Policy; Information Security Policy; Data Governance Policy.
relatedProcedures: Records management procedure; FOI search guide; decommissioning and disposal procedure.
reviewTriggers: Project closure; system decommissioning; FOI request; records authority change; audit finding.
notes: A clear decision trail reduces delivery risk and supports FOI, audit and future maintenance.

policyTitle: NDIA ICT Technology Enabled Projects Policy
title: Secure-by-design lifecycle, system definition, change control and authorisation
obligationDescription: Projects must apply an ISM-aligned secure technology lifecycle by defining system boundaries, security objectives, classifications, owners, authorised technology registers and material change triggers; prohibited or legacy technology must have approved mitigations, and no system may go live or continue after material change until residual risk is assessed and authorised.
requirement: Projects must use a secure-by-design lifecycle. They must define the system boundary, owners, security goals, classification and change triggers, record the technology in approved registers, and get residual risk authorised before go-live or after a material change.

evidence: System security plan; risk assessment; control test results; security assessment report; risk acceptance; technology register entry.

title: Cloud, hosting, outsourced ICT, gateways and shared responsibility

requirement: Projects that use cloud, hosting, gateways, data centres or outsourced ICT must check security and hosting evidence before approval. They must define who is responsible for each control, where data is stored, how services are monitored, backed up, recovered, costed and exited.

Identity risks, shared risks, residual risks and control exceptions must be assessed against NDIA's risk appetite, documented, time bound, treated or escalated before approval.

title: Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance
obligationDescription: Procurements, contracts, cloud services and third-party arrangements involving NDIA identities, identity data, credentials or system access must include identity, privacy, security, audit, offboarding, breach-notification and subcontractor controls. Suppliers must comply with NDIA requirements, provide assurance evidence and support timely revocation, data return and risk reassessment through the contract lifecycle.
requirement: Any supplier, cloud service or third party that handles NDIA identities, identity data, credentials or system access must follow NDIA identity, privacy and security requirements before access is granted and throughout the contract. Contracts must require assurance evidence, timely offboarding and breach reporting.

section: 3. Classified, caveated and protected information access
title: Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access
obligationDescription: Access to NDIA information must be authorised according to information value, sensitivity, classification, caveat, metadata, lawful NDIS purpose, verified need-to-know, clearance or citizenship conditions and approved disclosure authority. Protected Agency information must only be accessed, used, disclosed or externally shared by authorised identities for approved roles, functions and recipients.
requirement: People and systems may only access NDIA information when their identity, role, need to know, clearance or caveat conditions and lawful purpose have been verified. Protected Agency information must only be used or shared by authorised identities for approved NDIA functions.

section: 4. Identity proofing, assurance and authority verification
title: Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority
obligationDescription: NDIA must use risk-based identity assurance before issuing or relying on an identity, credential or access right. Workforce, contractors, providers, representatives, participants, nominees, organisations and external verification services must be identity-proofed, eligibility or authority checked, fraud screened, and linked to verified evidence or authoritative sources using only necessary data and approved verification channels.
requirement: Before the NDIA creates or trusts an identity, it must check that the person, organisation, representative, provider, participant or system is who they claim to be and has the right authority. Checks must be risk based, use approved sources and collect only the information needed.

requirement: Every human and non-human identity must have access requested, approved, provisioned, reviewed, changed and removed through a managed process. Access must be unique, traceable, least privilege, role based, segregated where needed and promptly removed when no longer required.
