notes: This requirement should be placed close to authentication and least-privilege clauses in the policy.

title: Identity platform, application and infrastructure security
obligationDescription: Identity platforms, directories, federation components, authentication services, access-control integrations and administration workstations must be designed, configured, patched, hardened, backed up and recovered using ISM, Essential Eight and approved secure-application controls, including server-side authorisation, secure sessions, token validation, TLS and protection against credential or token theft.
requirement: Identity platforms and connected applications must be securely designed, hardened, patched, backed up and recovered. They must enforce server-side authorisation, secure sessions, validated tokens, current TLS and protection against credential or token theft.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 85 (PSPF 2025): 13. Technology Lifecycle Management
ISM-1110 (ISM): ISM - Guidelines for software development: authentication and authorization
E8-94 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - Patch applications
E8-95 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - Patch operating systems
E8-97 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - User application hardening
E8-98 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - Regular backups
E8-99 (Essential Eight): Essential Eight - Assessment process
FAPP-07 (Federation / FAPP standards): TLS 1.3 RFC 8446
ismControls: ISM-1110 (ISM): ISM - Guidelines for software development: authentication and authorization
otherStandards: PSPF 2025; Essential Eight; Federation / FAPP standards
controlObjective: Ensure identity services and applications are secure, resilient and resistant to common authentication and authorisation attacks.
threat: Vulnerable identity infrastructure, broken authorisation, token theft, insecure TLS, patch gaps, misconfiguration and failed recovery.
applicability: Identity platforms, directories, federation components, authentication services, access-control integrations, administration workstations and connected applications.
excluded: Systems with no identity or access-control role, except where they support identity platform infrastructure or recovery.
guidance: Build secure-by-design patterns into identity platforms and applications. Keep configuration baselines, patching and recovery evidence current.
technicalControls: Secure baselines; patching; vulnerability management; server-side authorisation; secure cookies and sessions; token validation; TLS 1.3 where supported; backups.
processSteps: Design to approved patterns, assess security, harden, patch, test authorisation and recovery, monitor vulnerabilities and remediate within agreed timeframes.
responsible: Platform Engineering; Application Owners; Cyber Security Engineering; IAM team; Change Management
consulted: Cyber Architecture; Security Operations Centre; Business Owners; Vendor Support
informed: System owners; application teams; service desk; affected users during changes
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, controlled exception only where risk is accepted and compensating controls are in place.
exceptionProcess: Raise a security exception for unsupported hardening, patching, backup or protocol requirements with remediation dates and monitoring controls.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and relevant Platform or Application Owner.
verification: Configuration review, vulnerability scan, penetration or security test, backup and recovery test and change record review.
evidence: Secure design records; configuration baselines; patch reports; vulnerability reports; test results; backup and recovery evidence.
auditFrequency: Quarterly configuration and vulnerability review; annual recovery test.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Secure System Development Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Change Management Policy; Backup Policy
relatedProcedures: Identity platform hardening standard; secure application design guide; vulnerability management procedure; backup and recovery procedure
reviewTriggers: New identity platform; major application release; vulnerability; penetration test finding; Essential Eight or ISM update.
notes: This requirement connects identity policy to secure build, hardening, application security and resilience controls.

section: 10. Federation, Digital ID and API trust
title: Federation, Digital ID, APIs and relying-party trust
obligationDescription: Federated identity, Digital ID, SSO, APIs and identity-provider integrations must be approved, documented and operated under current standards and relying-party obligations. NDIA must validate identity-provider trust, assertions, claims, tokens, scopes, metadata, revocation arrangements and audit identifiers, share only required attributes, and transition legacy terminology to current Digital ID requirements.
requirement: Federated identity, Digital ID, single sign-on, APIs and relying-party integrations must be approved and documented before use. The NDIA must validate provider trust, claims, tokens, scopes, attributes and audit identifiers, and share only the attributes needed.
obligationRef:
NDIS-80 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act s 66 and related rules - Disclosure by CEO or delegate
DID-24 (Digital ID Act): Digital ID Act 2024 - Framework for regulated Digital ID services
DID-26 (Digital ID Act): Digital ID Rules 2024
DID-27 (Digital ID Act): Digital ID Accreditation Rules 2024 - accreditation obligations
DID-30 (Digital ID Act): Digital ID (AGDIS) Data Standards 2024 - SAML data flows and relying party audit identifiers
DID-32 (Digital ID Act): Trusted Digital Identity Framework (TDIF) transition
DIG-31 (Digital Experience Policy): Digital Service Standard - Connect services
FAPP-01 (Federation / FAPP standards): OASIS SAML 2.0
FAPP-02 (Federation / FAPP standards): OpenID Connect Core 1.0
FAPP-03 (Federation / FAPP standards): OAuth 2.1 and OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice RFC 9700
FAPP-08 (Federation / FAPP standards): OAuth token revocation, introspection and proof-of-possession profiles
NIST-SP-04 (NIST Digital Identity / Zero Trust): NIST SP 800-63C - Federation and assertions
ismControls: No direct ISM control listed in source register.
otherStandards: NDIS Act; Digital ID Act; Digital Experience Policy; Federation / FAPP standards; NIST Digital Identity / Zero Trust
controlCategory: Federation, Digital ID and API trust
controlObjective: Use trusted identity integrations that share only necessary information and can be audited end to end.
threat: Excessive attribute sharing, weak trust setup, token misuse, federation misconfiguration, untraceable transactions and non-compliance with Digital ID obligations.
applicability: Federated identity, Digital ID, SSO, SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth, APIs, relying-party connections and identity-provider integrations.
excluded: Integrations that do not exchange NDIA identity attributes, authentication assertions, tokens, credentials or protected information.
guidance: Document each trust relationship and relying-party obligation. Prefer current federation and API security standards and minimise identity attributes.
technicalControls: Federation metadata validation; signed assertions or tokens; scope controls; token revocation and introspection; attribute release controls; API gateway logging.
processSteps: Assess business need, approve trust model, configure claims and scopes, test security, record audit identifiers, monitor usage and review the integration annually.
accountable: Digital Identity and Federation Service Owner
responsible: IAM Federation team; API Platform team; Application Owners; Cyber Security Architecture
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Digital Service Owners; Records Management; External identity providers
informed: Relying-party owners; service teams; support teams; affected users where notices are required
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, controlled exception only for legacy integrations with an approved transition plan.
exceptionProcess: Document the legacy gap, risk, compensating controls, data minimisation approach, audit limitations and transition date.
exceptionAuthority: Digital Identity Service Owner with CISO and Privacy Officer approval for high-risk integrations.
verification: Integration design review, claims and scopes review, token validation test, privacy review and audit log sampling.
evidence: Federation design; metadata; approved claims and scopes; privacy assessment; test results; relying-party records; audit logs.
auditFrequency: At onboarding, after material change and annually for active integrations.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Digital Service Policy; API Security Policy; Privacy Policy; Information Sharing Policy
relatedProcedures: Federation onboarding procedure; Digital ID relying-party guide; API integration security standard; attribute release approval procedure
reviewTriggers: New identity provider; Digital ID rule change; federation standard update; material claim or scope change; privacy concern.
notes: This requirement supports future-facing SSO, Digital ID and API trust patterns while preserving privacy and auditability.

title: Non-human identities, PKI, certificates and keys
obligationDescription: Non-human identities, service accounts, devices, workloads, organisation credentials, certificates and cryptographic keys used for identity or federation must have an accountable owner, approved purpose, verified subject, minimum privileges, secure key storage, expiry monitoring, renewal, rotation, revocation, trust validation and logging equivalent to the risk of their access.
requirement: Service accounts, workloads, devices, certificates, cryptographic keys and other non-human identities must have an accountable owner, approved purpose, minimum privileges, secure storage, expiry, rotation, renewal, revocation and monitoring.
obligationRef:
ISM-1111 (ISM): ISM - Cryptography and certificate management controls
ISM-1112 (ISM): ISM - System administration and service account management
GATE-PKI-01 (Gatekeeper PKI): Gatekeeper PKI Framework
GATE-PKI-02 (Gatekeeper PKI): Gatekeeper - Subscriber identity assurance
GATE-PKI-03 (Gatekeeper PKI): Gatekeeper - Certificate lifecycle
GATE-PKI-04 (Gatekeeper PKI): Gatekeeper - Private key protection
GATE-PKI-05 (Gatekeeper PKI): Gatekeeper - Revocation and status checking
GATE-PKI-06 (Gatekeeper PKI): Gatekeeper - Organisation and role certificates
NIST-SP-08 (NIST Digital Identity / Zero Trust): NIST SP 800-207A - Identity-centric access control
ismControls:
ISM-1111 (ISM): ISM - Cryptography and certificate management controls
ISM-1112 (ISM): ISM - System administration and service account management
otherStandards: Gatekeeper PKI; NIST Digital Identity / Zero Trust
controlObjective: Control machine and service identities with the same discipline as human identities, adjusted for their technical risk.
threat: Secret leakage, expired certificates, over-privileged service accounts, unmanaged workload identities and unauthorised automated access.
applicability: Service accounts, workload identities, device identities, organisation credentials, certificates, cryptographic keys and secrets used for identity or federation.
excluded: Human user accounts, which are covered by lifecycle, authentication and privileged access requirements.
guidance: Inventory non-human identities and certificates. Avoid shared secrets where possible and rotate or revoke credentials on a defined schedule.
technicalControls: Secrets vault; certificate lifecycle management; key management; owner and purpose metadata; minimum privileges; expiry monitoring; automated rotation; logging.
processSteps: Register the identity, assign owner and purpose, approve privileges, store secrets securely, monitor expiry, rotate or renew and revoke when no longer needed.
responsible: Platform Engineering; Application Teams; IAM team; PKI Administrators; DevSecOps
consulted: Cyber Architecture; Security Operations Centre; Records Management; Vendor Support
informed: Application owners; platform owners; change managers; operational support teams
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, controlled exception only where a technical limitation prevents standard lifecycle controls.
exceptionProcess: Record the non-human identity, technical constraint, risk, compensating controls, expiry and remediation date in the exception register.
exceptionAuthority: Identity Platform Owner and CISO for high-risk or internet-facing identities.
verification: Inventory review, certificate and secret expiry report, privilege review and rotation evidence sampling.
evidence: Non-human identity register; owner and purpose records; certificate inventory; key rotation logs; vault records; revocation evidence.
auditFrequency: Monthly expiry monitoring and quarterly service-account and secret review.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Cryptography Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Secure Development Policy; Change Management Policy
relatedProcedures: Service account procedure; certificate lifecycle procedure; secrets management standard; key rotation procedure
reviewTriggers: Expired or compromised secret; new platform; certificate authority change; cryptography requirement change; service account audit finding.
notes: This requirement covers machine identities and certificates that are often missed by human-user access processes.

title: Monitoring, logging, telemetry, audit evidence and certification
obligationDescription: Identity events, access grants, verification checks, protected-information access, privileged actions and high-risk access activity must be logged, protected, retained with useful metadata, monitored for anomalous or suspicious activity, and periodically reviewed or certified by accountable owners to support audit, investigation and risk response.
requirement: Identity events, access grants, privileged actions and high-risk access must be logged, protected and monitored. Accountable owners must regularly review and certify access so the NDIA can detect misuse, investigate incidents and prove compliance.
obligationRef:
ISM-1109 (ISM): ISM - Event logging and monitoring controls
NDIS-79 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act ss 63-64 - Soliciting or offering protected information
NDIS-83 (NDIS Act): NDIS Act - Evidence and accountability
IDVS-06 (IDVS Act): IVS audit and reporting
CRMP-27 (CRMP): Risk oversight and internal accountability
NIST-SP-07 (NIST Digital Identity / Zero Trust): NIST SP 800-207 - Continuous diagnostics and telemetry
ismControls: ISM-1109 (ISM): ISM - Event logging and monitoring controls
otherStandards: NDIS Act; IDVS Act; CRMP; NIST Digital Identity / Zero Trust
controlObjective: Provide reliable evidence that identity controls are working and that suspicious access can be detected and investigated.
threat: Undetected account misuse, missing evidence, poor incident investigation, unauthorised access remaining active and failed audit accountability.
applicability: Identity events, access approvals, access grants, privileged actions, high-risk access activity, protected-information access and access certifications.
excluded: Operational logs unrelated to identity or access are covered by broader monitoring requirements.
guidance: Define the minimum events to log and retain. Protect logs from alteration and ensure owners certify access at the required interval.
technicalControls: Central logging; SIEM monitoring; alert rules; immutable or protected logs; access certification tooling; anomaly detection; log retention controls.
processSteps: Collect identity events, protect and retain logs, monitor alerts, review access, certify outcomes, remediate issues and keep evidence for audit.
responsible: Security Operations Centre; IAM Assurance team; System Owners; Data Owners; Audit and Compliance team
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Internal Audit; Records Management; Business Owners
informed: Access approvers; accountable owners; incident responders; executive governance forums
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, controlled exception only where logging or certification is technically unavailable and compensating monitoring exists.
exceptionProcess: Record the logging or certification gap, risk, compensating control, remediation date and owner in the exception register.
exceptionAuthority: CISO and relevant System Owner; Privacy Officer for monitoring involving personal information risk.
verification: Log source coverage review, alert testing, access certification completion check and audit evidence sampling.
evidence: Log source inventory; SIEM alerts; access certification reports; review attestations; investigation records; remediation tickets.
auditFrequency: Continuous monitoring with quarterly certification and annual audit sampling.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Logging and Monitoring Policy; Cyber Security Policy; Access Control Policy; Records Management Policy
relatedProcedures: Identity logging standard; access certification procedure; monitoring and alert response playbook; audit evidence guide
reviewTriggers: New identity platform; missing log source; incident; audit finding; retention requirement change; monitoring control update.
notes: This requirement provides the evidence base for identity assurance, investigations and compliance reporting.

title: Privacy, data minimisation and individual rights
obligationDescription: Identity information must be collected, used, disclosed, secured and corrected in accordance with privacy obligations. NDIA must provide clear privacy notices, collect only necessary attributes and evidence, use approved identifiers, maintain data quality, assess high privacy-risk identity changes through PIAs, involve privacy expertise, train identity personnel and apply privacy-by-design controls.
requirement: The NDIA must handle identity information in line with privacy obligations. It must be clear about why information is collected, collect only what is needed, keep it accurate and secure, complete privacy impact assessments for high-risk changes and support access and correction rights.
obligationRef:
PA-84 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 1 - Open and transparent management of personal information
PA-86 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 3 - Collection of solicited personal information
PA-87 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 5 - Notification of collection
PA-88 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 6 - Use or disclosure of personal information
PA-90 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 9 - Adoption, use or disclosure of government related identifiers
PA-91 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 10 - Quality of personal information
PA-92 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 11.1 - Security of personal information
PA-94 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 12 and APP 13 - Access and correction
PC-33 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy governance requirements
PC-34 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy management plan
PC-35 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy Impact Assessments for high privacy risk projects
PC-36 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy training and awareness
PC-37 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy by design
PC-39 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - High privacy risk project definition
PC-40 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy Officer
PC-41 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy Champion
PC-42 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Privacy capability
ismControls: No direct ISM control listed in source register.
otherStandards: Privacy Act APPs; Privacy Code
controlObjective: Protect personal information used for identity management and respect individuals privacy rights.
threat: Over-collection, unclear notices, inaccurate identity data, unauthorised use, privacy breach and failure to support access or correction rights.
applicability: All personal information, identifiers, evidence, attributes, logs and decisions used to create, verify, manage or audit identities.
excluded: De-identified information where re-identification is not reasonably possible and it is not used to make identity or access decisions.
guidance: Apply privacy by design from the start. Use the minimum attributes needed and complete PIAs for high privacy-risk identity changes.
technicalControls: Data minimisation; access controls; encryption; audit logging; approved identifiers; data quality checks; retention controls; privacy notices and consent records where relevant.
processSteps: Identify personal information, confirm lawful purpose, provide notice, minimise collection, secure data, complete PIA when needed and support access or correction requests.
responsible: IAM Service Owner; Data Owners; System Owners; Privacy team; Records Management
consulted: Legal; Cyber Security; Service Design; Fraud Control; Business Owners
informed: Individuals whose information is collected; staff handling identity information; service teams
exceptionsPermitted: No for privacy law obligations; implementation exceptions only where privacy risk is formally accepted.
exceptionProcess: Seek Privacy Officer advice, document privacy risk, complete or update PIA if required and approve only with clear controls and expiry.
exceptionAuthority: Privacy Officer and relevant Business Owner; CISO for security control exceptions.
verification: Privacy impact assessment review, access-control audit, data quality sampling and review of notices and retention controls.
evidence: Privacy notices; PIAs; data mapping; access logs; data quality reports; access or correction request records; training records.
auditFrequency: At least annually and for each high privacy-risk identity change.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Privacy Policy; Data Governance Policy; Records Management Policy; Cyber Security Policy
relatedProcedures: Privacy impact assessment procedure; identity data handling guide; access and correction procedure; data minimisation guide
reviewTriggers: New identity data collection; high privacy-risk project; data breach; Privacy Act or Privacy Code update; complaint or audit finding.
notes: This requirement should be easy for policy readers to understand because identity management relies heavily on personal information.

title: Identity incident, breach response and notification
obligationDescription: NDIA must maintain identity incident and breach playbooks that rapidly triage suspected compromise of identity information, credentials, authentication, authorisation or access controls; contain harm by revoking credentials, sessions, accounts and secrets; notify affected individuals, the OAIC, suppliers or other reporting pathways where required; preserve evidence; perform root-cause analysis and track remediation.
requirement: The NDIA must have identity incident and data breach playbooks. Suspected compromise of identity data, credentials or access controls must be triaged quickly, contained by revoking access or secrets, notified where required, investigated and remediated.
obligationRef:
PSPF - 42 (PSPF 2025): 06. Third Party Risk Management
NDB-21 (NDB Scheme): NDB scheme - Eligible data breach
NDB-22 (NDB Scheme): NDB scheme - Assessment of suspected breach
NDB-23 (NDB Scheme): NDB scheme - Notify affected individuals and OAIC
NDB-24 (NDB Scheme): NDB scheme - Remedial action
NDB-25 (NDB Scheme): NDB scheme - Supplier and third-party breaches
NDB-26 (NDB Scheme): NDB scheme - Post-incident improvement
ismControls: No direct ISM control listed in source register.
otherStandards: PSPF 2025; NDB Scheme
controlObjective: Respond quickly and lawfully when identity data, credentials, authentication or access controls are compromised.
threat: Account takeover, credential compromise, data breach, delayed notification, evidence loss and repeated identity-control failure.
applicability: Incidents involving identity information, credentials, authenticators, secrets, sessions, access controls, privileged access or identity suppliers.
excluded: Non-identity incidents are handled under the broader cyber incident and privacy breach response processes.
guidance: Keep playbooks current and test them. Ensure the first response includes containment actions such as revoking sessions, credentials, tokens and secrets.
technicalControls: Incident ticketing; credential and session revocation; PAM emergency controls; SIEM alerts; forensic log retention; breach notification workflow; supplier escalation channels.
processSteps: Triage, contain, preserve evidence, assess harm and notification duties, notify required parties, remediate root cause and track lessons learned.
responsible: Cyber Incident Response team; Security Operations Centre; IAM team; Privacy team; Supplier Managers
consulted: Legal; Communications; Records Management; Business Owners; External providers where relevant
informed: Affected individuals where required; executive governance; system owners; service desk; suppliers
exceptionsPermitted: No for mandatory breach notification duties; operational deviations must be recorded after urgent containment.
exceptionProcess: During an active incident, record deviations in the incident log and obtain post-incident approval and remediation actions.
exceptionAuthority: CISO; Privacy Officer for eligible data breach assessment and notification decisions.
verification: Playbook exercise, post-incident review, containment evidence review and breach notification decision audit.
evidence: Incident tickets; playbooks; revocation logs; forensic evidence; breach assessment; notification records; root cause analysis; remediation plan.
auditFrequency: After each identity incident and through an annual identity incident exercise.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Cyber Incident Response Policy; Privacy Policy; Data Breach Response Policy; Supplier Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: Identity compromise playbook; notifiable data breach procedure; credential revocation procedure; supplier incident escalation procedure
reviewTriggers: Identity incident; suspected eligible data breach; exercise finding; supplier breach; NDB or PSPF change.
notes: This requirement should cross-reference the broader cyber incident and privacy breach response arrangements.

title: Records, retention, metadata and disposal
obligationDescription: Identity lifecycle records, identity evidence, audit records, metadata, access decisions, PIAs, logs and operational identity datasets must be captured, owned, protected, retained, searchable, disposed of or transferred only under approved records authorities and with enough metadata to reconstruct identity, access and privileged activity.
requirement: The NDIA must keep reliable records of identity proofing, access decisions, approvals, audit logs, PIAs and identity lifecycle events. Records must be protected, searchable, retained and disposed of or transferred only under approved records authorities.
obligationRef:
PA-93 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 11.2 - Destruction or de-identification
PC-38 (Privacy Code): Privacy Code - Register and review of PIAs
ARC-64 (Archives Act): Archives Act 1983 - Commonwealth records
ARC-65 (Archives Act): NAA Information Management Standard
ARC-66 (Archives Act): Information Management Standard Principle 4 - Suitably stored and preserved
ARC-67 (Archives Act): Information Management Standard Principle 6 - Accountable destruction or transfer
ARC-68 (Archives Act): Records authorities
ARC-69 (Archives Act): Data and datasets as records
ARC-70 (Archives Act): Audit accessibility and retrieval
ismControls: No direct ISM control listed in source register.
otherStandards: Privacy Act APPs; Privacy Code; Archives Act
controlObjective: Keep identity records long enough to prove decisions, support audits and meet records and privacy obligations.
threat: Lost evidence, unlawful disposal, excessive retention, inability to reconstruct access decisions and inability to support investigations.
applicability: Identity lifecycle records, evidence, approvals, access decisions, PIAs, audit logs, metadata and operational identity datasets.
excluded: Records that do not relate to identity, access, identity evidence, identity risks or access-control decisions.
guidance: Apply approved retention and disposal rules to identity data and logs. Keep enough metadata to reconstruct who had access and why.
technicalControls: Records classification; retention labels; protected storage; searchable audit repositories; disposal controls; legal hold; metadata standards.
processSteps: Identify record type, assign owner and retention rule, protect the record, retain and retrieve when needed, then dispose of or transfer under authority.
responsible: Records Management; IAM team; System Owners; Data Owners; Privacy team
consulted: Legal; Cyber Security; Internal Audit; Business Owners
informed: Identity process owners; access approvers; audit and compliance teams
exceptionsPermitted: No for records authority requirements; retention or disposal changes need formal records approval.
exceptionProcess: Seek Records Manager advice, document legal or business need and obtain approval before varying retention, disposal or transfer controls.
exceptionAuthority: Records Manager with Legal and Privacy input where needed.
verification: Records inventory review, retention and disposal sampling, audit evidence retrieval test and metadata quality check.
evidence: Retention schedules; records authority mapping; disposal approvals; audit log retention evidence; metadata samples; retrieval test results.
auditFrequency: At least annually, with targeted review after system decommissioning or major identity process change.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Records Management Policy; Privacy Policy; Data Governance Policy; Cyber Security Policy
relatedProcedures: Identity records retention guide; audit log retention procedure; records disposal procedure; data set management guide
reviewTriggers: New identity record type; system decommissioning; retention authority change; audit finding; privacy requirement change.
notes: This requirement ensures identity evidence remains usable for accountability without keeping personal information longer than allowed.

title: Accessible, inclusive and user-centred identity services
obligationDescription: Identity journeys must be designed as accessible digital services that are transparent, inclusive, plain-language, measurable and supported by assisted or alternative channels. Standard identity, Digital ID, MFA and recovery controls must not create unlawful or discriminatory barriers and must provide secure alternatives for people who cannot use default pathways.
requirement: NDIA identity services must be accessible, inclusive and easy to understand. People who cannot use standard Digital ID, MFA or account recovery pathways must be offered secure alternatives or assisted support that do not create unfair barriers.
obligationRef:
PA-85 (Privacy Act APPs): APP 2 - Anonymity and pseudonymity
DID-25 (Digital ID Act): Digital ID Act 2024 - Voluntary, secure, convenient and inclusive identity verification
DIG-27 (Digital Experience Policy): Digital Experience Policy - mandated from 1 January 2025
DIG-28 (Digital Experience Policy): Digital Service Standard - Leave no one behind
DIG-29 (Digital Experience Policy): Digital Service Standard - Build trust in design
DIG-30 (Digital Experience Policy): Digital Service Standard - Do no harm
DIG-32 (Digital Experience Policy): Digital Service Standard - Monitor service performance
DIG-33 (Digital Experience Policy): Digital Service Standard transition guidance
DIS-08 (Digital Inclusion Standard): Digital Inclusion Standard
DIS-09 (Digital Inclusion Standard): Digital Inclusion Standard criterion 4 - Make it accessible
DIS-11 (Digital Inclusion Standard): Australian Human Rights Commission - Equal access to digital goods and services
DIS-12 (Digital Inclusion Standard): Digital Inclusion Standard - Assisted digital support
DIS-14 (Digital Inclusion Standard): Plain language and content accessibility
ismControls: No direct ISM control listed in source register.
otherStandards: Privacy Act APPs; Digital ID Act; Digital Experience Policy; Digital Inclusion Standard
controlObjective: Make identity services secure without excluding people who need accessible, assisted or alternative channels.
threat: Digital exclusion, inaccessible authentication, privacy confusion, poor service outcomes, insecure workarounds and reduced trust in NDIA services.
applicability: Participant, provider, representative, workforce and supplier identity journeys, including Digital ID, MFA, recovery, notices and assisted support channels.
excluded: Purely internal technical controls with no user journey, except where they affect authentication usability or recovery.
guidance: Design identity journeys with accessibility, plain language and assisted support from the start. Test alternatives so they remain secure and usable.
technicalControls: Accessible authentication options; assisted digital workflows; secure alternative verification; plain-language notices; service metrics; WCAG-aligned interfaces.
processSteps: Research user needs, design accessible pathways, test with users, approve secure alternatives, monitor completion and support rates, and improve weak points.
responsible: Service Design; IAM team; Digital Delivery; Contact Centre; Accessibility specialists
consulted: Privacy; Cyber Security; Legal; Participant and Provider service teams; Communications
informed: Users; support staff; service owners; external partners where service journeys connect
exceptionsPermitted: No for mandatory accessibility obligations; implementation constraints need a documented remediation plan.
exceptionProcess: Record the accessibility issue, impact, interim support pathway, risk and remediation date in the service improvement backlog.
exceptionAuthority: Digital Service Owner with Accessibility Lead, Privacy Officer and CISO input for security-sensitive alternatives.
verification: Accessibility testing, service performance monitoring, user feedback review and assurance that alternative pathways remain secure.
evidence: User research; accessibility test results; plain-language content review; assisted support procedure; service metrics; issue remediation records.
auditFrequency: At least annually and after material identity journey changes.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Digital Service Policy; Accessibility Policy; Privacy Policy; Customer Service Policy
relatedProcedures: Accessible authentication guide; assisted digital procedure; plain-language content guide; service performance measurement guide
reviewTriggers: New identity journey; accessibility complaint; service performance issue; Digital Service Standard or Digital Inclusion Standard update.
notes: This requirement keeps the identity policy usable for participants and providers, not only for technical teams.

title: Responsible AI and automated agent identity controls
obligationDescription: AI systems, AI agents and automated identity decision support must be registered, risk-assessed and governed as identities where they can access, process, decide or act in NDIA systems. AI agents must have accountable owners, purpose-limited permissions, approved data access, logs, explainable and testable controls, and human accountability for privileged or conflicting access changes.
requirement: AI systems, AI agents and automated identity decision tools must be registered, risk assessed and managed as identities when they can access, process or act in NDIA systems. They must have human owners, purpose-limited access, logs, testing and human accountability for high-risk decisions.
obligationRef:
RAI-25 (Responsible AI): Policy for responsible use of AI in government
RAI-26 (Responsible AI): AI policy - Accountability
RAI-27 (Responsible AI): AI policy - Strategy and oversight
RAI-28 (Responsible AI): AI use case impact assessment
RAI-29 (Responsible AI): AI policy - Staff training
RAI-30 (Responsible AI): AI policy - Data governance, cyber, privacy and ethics alignment
RAI-31 (Responsible AI): National AI assurance framework
RAI-32 (Responsible AI): Agentic system safety controls
ismControls: No direct ISM control listed in source register.
otherStandards: Responsible AI
controlObjective: Ensure AI and automation cannot make or act on identity and access decisions without ownership, limits, evidence and human accountability.
threat: Uncontrolled automated access, opaque identity decisions, excessive permissions, data misuse, model or agent error and accountability gaps.
applicability: AI systems, AI agents, bots and automated decision-support tools that access, process, decide or act in NDIA identity or access processes.
excluded: Automation with no access, identity, personal information or decision impact.
guidance: Treat AI agents as identities when they can act in systems. Record purpose, owner, permissions, data access, testing and human review points.
technicalControls: AI use-case register; service identities; least privilege; approval workflow; audit logging; human-in-the-loop checks; test evidence; data access controls.
processSteps: Register the AI use case, assess risk, assign owner, approve access, test controls, monitor activity and review outcomes before expanding permissions.
accountable: Responsible AI Governance Lead and CISO
responsible: AI Product Owners; IAM team; Data and Analytics; Cyber Security; System Owners
consulted: Privacy; Legal; Ethics or Responsible AI forum; Fraud Control; Business Owners
informed: Affected process owners; users where transparency is required; executive governance forums
exceptionsPermitted: Yes, controlled exception only for low-risk pilots with defined limits and oversight.
exceptionProcess: Document pilot scope, risk, data access, human oversight, expiry date and conditions before use in identity or access processes.
exceptionAuthority: Responsible AI Governance Lead, CISO and relevant Business Owner; Privacy Officer for personal information use.
verification: AI use-case register review, access review, log sampling, model or agent control testing and human-accountability check.
evidence: AI impact assessment; use-case register; access approvals; logs; test results; human review records; risk acceptance records.
auditFrequency: At least annually and before new or materially changed AI identity use cases go live.

title: Critical infrastructure and conditional SOCI identity obligations
obligationDescription: Where SOCI or critical-infrastructure obligations apply, NDIA must assess identity services, identity data stores and suppliers for applicability; include identity, privileged access and supplier access controls in the risk management program; apply required data storage and processing controls; and support cyber incident, ransomware and third-party reporting obligations.
requirement: When critical infrastructure or SOCI obligations apply, the NDIA must assess identity services, data stores and suppliers for those obligations. Required identity, privileged access, data storage, supplier and incident reporting controls must be built into the risk management program.
obligationRef:
SOCI-37 (SOCI Act): SOCI Act 2018 - Critical infrastructure sectors and assets
SOCI-38 (SOCI Act): SOCI - Critical infrastructure risk management program (CIRMP)
SOCI-39 (SOCI Act): SOCI - Data storage or processing assets
SOCI-40 (SOCI Act): SOCI - Access and control obligations for data storage
SOCI-41 (SOCI Act): SOCI - Cyber incident reporting obligations
SOCI-42 (SOCI Act): Cyber Security Act 2024 - Ransomware payment reporting
SOCI-43 (SOCI Act): SOCI and supplier flow-down
ismControls: No direct ISM control listed in source register.
otherStandards: SOCI Act
controlCategory: Critical infrastructure and conditional SOCI obligations
controlObjective: Ensure identity services support any critical infrastructure duties that apply to NDIA assets, data processing or suppliers.
threat: Failure to identify applicable SOCI obligations, inadequate supplier controls, weak privileged access, unmanaged data storage or missed incident reporting.
applicability: Identity services, privileged access, identity data stores, data processing assets, suppliers and incident reporting where SOCI or critical infrastructure duties apply.
excluded: Assets assessed and recorded as not subject to SOCI or critical infrastructure obligations; the assessment record remains in scope.
guidance: Confirm whether identity assets or suppliers fall under SOCI requirements. Flow required controls into risk management, contracts and incident reporting processes.
technicalControls: Critical asset register; privileged access controls; supplier access controls; data storage location controls; incident reporting workflow; ransomware reporting support.
processSteps: Assess applicability, document decision, update the risk management program, implement identity and supplier controls, test reporting pathways and review after changes.
responsible: Critical Infrastructure Risk team; IAM team; Supplier Managers; System Owners; Cyber Incident Response team
consulted: Legal; Enterprise Risk; Procurement; Privacy; Records Management; Business Continuity
informed: Executive governance; affected system owners; suppliers; incident response stakeholders
exceptionsPermitted: No for mandatory statutory obligations; implementation risk decisions must be formally approved.
exceptionProcess: Document applicability, statutory obligation, risk, interim control, reporting impact and remediation date for executive approval.
exceptionAuthority: SOCI Accountable Executive with CISO and Legal endorsement.
verification: Applicability assessment review, critical asset register check, supplier control review and incident reporting exercise.
evidence: SOCI applicability assessment; critical asset register; CIRMP records; supplier clauses; access reviews; incident reporting test results.
auditFrequency: At least annually and after material changes to assets, suppliers or legislation.
relatedPolicies: NDIA ICT Identity Management Policy; Critical Infrastructure Risk Policy; Business Continuity Policy; Cyber Incident Response Policy; Supplier Risk Management Policy
relatedProcedures: SOCI applicability assessment procedure; critical asset identity control checklist; cyber incident reporting playbook; supplier flow-down guide
reviewTriggers: SOCI applicability change; new critical supplier; data storage change; cyber incident; Cyber Security Act or SOCI Act update.
notes: This is conditional: it applies where NDIA identity services, data stores or suppliers fall within SOCI or critical infrastructure obligations.
